      Grant Criteria 
      The 2 Billion Trees program aims to motivate and support new tree planting projects. Over the course of 10 years, by 2031 up to $3.2 billion will be invested in tree planting efforts to support provinces, territories, third-party organizations and Indigenous organizations plant two billion trees across Canada. Grant Value:Up to $40 million per fiscal year; ORUp to 50% of eligible project costs for regular applicants or up to 75% of eligible project costs for Indigenous-led projectsTurnaround Time: Approximately 6 months. Eligible Applicants: A municipal or local government or one of their agencies, or a regional municipal organization;A not-for-profit organization registered in Canada, such as a charitable organization, volunteer organization, community, professional, industry or other association, land conservation organization, or non-government organization;A for-profit organization (legally incorporated or registered in Canada);An Indigenous organization (for-profit and not-for-profit) or community; andOrganizations looking to be project aggregators. Potential aggregators should describe their concept of operations in their project description. Ineligible Applicants:Individual landowners;Provincial and Territorial Governments;Federal Government Departments; andCrown Corporations.Eligibile Expenses:Salaries and benefits, and employee recruitment and training;Professional, technical, and capacity building services;Community and landowner engagement;Purchase or lease of land for nurseries to grow seedlings;Translation, production, printing, publication and distribution, and media services;Contractors, such as for tree planting and silviculture;Materials and supplies, such as seeds and trees for planting;Transportation;Facilities;Machinery and equipment;Travel expenses including accommodation and venue expenses; Honoraria and ceremonial costs where Indigenous recipients or Indigenous partners are involved; andOverhead expenditures, provided that they are directly related and essential to the conduct of the project, up to 15% of eligible expenditures. Eligible Projects: Contribute to incremental planting and associated management of trees and forests. Activities must be in addition to that which would occur without the initiative, and not legally required, such as following commercial activity or as a condition for impact assessment approval;Contribute clear benefits in terms of net carbon sequestration and greenhouse gas emission reduction in the period up to 2050, and seek to minimize GHG emissions in the early years. Examples of carbon sequestration considerations include: Selecting planting sites where no or minimal vegetation removal is required;Purchasing seedlings from local nurseries and minimizing the distance travelled for planted, monitoring and maintenance, thereby reducing transportation emissions;Limiting intensive site preparation activities, such as salvage harvesting after an insect infestation, trenching, or vegetation removal, all of which can cause substantial emissions early in the project;Reducing the use of pesticides/herbicides; and Limiting equipment use.Seek to achieve human well-being and environmental co-benefits;Contribute to planting that is ecologically suitable or otherwise appropriate for its location, given site conditions (this includes not planting on sites that naturally would be non forest ecosystems, such as natural grasslands or wetlands); and Result in permanent additions to forests, improve existing forests, or allow for permanent protection of forests.Ineligible Projects: Projects that help organizations that have a legal obligations to regenerate forests, such as a legal obligation to regenerate after harvesting under sustainable forest management regimes; andProjects that regenerate forests on private lands as part of business-as-usual commercial forestry activities.Program Details: Max funding through the Tree Planting streams is $40 million per fiscal year, for a maximum of 8 fiscal years (for a total of 320 million); The maximum that NRCan contribution for eligible project costs is 50% of eligible expenditures;For Indigenous-led projects the 2BT Program will consider up to 75% of eligible costs for the tree planting projects;Apply by January 16, 2025, for a decision by July 2025;Apply by May 15, 2025, for a decision by November 2025;Apply by September 18, 2025, for a decision by March 2026;There are currently 3 streams under the 2 Billion Tree Program:Mass Planting Stream;Small-Scale Planting Stream;Urban/ Suburban Stream;Mass Planting Stream: Must plant an average of 500,000 seedlings/trees per calendar year (January to December) in each year in which planting occurs. Projects can include Long-Term-Planting Work;Allow for planting to occur across multiple sites, as long as the average number of trees planted per calendar year, in years which planting occurs, is equal to or greater than 500,000;Can include forest or tree restoration portions of work involving riparian zones, habitat restoration and
other ecosystem improvement projects;Cannot be located in urban and suburban areas;When preparing a Mass planting Stream proposal, please consider the following: Choice to pursue afforestation, reforestation or both;choice of seed sources, variety of tree species of trees planted and their ability to survive and grow in the climate that may exist over the next century; co-benefits resulting from chose tree plating activities including permanence.Small-Scale Planting Stream:Must plant an average of 50,000 trees per calendar year (January to December) in each year in which planting occurs;Allow for planting to occur across multiple sites, as long as the average number of trees planted per calendar year, in years in which planting occurs, is equal to or greater than 50,000;Can include forest or tree restoration portions of work involving riparian zones, habitat restoration and other ecosystem improvement projects;Cannot be located in urban and suburban areas;Must have clearly defined planting sites;When preparing a Small-scale Planting Stream proposal, please consider the following: Choice to pursue afforestation, reforestation or both;choice of seed sources, variety of tree species of trees planted and their ability to survive and grow in the climate that may exist over the next century; co-benefits resulting from chose tree plating activities including permanence.Urban/ Suburban Stream): Must plant an average of 10,000 trees per calendar year (January to December) in each year in which planting occurs;The program recommends collaborative project proposals in order to meet this threshold, as needed;Allow for planting to occur across multiple sites, as long as the average number of trees planted per calendar year, in years in which planting occurs, is equal to or greater than 10,000;Must be located in and around urban areas, population centres or communities;Must have clearly defined planting sites;When preparing a Urban/Suburban Stream proposal, please consider the following:Choice of seed sources, variety of tree species of trees planted and their ability to survive and grow in the climate that may exist over the next century;Co-benefits resulting from chosen tree planting activities including permanence.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Process Best Practices: Ongoing funding is encouraged, and applicants are encouraged to apply for more than one fiscal year;Eligible Best Practices:This program covers up to 50% of eligible project costs or 75% for indigenous-led projects;This program is not retroactive;The program allows for additional support from other federal and provincial programs up to 100% of total project costs.Forms:Program Webpage: click  hereEligibility Assessment Page: click hereProgram Guidelines: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This federal program aims to promote entrepreneurship in Indigenous communities and increase the number of viable businesses owned by Indigenous people through non-repayable grants of up to $99,999, issued through designated Aboriginal Financial Institutions (AFIs) located across the country. Program details are determined by the AFIs, and may vary from location to location, but in general, the funds may be used to support proposals for starting, acquiring, or expanding a business, and to leverage other sources of funding. Consult your local AFI for application instructions (see "Forms" for directory link).Grant Value: Up to $99,999 for Individual Indigenous entrepreneurs; andUp to $250,000 for eligible Indigenous community businesses.Turnaround Time: 2-8 weeksEligible Applicants:Indigenous individuals;Businesses owned and controlled by Indigenous people;Indigenous and non-indigenous organizations and associations (except those with a religious or charitable purpose); First Nations and Inuit communities and governments;Canadian owned and controlled banks, credit unions, and trust companies;Private equity providers;Provincial and federal crown corporations; andMunicipal governments, labour organizations, and post-secondary institutions. Note: Eligibility criteria may vary between AFIs. Many AFIs only serve Indigenous individuals, businesses, and organizations in their local area.Eligible Projects:Projects may involve starting, purchasing, expanding, or modernizing a business, and must create measurable benefits, including but not limited to additional revenue, new markets, and/or new job opportunities;Examples of eligible activities include: Advertising campaigns, trade shows, seminars, and conferences; Research; Process and product development; Productivity improvement; and Investment in new technology and/or systems.Ineligible Projects:Community infrastructure projects that are unrelated to commercial enterprise;Purchase of land, buildings, and/or investment property; andBusiness activity related to pawn shops, payday loan firms, gaming operations, and/or the production/distribution of alcohol, tobacco, and sexually exploitative materials.Note: Be sure to consult your local AFI for a more detailed list of eligibility criteria.Program Details: Application requirements vary slightly between AFIs. In most cases, the first step is to submit an application form and business plan;Financial support for the creation of the business plan is available from most AFIs;Applicants must provide proof of their ability to cover at least some of the project costs (usually 10% of the total);Project financials and performance may be monitored for up to three years after the funding agreement is issued; andTo proceed with an application, consult the AFI directory to find an Aboriginal Financial Institution near you. 

      Best Practices & Forms
      Process Best Practices:This program can be combined with funding from provincial sources;Because application processes vary between institutions, it is essential to find an AFI near you, and review the instructions for their version of the program;Indigenous business owners in BC can access this funding through the Business Equity Program at Tale’awtxw Aboriginal Capital Corporation.Eligible Best Practices: Most AFIs do not allow the funding to be used retroactively.Forms:Program website: click hereDirectory of Aboriginal Financial Institutions: click here

      Grant Criteria

      Grant Criteria 
      The Access to Talent Program enables SMEs and start-ups in the natural product sector to receive up to 40% to a maximum of $150,000 towards hiring a new experienced member on their team. The individual will be expected to support a project aimed at product and technology development or pre-commercial business development. The aim of this program is to boost talent at small companies with natural products or technologies that are derived from a biological source and benefit people, animals, and the planet.Grant Value:Stream 1 - For individuals with 5-9 years of experience40% of eligible costs to a maximum of $75,000Stream 2 - For individuals with 10+ years of experience40% of eligible costs to a maximum of $150,000Turnaround Time:  2 monthsEligible Employer:Incorporated Canadian start-ups and SMEs;Up to 25 full-time equivalent employees;Be a member of Canada’s Natural Product Innovation Cluster; Have a novel pre-commercial (Technology Readiness Levels(TRL) 4-9) 'natural product or technology';Defined as a biologically-based innovation that benefits people, animals, and the planet, and can be applied to a range of industries, including: Food production and value-added agriculture; Bioproducts and sustainability; Human nutrition, health, and wellness; Animal health and nutrition; and Water and waste management.Have potential for: Achieving 10MM- 15MM in annual revenue within a market-reasonable period;Significant economic, social, health, and/or environmental benefits;Commercialization in Canada;Technological advancement and benefits to the natural products ecosystem across Canada;Spillover benefits to more than one sector; andImproving the representation of women, visible minorities, and Indigenous peoples in the natural products ecosystem.Employers do not need to have identified a candidate before applying, candidate can be chosen before or after application submission. Note: The program focus is on disruptive technologies, specifically proprietary biological-based technologies. However, the program does not invest in technologies based on software, or artificial intelligence. Eligible Candidate:Must be hired as a full-time employee;Demonstrated experience to successfully execute the project identified by the applicant that is critical to the product or technology development;Must be a new hire and not previously a full-time employee;The company can have the candidate identified at the time of application or can recruit the candidate after the application submission, but the candidate’s resume must be submitted to NPC for review and approval prior to final approval of funding.Cannot be responsible for or have other employees responding to them directly; andMust spend 100% of their time on activities directly related to the project and its key milestones.Eligible Activities :Include but are not limited to an employee:Working directly on product or technology development;Conducting pre-commercial business development;Working on the regulatory strategy and/or collecting necessary data for regulatory submissions; andWorking on product or technology scale-up.Evaluation Criteria: Novelty of the natural product or technology; Market opportunity; Business model;Competitors; Strength of the management team;Technical feasibility of the project to be undertaken;Position to be filled; Qualifications of the candidate; andKey milestones and their impact.Program Details:Funds may only be used for salary costs (any recruiting costs not included);Applicants are required to contribute 60% of salary costs unless leveraging other grants;Candidate may be identified at the time of application or can be recruited after application submission (within 3 months of approval):The candidate's resume must be submitted to NPC for review prior to final approval of financing.Eligible positions include but are not limited to:Product or technology development;Business development;Regulatory strategy and/or collecting necessary data for regulatory submissions;Product or technology scale-up;Marketing or sales strategy; andFundraising to support the growth of the product or technology.The project period is a maximum of 18 months (employment term expected to exceed this duration);The project must provide technological advancement and benefits to the natural products ecosystem across Canada;Contract with NPC will include project scope, reporting requirements, and key milestones to be achieved;Disbursement of funds takes place through reimbursement of eligible project costs upon approval of quarterly reports;Includes a written and financial claim containing invoices and proof of payment.Annual reporting required for 5 years following the program period.

Students gain real-world work experience and receive a $1,400 stipend upon successful completion, while employers benefit from skilled talent at no cost (100% Contribution).Grant value: $1,400. Turnaround Time: 5 Business Days. Eligible Employers: Must be a registered business or nonprofit based in Ontario; andMust be able to work with students during the set cohort dates.Eligible Candidates: Must be enrolled at an eligible Ontario post-secondary institution and invited into the program; andEligible to work in Canada.Program Details: The program is a 60-hour remote internship completed over 2–8 weeks (minimum 2 weeks);Projects should be meaningful, real-work tasks tied to actual business needs (e.g., marketing, analysis, tech tasks);Projects are fully subsidized for employers — there is no cost to the business;Employer benefits: Access to diverse talent, project support, and the ability to possibly hire students afterward;Deadlines vary by cohort, for the December 2025–June 2026 cycle, there are two cohorts:February 2026 Cohort : February 23 - April 10, 2026 : Cohort open for employers' projects on January 1, 2026;Students Invited to Confirm Eligibility and Submit an Application on January 5, 2026.April 2026 Cohort: April 27 - June 1,9 2026:Cohort open for employers' projects on February 9, 2026;Students Invited to Confirm Eligibility and Submit an Application on March 2, 2026.Employers can participate in multiple cohorts, while students may only participate in one cohort;Employers should not create multiple active accounts or participate through more than two companies, and each company must complete ID verification;Students will complete a total of 60 hours of work, with a maximum of 30 hours per week and no more than 10 hours per day;All projects must be completed by the cohort end date; otherwise, students will not be eligible for payment; andCommunication must happen through the Riipen platform to protect payment eligibility:Only students registered on the Riipen platform under Advance Ontario are eligible to be paid;Students are employed by Riipen Networks Inc., which handles workplace safety and legal requirements in Ontario; andPayment is made only if Riipen confirms the student and project meet all program requirements.Application & Participation ProcessFor Employers:Submit a project match request in Riipen before the cohort’s deadline;Review student applications and accept at least one (up to four); andProjects begin on the cohort start date and must be completed by the cohort end date;For Students:Receive an invitation to join Advance Ontario;Apply to up to three projects during the application window;Once accepted and matched, click “Start Project” by the start date; and Complete your hours, deliverables, and required exit survey.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices: Projects should be detailed and explain the goal, scope, tasks, required skills, timeline, and expected deliverables  (Checklist of Project Creation);Make sure the project is achievable within ~60 hours over 2–8 weeks, and clearly explains how students can succeed;Make sure mentorship and support expectations are included so students know what guidance they’ll receive.Process Best Practices:Student applications should be reviewed and responded to promptly, and applicants should be selected based on strong alignment with project needs;Project launch should be planned in advance to ensure work can begin as soon as the cohort starts.Forms & Links: Program Webpage: click hereProgram FAQs: click hereApplication Process: click hereApplication Portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Affordable Housing Fund: New Construction – Community Housing Sub-Stream provides low-interest repayable loans covering up to 95% of project costs for co-ops, non-profits, and Indigenous organizations, and up to 75% for municipalities, provinces, and private-sector applicants. It also offers forgivable loans covering up to 40% of costs (lower maximums for other applicant types).Grant Value: Up to 95% loan-to-cost (community housing providers);Up to 75% loan-to-cost (other applicants);Forgivable loans available up to 40% of eligible costs.Turnaround Time: pendingEligible Applicants:Non-profit housing providers;Housing co-operatives (rental, not equity co-ops);Indigenous governments, organizations, or development corporations;Municipalities, provinces, territories, and their agencies;Private and for-profit developers (lower loan support).Eligible Projects:New construction of affordable rental housing;Community housing projects with affordability commitments;Permanent rental housing (not transitional or temporary);Projects must meet the minimum affordability criteria as outlined by CMHC. Program Details:Affordability must be maintained for at least 10 years;Deeper affordability levels, longer affordability periods, accessibility features, and energy efficiency commitments strengthen applications;Non-residential components permitted, but must remain secondary to residential use (typically ≤30% of total cost and space);The Affordable Housing Fund increased its minimum energy efficiency and accessibility standards in November 2024, now requiring projects to meet Tier 2 of the 2020 National Energy Code of Canada for Buildings accessibility standards;However, projects in design could still use previous (lower) standards until September 30, 2025, as long as the full application (with all required documents) is submitted by 11:59 pm ET on that date. Afterward, only applications meeting the new standards will be accepted.Submit complete applications by the deadline to qualify for the transition period—incomplete or late applications will not be processed. CMHC will prioritize applications that exceed these minimum requirements, especially those demonstrating strong social outcomes, such as deeper affordability, accessibility, and energy efficiency.Application involves CMHC review, and conditional approval leads to a loan agreement;Project underwriting is completed by CMLS Financial on CMHC’s behalf;Application and underwriting fees apply depending on project size.

      Best Practices & Forms

      Grant Criteria 
      The Agricultural Clean Technology Program: Research and Innovation stream provides up to $2 million in funding to support the research, development, and demonstration of pre-market clean technology. The priority areas include green energy, precision agriculture, and bio-economy. The intent of the program is to promote sustainable growth and lower carbon emissions in Canada's agriculture and agri-food sectors.Grant Value: Up to 60% of project costs to a maximum of $2 million per project;The maximum amount payable to a recipient with multiple projects will generally not exceed $5 million.Note: Funding under this stream is repayable and non-repayable. Please see the Eligible Activities section below for details.Turnaround Time: 100 business daysEligible Applicants:For-profit organizations (including agri-food processors);Non-profit organizations (including co-operatives); andIndigenous groups.Ineligible Applicants:Financial institutions;Academic institutions;Crown corporations;Federal government;Foreign governments; andIndividuals.Eligible Activities:For non-repayable funding:Applied research and development of clean technologies;Piloting clean technologies;Technology evaluation;Demonstration and knowledge transfer activities.For repayable funding:Commercializing and scale-up of clean technologies.Program Details:Project funding is typically 50:50;60:40 funding is available for organizations owned or led by 1 or more of the following underrepresented groups:Women;Youth (35 and under);Indigenous;Visible minorities; andPersons with disabilities.Maximum funding across multiple projects will generally not exceed $5 million;Priority areas:Green energy and energy efficiency:Including but not limited to:Improvements on lighting, insulation, heating, refrigeration, and ventilation efficiency;Energy efficiency technology;Zero-emissions on-farm equipment and machinery; andEnergy generation technologies such as solar panels, heat pumps, and biodigesters.Precision agriculture - technologies to gather and process data to guide targeted actions that improve the sustainability, efficiency, and productivity of agricultural operationsIncluding but not limited to:Driver assistance and machine auto-guidance; andDecision support tools and technologies that improve in real-time input, use, and nutrient management.Bioeconomy - utilization of agriculture waste and by-products for energy and bio-product generationIncluding but not limited to:Biofuels and digestate production used as bioenergy, soil nutrients, and water;Manure management technologies;Agri-based products, such as:Bioplastics;Biomass-based construction products and car parts.Costs incurred from the date of the submission of a completed application are eligible;In-kind contributions are not eligible under the Agricultural Clean Technology Program;Payments for eligible project costs will only be made once a Contribution Agreement is signed;Applicants will be required to provide financial, progress, and performance reports, or other reports as detailed in the contribution agreement; andRepayable funding will be repaid over a period of up to 10 years following project completion.

      Grant Criteria 
      Through this program, primary and Indigenous producers, conservation groups, water purveyors and Indigenous communities will have access to cost-shared funding to adapt to climate change by investing in water infrastructure. Stream 3 offers up to $100,000 for agricultural water supply assessments, engineering studies or plans.Grant Value: Stream 3: 75% up to $100,000.Turnaround Time: Up to 60 days after deadline.Eligible Applicants: Activities 1 & 2: Irrigation/ Improvement districts & local/municipal governments including First Nations.Activity 3: Incorporated and individual producers;Agricultural and conservation groups;Irrigation/improvement districts and local/municipal governments that supply water to agricultural; andIndigenous Communities and Indigenous Producers. Ineligible Applicants: Non-agricultural individuals or groups;Provincial and federal governments; andCrown Corporations.Eligible Activities: Activity 1: Water supply assessment or feasibility studies in key agricultural areas to determine available water supply:In some areas of B.C., some streams or aquifers may be fully subscribed for licensing. Identifying streams or aquifers that are not fully subscribed may allow increase water supplied for agriculture; andIdentifying potential water storage sources could help alleviate future climate change induced drought.Eligible Costs: Consulting services by Qualified Professionals.Ineligible Items: Construction services. Activity 2: Engineering studies or plans for water purveyors to assess and determine opportunities for upgrades and expansion of existing purveyed water systems:Many purveyed water systems engineering studies or plans before any efficiency upgrades or expansion can occur.Eligible Cost:Consulting services by Qualified Professionals.Ineligible Items:Construction services.Activity 3: Dam engineering assessments, water release plans, dam safety reviews, redetermination of consequences classification or any professional consultative services under the Dam Safety Regulation:Dams are assessed for their risk consequence rating and may require upgrades to continue use. The cost of the engineering assessment and a design plan are often a financial barrier to producers.Eligible Costs:Consulting services by Qualified Professionals.Ineligible Items: Construction services. Ineligible Activities: Activities or costs incurred prior to approval;In-kind activities;Activities to support non-agricultural water use;Activities not directly related to agricultural water use;Purchase of farm equipment and related accessories or attachments (including tractors, skid steers and trailers);Activities that are not compliant with federal, provincial, or local/municipal regulations;Financial compensation for lost income, production or land or other associated losses due to water shortages, government orders, or other reasons;Activities to remove land from the Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR);Purchase of land or easement;Regular or on-going operating or maintenance activities;Training or educational courses;Financing charges, loan interest payments, bank fees and related charges;Activities currently receiving funding from other funding sources; andGST and other taxes/credits reimbursed to applicant.Program Details:Deadline for application July 31, 2023;All projects must be completed by January 15, 2026;An initial payment (50%) will be made by IAF to all projects upon signing of their contribution agreement, however IAF may reduce this advance based on project/applicant risk;Interim and final payments will not be initiated by IAF until reporting requirements are satisfactorily met by the client; Interim and final payments will be made based on actual expenses reported and payments will be made in arrears;All reports require a final report and a minimum of 20% of approved funding will be retained by IAD, pending submission of final reporting; andIf permits are pending/under review but the application is otherwise complete, IAF will proceed to consider and adjudicate the application, however any approval will be conditional until all required documentation is received.

      Grant Criteria

andMust be in good standing with Alberta Innovates or its subsidiaries (InnoTech Alberta, C-FER Technologies).NOTE: Although Partners are not required they are highly encouraged. Eligible Projects: Align with the objectives of the Program (listed below in program details); Be between Technology Readiness levels 3 and 7 at the start of the project (higher start-level TRLs may be considered on a case-by-case basis);Be stepped with critical "go/ no go" milestones;Be completed within 36 months; and Comply with other criteria that Alberta Innovates may develop from time to time.Eligible Expenses: Labour costs for those that are partaking in the project;Cost of materials;Acquisitions of property including capital improvements to facility premises and capital equipment (but excluding buildings);Acquisitions of software or information databases;Direct operational costs;Travel expenses relating to the project only if it has been pre-approved by Alberta Innovates;Publishing costs for knowledge translation activities directly related to the Project; andAny other costs pre-approved by Alberta Innovates in writing.Ineligible Expenses: General overheads;Any costs incurred prior to the project start date;Transactions between related persons;Allowance for interest on debt;Losses on investments, bad debts and expenses for collection charges;Losses on other projects or activities outside the approved project;Fine and penalties;Unreasonable compensation for project labour;Costs for professional training and development;Advertising costs;Costs associated with applying for government grants and programs;Basic professional services;Passport or immigration fees;Routine testing and maintenance;Commuting costs; and Any other costs deemed ineligible.Program Details: Program objectives include: Sustain, grow, and optimize productivity, and reduce the cost of production of Alberta's agri-food and bioIndustrial industries;Add value to enhance new commodities in the agri-food and bioIndustrial sectors;Increase environmental sustainability and social benefits for Albertans.The key outcomes of the program include: The development, and advancement of innovations that will lead to a strong agri-food and bioIndustrial sectors and a value-added resource industry in Alberta, one that helps our province become a global leader in environmental, social, and governance performance. Improved economic prosperity and social well-being in Alberta;Reduction of negative environmental impacts. Strategic focus areas include: Data and digital solutions;Autonomous systems;Agricultural biotechnology;Food processing innovation;Biofiber utilization;Value-added biomass;Green construction.Areas that are out of scope include: Bioenergy, biochar, and biofuel applications;Marketing and/or new agri-food product development.

      This federally funded program offers wage subsidies to agriculture employers looking to hire students for a work-integrated learning experience. Accordingly, students may be in any field of study, and employers are encouraged to recruit students from under-represented groups.Grant Value:50% of the wages to a maximum of $5,000 for regular participants70% of the wages to a maximum of $7,000 for under-represented groups including women in STEM, Indigenous students, newcomers, persons with disabilities, visible minority as well as first-year studentsTurnaround Time: 2 weeks Eligible Employers:Registered Canadian business and not-for-profits in the agriculture industry, including:Primary growers;Industry associations;Research units;AgriTech firms;Agriculture start-ups;Veterinary clinics servicing farm animals/ livestockHorticulture; andAquaculture.Farm equipment dealerships;Input dealers;Agriculture-focused media agencies.Must be able to provide a quality learning experience to the student;Must have the capacity to pay the student for the duration of the placement, as the subsidy is administered at the end of the placement, after the final pay stub has been received; andWhere legally required, responsible for Workplace Safety and Insurance Board (WSIB) or alternate workplace insurance coverage; andEmployers can apply with or with or without a candidate. Ineligible Employers:Federal, provincial, territorial, and municipal governments;Non-secular institutions;Post-secondary institutions;Federal and provincial Crown corporations; andMust have the placement recognized as a Work Integrated Learning component in connection with a course, degree, certificate, diploma, or program at their institution.Ineligible CandidatesInternational students;High school students;Students starting university/college the same semester.Students must have attended school the semester prior to the placement and must continue their studies in the same semester as the placement.Placement Details: Wage subsidy will apply to gross wages between:Winter 2025 - January 1, to April 30: OPENSummer 2025 - May 1, to August 31 : CLOSEDFall 2025 - September 1, to December 31: OPENCan be full- or part-time;Note: The program typically does not fund consecutive semesters if the placement stretches across multiple semesters.Can be a co-op, internship, field placement, or applied project;Placements must be "net new," meaning that the SWPP student is incremental to the employer's "baseline" of student hires. An employer's "baseline" is the number of students they hired without SWPP support the year prior to participating in SWPP;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2022, 2023, or 2024, use the number of students hired in the year prior to that first time you accessed SWPP support;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2024, use the number of students hired in 2023;Net new baselines must be calculated each year (if you participate in SWPP every year, your net new baseline will increase accordingly).Include co-op and non-co-op students in your initial baseline calculation. Do not include high school students, recent graduates, or international students, as they are not included in the SWPP program;If a student placement crosses over the fiscal year (ie: January - April), they count toward the earlier fiscal year;If you hire a student for separate placements in different fiscal years (ie: Summer 2022, Summer 2023), you must count them in both fiscal years.There is no limit on the number of placements an employer can apply for so long as the net new requirement is met.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Alberta-DT program supports digital SMEs by providing up to $50,000 to fund projects that enable businesses to build traction through customer acquisition, activation, retention, referral, and ultimately revenue. The aim of this program is to accelerate the growth of digital firms that rely on software development for their product or service offerings, in order to generate economic and social impact for Alberta.Grant Value: 50% up to $50,000Turnaround Time: 6 to 8 weeksEligible Applicants:Be a for-profit 'digital SME';An SME that relies on software development for 1 or more of its products and/or services and intends to rapidly scale in the global marketplace.Have fewer than 50 full-time employees;Have less than $1M annual reoccurring revenue;Have a founding team larger than 1;Demonstrate previous investment into the company by the founding team;Be an Alberta-based company:Physical and corporate operational presence in Alberta;Albertan ownership and incorporation;May otherwise be incorporated federally or in another jurisdiction AND extra-provincially registered in Alberta; ORBe a General Partnership, Limited Partnership, or Limited Liability Partnership AND registered in Alberta.Intent that operational benefits will flow primarily within the province.Have up-to-date corporate filings;Have not previously received Digital Traction funding;Be in good financial standing with Alberta Innovates and its subsidiaries InnoTech Alberta and C-Fer Technologies.Note: Applicants cannot concurrently receive funding from other Alberta Innovates Programs.Eligible Activities:Customer and/or client discovery;Digital market assessment and segmentation analysis;Data-driven, online market assessment testing;Product development based on client feedback;Advanced market assessment or segmentation analysis; andAdvanced sales and/or marketing strategies.Eligible Expenses:Costs incurred after the signing of the Investment Agreement;Costs incurred between arm's length entities (with no existing relationships);Wages and salaries for individuals working directly on the project:Up to $50/hour for T4 or contract employees; andUp to 50% of total funding for founder's salary costs (must have 15% equity in applicant company).Costs of materials;Acquisitions of software or information databases (prorated over the duration of project);Advertising costs for data-based marketing strategies for customer discovery purposes; Cost of sub-contractors at fair market rates;Additional direct operating costs beyond labour and materials; andAny other cost which Alberta Innovates pre-approves in writing.Program Details:The project must be completed within 1 year;The project start date should be at least 45 days from the application submission date;Businesses must provide a minimum 25% cash contribution; The project must outline 3 defined business milestones to be reached during the project to measure progress;Have the first milestone activities identified to a maximum of $15,000 (includes payment upon execution of agreement, up to $10,000);Individual milestones cannot exceed $20,000 to a maximum of $50,000 for all 3 milestones; Project milestones are based on business outcomes, with activities required to reach those milestones; TDAs will monitor the progress of the project and provide coaching to the business; Milestone activities are flexible and may be adjusted as the project progresses;An advance payment of up to $10,000 will be released once the Investment Agreement is signed by both parties; Further funding is disbursed at the completion of each milestone; andAnnual reporting to the program will be required for 5 years following project completion.The Ideal applicant will have:a minimum viable product (MVP) to test with customers;a minimum TRL 4 and at the Validating stage of development;not previously received Digital Traction funding;performed preliminary customer discovery work to inform the development;a digital technology employed in an innovative way and/or with proprietary features to allow for a competitive advantage over existing solutions;a digital technology that could scale up in one to two years, if successful;no significant capital or regulatory barriers, not addressed by the project, that may be better addressed by other funding resources;completed a lean canvas, business model canvas, or similar tools to demonstrate anunderstanding of the problem to be solved and the customer profile; anda traction roadmap or similar tool to demonstrate customer acquisition targets for the next three years and what is required to get to those targets.Note: If the application is rejected two times for an Alberta Innovates funding program, the applicant can no longer be eligible to apply for funding for that project/technology.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Applicants can use this program funding in conjunction with other sources of government funding to a maximum of 75% of eligible project costs;This program does not allow funding to be used retroactively for costs incurred prior to signing the contribution agreement;Applicants should have:A minimum viable product (MVP) to test with customers;Performed preliminary customer discovery work to inform the development;A product with proprietary features to allow for a competitive advantage over existing solutions;No significant capital or regulatory barriers not addressed by the proposed project;Completed a lean canvas or a business model canvas;Have a traction roadmap to demonstrate customer acquisition targets for the next 3 years.Meeting the eligibility criteria does not guarantee access to funding;Third-party contractors, including developers, should be sourced locally unless the resources don’t exist in Alberta or there is a strong business need presented in the application to connect nationally or internationally to achieve business outcomes; andProcess Best Practices:The program reviews application based on merit with the recommendation from the Ecosystem, the business opportunity, the founding team, financial position, the project, and the overall benefit to Alberta;Applicants are recommended to apply well in the advance of their intended project start date as expenses incurred prior to an approval are highly unlikely to be funded;Milestone activities are flexible and may be adjusted as the project proceeds. Forms:Program website: click hereProgram guidelines: click hereApplication portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This provincial program provides up to $15,000 for businesses in Alberta seeking new export opportunities in foreign markets. Applicants must be legal entities that have a minimum annual revenue of $250,000 and have between 1 and 499 full-time employees in Alberta. Applicants are to present an adequate market entry plan. Grant Value:For-profit applicants: 50% of eligible costs - $1,000 to $15,000 per year.Turnaround Time: 25 business days - applications must be received within two months after the first day of formal event participation.Eligible Applicants:Be one of the following organization types:For-profit SMEs, non-profits, municipalities, industry associations, tertiary education institutions, technical institutes, Indigenous communities, and economic development organizations operating in Alberta.For-profit organizations must:Be an incorporated legal entity in Alberta;Be operating and have a permanent establishment in Alberta;Present an adequate market entry plan; Must have at least 1 full-time employee and fewer than 500 full-time equivalent employees;Must have annual revenues of $250,000 - $25,000,000.Emerging technology companies may be eligible at a lower annual gross
sales amount of $50,000,This requirement may be waived for start-up companies with emerging technologies but will be determined on a case-by-case basis.Eligible Activities:Registration fees for participation at select tradeshows and/or events in the target marketFor International trades event, base entry registration fee may be reimbursed up to 50% up to a max of $1,000;Accommodation;International business travel;There is a maximum of two travelers who must be Alberta-based employees of the applicant organization:The organization’s first traveler will receive a $400 CAD per diem for the eligible days;The organization’s second traveler will receive a $200 CAD per diem for the eligible days.Translation of marketing materials.Note: Maximum of 2 employees per activity. Travelers must also be Alberta based.Ineligible Activities:International travel focused on investment, recreational and/or educational purposes;Projects that do not have a product or service to market;Travel for business meetings alone (without attending a formal trade event);Days involving business meetings only;Pre-commercial projects seeking research collaborations, proof of concept or demonstration partners;Trade show booth costs;Personal travel;Brokerage services;Ongoing operational activities or activities that are considered core to the applicant's business and not specific to
pursuing export opportunities in a new target market;Travel related to acquisitions or mergers;Travel and trade events taking place in Canada;Travel to countries with sanctions imposed by Canada; orTravel and trade events relating to expanding sales within international markets where a for-profit organization
already has a well-established presence (more than $150,000 CAD sale generated in target market and more than
15 per cent of the company’s total annual sales).Program Details:There is a maximum of two travelers who must be Alberta-based employees of the applicant organization:The organization’s first traveler will receive a $400 CAD per diem for the eligible days;The organization’s second traveler will receive a $200 CAD per diem for the eligible days.There is no limit on the number of days eligible for per diems; however, total annual funding for eligible applicant
organizations is capped at $15,000 CAD;Multiple formal trade events can be
submitted in one application if they occurred as part of the same trip;however, if applicant organization returns to Canada
between formal events, separate applications must be submitted.Once applications are received, they are assessed on a first-come first-served basis.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:This program can be combined with funding from other provincial and federal sources, as long as the total amount of government funding for a project does not exceed 75% of eligible project costs;Applicants must disclose all sources of funding in their applications and project reports.Process Best Practices:Applications must be submitted within two months after the first day of formal event participation;If there are changes to planned activities, notify the funder immediately so that the funding agreement can be amended; andEmerging technology sectors (cleantech, bio-industrial technology, life sciences) may have reduced application requirements. (E.g. $50,000 in annual sales in the prior year. Program staff will consult with subject matter experts within the Government of Alberta and these applications will be considered on a project-by-project basis).Forms:Program website: click hereProgram guidelines: click hereProgram eligiblity assessment: click hereApplication portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This program provides up to $100,000 of funding (up to 75% of costs) to accelerate the technological and business development of small and medium-sized enterprises. Companies are eligible to cover costs from 3 different service providers that contribute to advancing the technology and helping the applicant approach the commercialization stage sooner.Grant Value: 75% from $10,001 to $100,000Turnaround time: within 7 weeksEligible Applicants:For-profit small and medium-sized enterprises (less than 500 full-time employees);Incorporated and have a physical presence in Alberta;Less than $50,000,000 in annual gross revenue; Must contribute a minimum of 25% cash contribution of the total eligible project costs;Have a level 7 on Technological Readiness Level (TRL) (see here); andGood credit under Alberta Innovates, InnoTech Alberta, and C-Fer Technologies.Eligible Service Providers:Legally provide services in Canada;Are involved in the following:New product research and development;Design, engineering, and prototyping (must be leading edge);Advanced product testing and refinement;Patent development (excluding patent maintenance);Intermediate market assessment and analysis;Business and marketing strategies; andOther tech development activities must be approved;Cannot have any legal relationship with applicant (be Arm's Length with applicant);Products/services are offered at market rates; andGood credit under Alberta Innovates, InnoTech Alberta, and C-Fer Technologies.Note: Service providers can be based in any country that Canada does business with.Eligible Expenses:Labour costs resulting from eligible service providers;Materials needed for the project (must be reasonably priced);Software necessary to complete the project; andCapital assets necessary to complete the project. Note: This list is not exhaustive, the funder may allow other costs on a discretionary basis.Ineligible Expenses:Overhead costs;Administrative materials;Training subsidies;Sales and marketing costs;Capital acquisition, improvements, equipment;Travel costs;Costs associated with applying for grants;Routine testing and maintenance;GST and PST; andOther expenses Alberta Innovates deems ineligible.Note: This list is not exhaustive, the funder may allow other costs on a discretionary basis.Program Details:Maximum project duration is 2 years; andMust be have specific goals and objectives (timeline below mentions potential objectives that can be set out as goals - also referred to as "performance indicators"); and Must be outlined in a formal business plan document (with 5 years financial projections).

      Grant Criteria 
      The Alberta Manufacturing Productivity Grant aims to help small and medium manufacturers by providing funding of 50% up to $30,000 to improve their operations, invest in technology to automate production and increase competitiveness across Canada and abroad.Grant Value: 50% up to $30,000.Turnaround Time: 45 business daysEligible Applicants:Must be a manufacturer based on the following definition:A manufacturer is described as involved in operations to produce or support products/services related to manufacturing, processing, fabricating or refining.Must be operating in Alberta;Must be an incorporated business (federally or provincially) for 2 years or more;Must demonstrate financial stability; and Must have greater than 5 and fewer than 750 full-time employees (FTE) in Alberta.Eligible Activities:The program provides funding for investments and implementation of long-term production assets and technology that increase capacity on production.Technologies may include: equipment; robotics; automation; artificial intelligence; machine learning; advancing networks; and equipment for investments in the Internet of Things. NOTE: investments in ERP systems and general training are not covered under this program.Eligible Costs:Capital equipmentInstallation of capital equipment related to the projectTraining on new equipment related to the projectDirect materials related to the projectDirect labour devoted to the completion and management of the projectProject management/consulting fees (excluding travelNOTE: Any expense claimed that does not have a receipt included will be removed from eligible costs.Program Details:Only one project will be funded per company;Applicants must complete a CME approved operational assessment;The acquired technology or equipment must be used and/or located in Alberta;Phase one of the program requires the following:A technology assessment by a qualified assessor will work on-site with companies to create a customized plan on how to improve productivity by using existing assets and implement the latest advanced manufacturing technologies including:Hardware;Software; and Cloud computing.Upon completion the expert will recommend and action plan;NOTE: this will occur before an application is submitted for phase two which is the funding aspect.Phase two of the program includes the following:Direct financial assistance to invest in new productivity enhancing technologies;Technologies may include:Equipment;Robotics;Automation;Artificial Intelligence;Machine Learning;Advancing networks.Applications will be evaluated based on their ability to meet the following criteria:Technology investments that aim to improve and modernize the manufacturing process, leading to increased productivity and competitiveness;Creation of long-term employment and high-value jobs.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Program may allow funding to be retroactive to April 1, 2025;Program allows funding to be stacked with other eligible federal programs however, this funding cannot be stacked with other Government of Alberta-funded programs.Process Best Practices:Any expense claimed that does not have a receipt included will be removed from eligible costs;A final report and expense claim must be submitted to CME for approval prior to receiving the final payment.Forms and Links:Program Webpage: click hereProgram Guidelines: click hereEligibility Application Form: click here

grants.grant_criteria: The Alliance Grants provides funding contributions of up to a maximum of $1 million per year to university researchers and partner organizations in collaboration. Funding may be used for salary support, materials and supplies, and activities that support collaboration and/or knowledge mobilization. The intent of the program is to encourage collaborative teams to generate new knowledge and accelerate the application of research results to create benefits for Canada.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Alliance Grants provides funding contributions of up to a maximum of $1 million per year to university researchers and partner organizations in collaboration. Funding may be used for salary support, materials and supplies, and activities that support collaboration and/or knowledge mobilization. The intent of the program is to encourage collaborative teams to generate new knowledge and accelerate the application of research results to create benefits for Canada.Grant Value:Option 1 - Up to 66.% to a maximum of $1 millionOption 2 - Up to 100% to a maximum of $300,000Turnaround Time: Small and medium projects - Up to 12 weeksLarge projects - up to 16 weeksEligible Applicants:Canadian university researcher to partner with one of the following organization types:Private, public, or not-for-profit.Partner organizations may be Canadian or foreign/multinational companies;Must provide supplemental information that describes the organization and enables NSERC to determine if the partner organization can be considered in NSERC’s cost-sharing calculations.Have at least 1 partner who can demonstrate the ability to exploit such research results;Must collectively support the project through cash contributions, where applicable;Each partner organization must actively play a role in the project and support it through in-kind contributions, such as:Play an active role in the project’s research activities;Utilize the project’s research results to help achieve its desired outcomes; andPlay an active role in translating or mobilizing knowledge to ensure that the research results have an impact.Note: Only Canadian university researchers who are eligible to receive NSERC funds can apply for an Alliance grant.Eligible Projects:Must be relevant in natural sciences or engineering;Cannot use an Alliance grant to support secret or contract research;Eligible Expenses:Salary support for research trainees (undergraduates, graduates and postdoctoral fellows) to perform research and related training;Salary support for technicians and research professional personnel;Materials and supplies;Activities that support collaborations and knowledge mobilization related to the project; andActivities to develop and grow the research collaborations with the partner organizations.Program Details:Option 1:The purpose of this stream is to:Generate new knowledge and/or technology to address complex challenges;Create economic, social and/or environmental benefits;Contribute to Canada’s long-term competitiveness;Support public policy;Train new researchers in areas that are important to Canada and to the partner organizations; andDraw on diverse perspectives and skill sets to accelerate the translation and application of research results.No limits on the number of applications per year;Value: $20,000 to $1,000,000 per year;Duration: 1-5 years.Option 2:In addition to Option 1 objectives, the purpose of this stream is also to:Address a societal challenge that will result in new natural sciences and engineering knowledge and societal impact;Bring together academic, partner organization, and societal perspectives and skillsets throughout the collaboration; andDemonstrate how all interested individuals will learn about and use the products, services, or policies that stem from this research.Limit of number of applications:1 within a 12-month period for researchers as applicants/co-applicants.Value: $30,000 to $300,000;Duration: 1-5 years; andNSERC will assess the relevance and potential impact of each partner organization and their proposed in-kind contributions and will give priority to funding projects that demonstrate clear relevance to the partner organizations and potential to provide economic, social and/or environmental benefits for Canada and Canadians.

      Grant Criteria 
      Amber Grants are comprised of 4 women's business grants broken out by category, including the Monthly Amber Grant, the Startup Grant, and the $50,000 Annual Amber Grant. To be considered for all these grants, applicants only need to apply once and will then be considered for all the grants which they are eligible for. The intent of the grants is to help women-owned businesses across Canada and the United States.Grant Value:Monthly Amber Grant: $10,000 for the top prize, $1,000 for 4 of the top 5 finalists (monthly)Business Category Grants: $10,000 (1 winner per month)The Startup Grant: $10,000 (1 winner per quarter)The Non-Profit Grant: $10,000 (1 winner per quarter)$25,000 Annual Amber Grant: $50,000 (3 winners per year)Note: Application to the Monthly Amber Grant allows applicants to receive an additional $10,000/$25,000 if eligible for the 3 categories- totaling a maximum grant value of $10,000  (monthly)+ $10,000 (Business Category)+ $10,000 (startup or non-profit, if applicable) + $50,000 (annual).Turnaround Time:Monthly Amber Grant: the 5 finalists will be announced by the 15th of the following month. The winner will be announced by the 23rd of the following monthThe Startup Grant: winner will be announced in March, June, September, and December of each yearThe Non-Profit Grant: winner will be announced in March, June, September, and December of each yearAt the end of the year, three of the 36 Business Category Grant winners is selected for a $30,000 year-end grant.Eligible Applicants:Eligibility across all grants:Businesses, startups, and non-profits must be at least 50% women-owned;The applicant must be a minimum of 18 years old;Be based in Canada or the United States.Additional eligibility for the Startup Grant:Be in the"idea phase" of business; ORHave less than $10,000 in sales.Additional eligibility for the Non-Profit Grant:Be a non-profit business/organization that benefits the community.Additional eligibility for the Business Category Grants:Be in the business category of the month:January - Skilled Trades;February - Health and Fitness;March - Food & beverage;April - Sustainability;May - Mental & emotional support;June - Business Support Service;July - Animal services;August - Haircare & skincare;September - Education & child care;October - Creative arts;November - Technology;December - Fashion & interior designers.Note: Applicants who fall under these specific business categories automatically become eligible (once per year) for the monthly $10,000 Business Category Grant. The same application remains active for the Category grant until the month of your category.Program Details:The deadline for the Monthly Amber Grant is at 11:59 pm Eastern Time on the last day of each month;The $50,000 Annual Amber Grant will be awarded to 3 of the previous Monthly Amber Grant winners;Applicants only need to apply once to be considered for all the grants they are eligible for;Applicants will be charged $15 for the application fee upon submission;Applicants will receive an email confirmation after the application is submitted;Details on the process will be included in the confirmation email.If the application does not get selected, it will not roll forward to the following month;Applicants who have not been selected will not be permitted to apply within 3 months of the application submission;Applicants who have not been selected should only reapply when something significant has changed in the business model or circumstances.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Apartment Construction Loan Program provides low-cost financing(loans) to a minimum of $1 million to support the construction of standard rental housing. It also supports the conversion of non-residential to standard rental housing.Grant Value: up to 100% loan to cost for residential space and up to 75% loan to cost for non-residential space to a minimum of $1 million.Turnaround Time: Approximately 6-7 months.Eligible Applicants:Private entrepreneur/builder/developer;Public or private non-profit housing organization;Rental co-operative (Note: equity co-ops are
not eligible); andOther levels of government (Indigenous Governing
Body, Province, Territory, Municipality).Eligible Projects:Have at least 5 rental units;Have a loan size of at least $1 million;Respond to a need for rental supply;The primary purpose of the project must be considered residential with the non-residential component not to exceed 30% of total gross floor space nor 30% of total cost; andBe permanent in nature (long-term stay).Program Details:Must meet and maintain one of the following affordability requirements for at least 10 years:Option 1: At least 20% of units must have rents below 30% of the median total income of all families in the subject market.Option 2:Alternatively, the requirement may be met if rents are established pursuant to an affordable housing program or other initiative (federal, provincial, territorial or municipal) that approves the proposal and provides support for the development of the standard rental housing project.Properties must be self contained units and primary use is residential with any non-residential component not exceeding 30% of total gross floor space;The proposed project must
respond to a need for rental supply;The program aims to prioritize the strongest projects applicants are encouraged to:Include accessible units within the project;Commit to deeper levels of affordability;Commit to a higher proportion of units being
considered affordable;Commit to longer affordability periods;Commit to greater levels of energy efficiency;Support community-oriented solutions;Work with other partners; and/orAchieve a unit mix that supports family-sized units.Once conditional approval is received CMHC will send application to CMLS for underwriting in which Application fees must be paid:Residential portion: $200 per unit for first 100 units,
then $100 per unit thereafter to a maximum of
$55,000 per loan; andNon-residential portion: 0.30% of the nonresidential loan amount if it exceeds $100,000.The borrower must have minimum net worth
equal to at least 25% of the loan amount being
requested, with a minimum of $100,000;There is a fixed interest rate that is locked in at first advance for certainty during the riskiest periods of development.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Must have the financial and operational ability to carry the project without ongoing subsidies and the ability to meet debt coverage ratio requirements;The borrower must have a minimum net worth
equal to at least 25% of the loan amount being
requested, with a minimum of $100,000.Process Best Practices:Ensure the application is fully complete when submitting as the program will only review fully completed applications.Forms and Links:Program Webpage: click hereGuidelines: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This program aims to meet the needs for new tools and technologies by co-investing in collaborative projects, comprised of consortia of two or more partner companies, that utilize artificial intelligence to help grow Canada's plant-based food, feed and ingredients ecosystem. Grant Value: Grant value is set at $4.1 million however this is the average across Protein Industries Canada programs as there is no set maximum a project can receive however the program will reimburse up to 45% of eligible costsTurnaround Time: Approximately 6-8 weeks.Eligible Applicants: Applicants must be a member of Protein Industries Canada;Must be a consortium of a minimum 2 Protein Industries Canada members, at least one of which is a Small or Medium Enterprise with 499 or fewer employees;Each member of the consortium must contribute to the project in a meaningful way;At least 2 members of the consortium must contribute financially to the project;A consortium may include academic or research institution(s). Not mandatory but encouraged;At least two partners must be Canadian companies or multi-national corporation that are legally entitled to do business in Canada with a significant Canadian business operation; andAt least one consortium member should represent a target customer or user of the new technology solution.Eligible Activities: Technology Leadership- activities in this area include:Advancing platform technologies central to future competitiveness; and Building a technology advantage for the Global Innovation Cluster.Partnership for Scale - activities in this area include: Projects that serve a target group of members to support their growth including increased domestic demand for Global Innovation Cluster products and services or by facilitating expansion;Linking start-tips with strategic partners;Offering business mentoring, consulting and coaching;Supply chain development or integration efforts for Global Innovation Cluster SMEs with local anchor firms; andWorking with public entities that provide access to capital and financing.Diverse and Skilled Talent Pools- activities in this area include: Recruitment campaign to repatriate Canadian talent to the Global Innovation Cluster;Development of curricula linked to industry needs and workforce integration programs for students;Development and promotion of specialized certifications in areas of technology leadership;Retraining programs for existing workforce;Assessment of Industry's workforce current or anticipated needs; andBuilding awareness of industry demand for skilled talent across stakeholder groups.Access to Innovation- activities in this are include: Support for access to specialized technical services;Installation of and access to dedicated laboratory or cutting-edge equipment; andAcquisition and assertion of jointly held intellectual property. Global Advantage- activities in this area include: Global Innovation Cluster promotion;Investment attraction to the general region of Global Innovation Cluster;Studies to identify new global markets for Global Innovation Cluster products and services;Participation in or leadership of trade missions to key markets;Development of regulatory or policy proposals to enhance technological advantage; andDevelopment and promotion of new international standards that incorporate the Canadian approach. Program Details: There are 3 streams under this program, the Project Stream, the System Stream and the Community Stream; Project Stream: This stream is designed to help individuals companies within the plant-based food, feed and ingredient ecosystem incorporate AI as a core business function;This requires collaboration with one or more entities within the AI ecosystem.Example of a project within this stream is a food manufacturer that wants to employ AI in the form of imaging technology and process automation for food safety and/or quality assurance.System Stream: This stream will focus on overall sector competitiveness and will require multiple partners from the plant-based food, feed and ingredient ecosystem; andAn example of a project within this stream is a consortium of plant-based food companies that are looking to iterate new products faster and improve consumer acceptance.Community Stream: This stream will help ensure that benefits of AI application in the plant-based food space are achieving societal benefits. This stream will focus on the nexus between plant-based foods and human health, as well as between plant-based foods environmental health; andAn example of a project in this stream could be a collaboration between national health advocacy agencies along with a number of plant-based food companies to use AI to design food products that help achieve certain health outcomes or to address health concerns.Protein Industries Canada will require all project participants to report on the IP assets generated by
their project, which may include patents, trade secrets, trademarks, copyright, data sets and other
types of intangible assets.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices: This program does not allow for funding to be used retroactively;All projects are required to pay a project administration fee to Protein Industries Canada. This fees will be 4% of the total eligible reconciled project cost; and This program can be stacked with other sources of funding. Forms and Links: Program Webpage: click here.Program Guidelines: click here.

      Grant Criteria 
      This funding stream supports projects that encourage economic growth, diversification, business competitiveness, and job creation in Northern Ontario. Through repayable and non-repayable contributions, it aims to strengthen the regional economy. Grant Value: The program does not set a specific funding dollar amount; however, supported projects may typically receive up to approximately $1–$1.5 million, depending on project scope and economic impact.Turnaround Time: Not specified. Eligible Applicants: Incorporated small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) with less than 499 employees (including Indigenous businesses such as First Nations, Métis, and Inuit);Other eligible legal entities capable of entering into binding agreements with FedNor;Priority may be given to manufacturers and value-added businesses in the mining supply, forestry, clean technology, bioeconomy, and agri-food sectors; andProjects must benefit Northern Ontario (economic benefits accrue primarily in the region)Note: Retail/wholesale, construction, tourism, and service-based businesses are not eligible under this program.Eligible Activities: Activities that support increased capacity and competitiveness of Northern Ontario SMEs.Eligible Costs:Labour costs (wages and benefits);Machinery, equipment, and training fees;Leasehold improvements;Professional/advisory/technical services; andMarketing costs (design, promotional materials, trade shows) when part of larger project.Ineligible Costs:Regular maintenance and ongoing operations;Scheduled capital expenditures/asset replacement;Refinancing existing debt;Land and building acquisition; andCosts incurred before eligibility date. Program Details:The BGC program foster economic growth and competitiveness of Northern Ontario businesses through investments that support:Access to capital;Modernization of operations and management;Trade, exports, and new market access.Applicants must demonstrate : Sustainable business model (normally 2+ years of operations); andFinancial capacity to complete project and repay contribution.Benefits must accrue to Northern Ontario;The program requires applicant contributions toward total project costs;Funding repayment begins no later than 1 year after project completion;Applications are made through the client portal after discussing the project with one of FedNor Officers. 

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligibility Best Practices:Must demonstrate clear benefit to Northern Ontario’s economy (job creation, diversification, innovation, increased competitiveness);Quantify impacts where possible (e.g., jobs created/maintained, increased revenues, productivity gains);Activities must directly support business growth, productivity, or competitiveness; andBusinesses must align with priority sectors such as manufacturing, value-added industries, clean technology, bioeconomy, forestry, mining supply, and agri-food.Process Best Practices:Limited budget availability due to high demand, applicants must contact FedNor officers before applying; andProvide complete and up-to-date financial documentation. Forms: Program website: click hereApplication Portal: click here

andUnemployed participants may be able to continue their EI benefit while in training under COJG.Note: Business owners, including individuals with a controlling interest in the applicant business, are not eligible as trainees under COJG.Eligible Training: Under 1 year in duration;Offered by an Ontario training provider classified as one of the following;Colleges of Applied Arts and Technology;Publicly-assisted universities;School boards;Private trainers operating in compliance with the Private Career Colleges Act, 2005;Union-based training centres;Product vendors (service providers who also produce or sell the product used in training): Training cannot be how to use the product or service;Training must be unrelated to the use of the product or service;Training involving essential skills, specialized and technical skills, management and business skills, and soft skills in the areas of career development, maintenance, and refresher training; and Must be transferrable/universal skills learned.For under 25 participants or under must apply through service provider in respective area; andFor over 25 participants must apply directly through the Ministry of Training, Colleges and Universities.Ineligible Training: Training that the employer legally has to provide itself;Executive training courses (MBA, CFA);Preparatory training courses (LSAT, MCAT, GMAT);Business Consulting services; Apprenticeship training; andTraining that displaces existing staff or replaces staff currently on lay-off.Note: The employer may deem many applications of over $25,000 ineligible depending on funding availability.Eligible Expenses:Tuition fees or fees charged by the training provider;Mandatory student fees;Textbooks, software, and other required materials;Equipment, clothing, tools;Examination fees; andTravel costs up to $500 (if the participant is traveling at least 24km each way).Eligible Training Provider:If the selected training is through a private trainer, then the training provider must meet the following requirements:Must have been in business and conducting training for at least 2 years at the time of application submission;Declare any conflict of interest between the employer, training participants and/or product vendor;Within the preceding 10 years, experience working in a profession relevant to the training being provided with:48 months of experience or teaching a program to prepare a student for the field (or a combination of the two); ORAt least 24 months of experience with one of the following qualifications:A Canadian bachelor’s degree (or equivalent foreign degree)A certificate of qualification issued under the Ontario College of Trades and Apprenticeship Act, 2009Status as a graduate of a college of applied arts and technology or registered private career college (or equivalent institution outside Ontario)Third-party regulatory requirements (if applicable)Program Details:Applications for 25 participants or under can apply through service providers; ORApplications for over 25 participants must apply directly through the Ministry of Training, Colleges and Universities (See Forms below).Applications are assessed by priority measured by these three tiers:1. Training results in a new or higher position and this is the employer's first successful application in the last 6 months;2. Training results in a new or higher position but this is not the employer's first successful application in the last 6 months OR training does not result in a new or higher position;3. Training per trainee is below $500 and lasts no longer than 1 week OR the training is required due to legislation, regulation or policy.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:This program cannot be combined with other provincial or federal funding;Funding is not retroactive and training should not be paid for until application approval;Priority will be given to Tier 1 applications where employers who have not received Canada-Ontario Job Grant funding in the past six months and there is an increase in wages for participants;Applicants are advised to use the Assessment Tool prior to applying;Tier 2 applicants will only be approved if there is sufficient program funding remaining.Process Best Practices:Employers can hold spots (apply without candidates) however, if they are requesting more funding, they will need to ensure they have identified new hires at that time;3 quotes are needed from different training providers (if cost of application exceeds $2500 or $700 per participant per day);Applicants with total budget requested under $25,000 (total) will process faster than those requesting above this amount;There is no limit to the amount of applications;Applicants may have training courses running concurrently (with one participant on one course at a time); If any training changes occur after the COJG training agreement has been signed, the employer is to immediately notify the service provider or the ministry; andReimbursement - 70% of the training costs will be reimbursed upon proof of payment—the remaining will be reimbursed upon completion of training.Forms: Program website and attestation forms: click hereApplication Portal: click here

      Grant Type
      Loan
    
    
      Grant Amount
      $500,000
    
    
      Regions
      All of Canada
    
    
      Industries
      Agriculture - Crop, Agriculture - Dairy, Agriculture - Livestock, Agriculture - Tree Fruit
