      Government of Canada
     

    
      Deadline
      
        

          Open until filled
      
    
    
  





    
      




  

      Grant Criteria 
      The Canadian Agricultural Loans Act program guarantees loans of up $500,000 to farmers and agricultural co-operatives. The program is intended for direct producers in the agriculture sector that are seeking to purchase the purchase, repair, construction of buildings and machines. The purchase of tools, machines, and breeding livestock is also eligible under this program.Loan Value:Up to $500,000 for the purchase of land and the construction or improvement of buildingsUp to $350,000 for all other loan purposes, including consolidation/refinancingNote: maximum of lender's prime rate plus 1%Turnaround Time: 15 business daysEligible Applicants:Must engage in one of the following:The production of field-grown crops, cultivated and uncultivated, and horticultural crops;The raising of livestock, poultry, and fur-bearing animals;The production of eggs, milk, honey, maple syrup, tobacco, fibre, wood from woodlots, and fodder crops;The production or raising of any other prescribed thing or animal.Must be one of the following organization types:Sole proprietors;Partnerships;Corporations; andCo-operative association.Must have a majority (50% + 1) farmer membership.The program allows farmers of all types to be eligible, including:Existing farmers;Beginning farmers (that is, less than 6 years of farming);Start-up farmers;Farmers taking over the family farm; andPart-time farmers.Note: Greenhouses are eligible under the programEligible Lenders:Chartered banks;Credit unions;Caisses populaires;Alberta Treasury Branches; andAny other organization designated by the Minister.Eligible Activities:Purchase of land;Construction, repair or alteration of any building or structure on a farm;Purchase, installation, alteration, major overhaul, or major repair to/of:Tools, implements, apparatus, and machines of any kind not usually affixed to real or immovable property;Machinery and apparatus for the generation or distribution of electricity, whether or not affixed to real or immovable property.Purchase of breeding livestock that will provide a long-term improvement to a farm operation including:Horses and other equinesCattle, sheep, goats, and other ruminants;Swine, poultry, bees, and fur-bearing animals;Any other prescribed animal.Erection or construction of fencing or works for drainage;Clearing, breaking, irrigating and reclaiming of land;Conservation of soil, prevention of soil erosion by the planting of trees and shelter belts;Repair or overhaul of fencing where the cost is $2,000 or more;Purchase and the planting of trees for syrup production and the purchase and planting of fruit trees, Christmas trees, and ginseng, where the cost is $2,000 or more;Construction of a road or driveway on a farm;Land transfer tax, survey, appraisal and legal costs relating to the purchase of additional land;Purchase of shares for inter-generational farm transfers; andConsolidation/refinancing of loans.Note: A loan for the purchase of shares in a farm or farming operation can be financed under the program for up to $350,000.  These loans can be amortized for up to 10 years.Ineligible Activities:Improvements to the family dwelling;Quota purchases of any kind;Operating loans and loans for the purchase of short-term feeder livestock; andConsolidation of a lender's ordinary loans.Program Details:Eligible amount of the loan:Existing farmers - Loans to existing farmers must not exceed the lesser of 80% of the appraised value of the property for which the loan was madeBeginning farmers - Loans to beginning farmers must not exceed the lesser of 90% of the appraised value of the property for which the loan was made.Application process:Approach an eligible lender as listed above;The lender will go through its loan application process and determine the financing best suited for the applicant;The lender may then register the loan with the CALA program through either the online loan registration system or by mailing the forms and registration fee in.Registration fee:0.85% of the amount of the loan;This fee must be submitted to the "Receiver General for Canada" at the time of loan registration.Administration fee:An administration fee may also be charged by the lender. For loans up to $250,000, the administration fee is capped at 0.25% of the amount of the loan (to a maximum of $250). For loans over $250,000, the administration fee is capped at 0.1% of the amount of the loan.Repayment terms:15 years for land purchases. Lenders may amortize loans for longer than 15 years provided a balloon payment is scheduled for the loan at the end of the 15 year period. The remaining loan amount could then be refinanced under the Canadian Agricultural Loans Act (CALA) for a further 10 years.10 years for all other purposes.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Process Best Practices:The lender organization will go through the loan application process and determine the financing best suited for the applicant's needs, which may or may not include a loan under the Canadian Agricultural Loans Act program.Forms:Program webpage: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Canadian Agricultural Strategic Priorities Program (CASPP) provides funding of up to 75% of eligible expenses up to $1,000,000. Typically only non-profit organizations and Indigenous groups are eligible for the program. However, if for-profit organizations are able to deliver significant benefits to the sector or the public good, they may also be considered for funding. The program's strategic priorities include adopting or commercializing new technology,  advancing environmental sustainability, sector capacity building, and addressing emerging sector-wide issues. The intent of the program is to help the Canadian agricultural sector remain competitive.Grant Value: 50%-75% of eligible expenses up to $1,000,000Note: The program may normally contribute 50% of eligible project costs, but may contribute up to 75% if the project is a high priority for the agricultural sector or for the Canadian public.Turnaround Time: within 100 business days from the date of submissionEligible Applicants:Be either: Non-profit organizations and associations, cooperatives, and marketing boards;Indigenous groups.Be legal entities that can enter into legally binding agreements; andHave relevant projects that are Canadian or sector-wide in scope.Note: For-profit organizations are normally ineligible, but if the project delivers significant benefits to the sector or the public good, they may also be considered for funding.Eligible Activities:Adaptation to new technology:Coordinated approaches to adapt and take full advantage of emerging opportunties;;Test and adopt technology solutions in collaboration with research centres;Solving technical hurdles to overcome barriers to the adoption of new technology in Canadian agriculture;Develop more value-added products.Environmental sustainability:Support the development of environmental initiatives, increase resilency, and projects adopting or demonstrating environmental technology; Complement environmental sustainability and climate change activities under the sustainable Canadian agricultural partnership and other programs.Strategic development and capacity building:Support organizational capacity;Support transformation in the agricultural sector;Develop strategic planning initiatives that complement value chain roundtable, agri-food economic table and other discussions.Addressing emerging issues:Program is available to support the agricultural sector in responding to unforeseen circumstances that require identification and planning for future changes expected in the sector.Eligible Expenses:Administrative CostsOngoing or core activities and overhead expenses (fundamental operational activities) will be calculated at a flat rate of 10% of total project costs.Capital assets with a per-item cost of more than $100,000 will not be included in the calculation of administrative costs.Salaries and benefits;Only the wages and benefits of staff directly related to the project are eligible.Contracted services;Professional or specialized services for which a contract is entered into, such as inspection, consultant/expert services, installation, and Canadian Environmental Assessment Act 2012.Travel costs;Costs directly related to the project, such as: per diems (accommodations, meals, taxis, and incidentals); air, rail and ground transportation (to an out-of-city destination).Capital assets;Costs that are tangible assets that are purchased, constructed, developed, or otherwise required to complete the project;Expenditures for capital assets should not exceed 25% of total project costs.Other direct project costs.Costs that are for project-related deliverables, such as shipping, translation, marketing costs related to the production of materials/documents/knowledge transfer, and other costs that AAFC deems eligible.Note: All costs must be incurred after the Contribution Agreement is signed. A complete breakdown of Eligible expenses can be found hereProgram Details:Applicants may submit and receive funding for more than 1 project;Maximum funding cannot exceed $5 million over 5 years per applicant;The application process is comprised of 2 stages:Stage 1: Pre-screeningMust download and submit CASPP pre-screening summary;Only successful applicants will be invited to Stage 2.Stage 2: Full applicationIf the program requests additional information, applicants must submit the required documents/information within 30 days of the request.Advances in funding may be made available based on the program's assessment of the project risk;Applications must show how the activities support a competitve and market-oriented agriculture, agri-food and agri-based products sector that proactively manages ricks through: Supporting sustainable growth, adaption and sector prosperity; andSupporting the sector to be more innovative, safer and stronger.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Funding from this program may be used in conjunction with other sources of grant funding (Federal, Provincial, municipal, and other sources) so long as combined funding does not exceed 85% of eligible project expenses;This program does not allow funding to be used for costs incurred prior to the signing of the Contribution Agreement; andFor more information on eligible and ineligible costs, please see the Annex B section.Forms:Program webpage: click hereOnline portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The CanExport – Innovation (CXI) program offers funding to researchers from Canadian small and medium-sized businesses, universities and NGOs who aim to commercialize their technology abroad. The program assists companies pursuing international collaboration (e.g. for the purposes of R&D) and seeking to establish key partnerships in foreign markets.Grant value: 75% of eligible costs to a maximum of $75,000 (based on project total of $100,000)Note : For Nov 17th intake, the program is prioritizing applications with budget of less than $50,000 (maximum funding is $37,500).Turnaround Time: Within 60 business daysEligible Applicants:Organizations can either be:  Small or Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs)  ORAcademic institutions OR;Non-government research centers.Have Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) business number;Have existing prototype;Own the intellectual property for their technology or product;Technology must be at Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 4 or higher;Technology intended to be commercialized within 5 years;Have clear benefit to Canadian economy should proposed project be successful;Must have financial and HR capacity to carry out proposed activities and cover their share of costs;Must not receive more than 75% government assistance for the same activities;Returning applicants must have demonstrated a good track record of progress reporting and effective use of CanExport Innovation funding.Note: The applicant eligibility will be part of the assessment criteria. Please ensure all the criteria are met.Eligible Activities:Activities in pursuit of key strategic partnerships with foreign organizations and individuals, with the overarching aim of commercializing technology:Partnerships should have the following objectives:Securing investments from foreign partners for R&D work;Licensing or purchasing the Intellectual Property of foreign partner's technology;Negotiating R&D collaborations that will lead to development, adaptation or validation of applicant's technology.Technology development or enhancement work with foreign partner, including:Working with the foreign partner to conduct a pilot of the applicant's technology:Working with the foreign partner to conduct clinical trials using the applicant's technology;Leveraging the technical expertise and/or technology of the foreign partner to test the applicant's technology.Technology validation:Pilot application and clinical trials.Virtual meetings;Pre-identified in-person meetings;Seeking expert legal business advice from consultants;For the purposes of:New certification requirements (only for countries where there is a pre-identified partner);Navigating foreign market legal framework;Pursuing IP protection;Due diligence on foreign partner and its technology;Drafting/ reviewing legal agreements;Identifying potential foreign partners;Market research; andInternational expansion roadmap.Development of professional promotion plans or materials for meetings with potential partners;Applying for intellectual property (IP) protection in the country of the foreign partners;Shipping applicant's technology for assessmentIneligible Activities:All activities after partnership formalization;Any services requiring payments to/from foreign partners;R&D activities;Customizing the technology to client's needs;Activities for sales and distribution purposes;Manufacturing;Client acquisition; andLobbying.Eligible Expenses:Consultant and legal fees (previously capped at $4,000); Foreign regulation certification fees;Only eligible in countries where the applicant has a pre-identified partner.Intellectual property protection fees;Development and printing of promotional materials;Translation or interpretation services (maximum cost: $2,000); Shipping costs (maximum cost: $4,000); Eligible travel expenses;Approval will be assessed based on:Duration - maximum of 5 days per travel destination;Number of participants - maximum of 2 travelers per trip;Costs (high costs may impact approval).Per diem (ie. accommodation & meals);Capped at $400 per approved travelerSingle entry visas; andRegistration fees for virtual/in-person events; andCost of video conferencing platform (only covered during the months in which meetings with the project partners are scheduled to take place).  Note: The program only supports travel activities that comply with the Government of Canada's travel advisories.Ineligible Expenses:Expenses incurred prior to application submission;Any travel expenses that are inconsistent with Canada's official travel advisories;Airfare costs paid with bonus points from programs such as Air Miles/Aeroplan/World Points or any other barter systems;Capital costs and office supplies;Cell phone charges;Passport costs;Costs of hospitality, entertainment, and gifts;Core activities and overhead expenses;Salaries and commissions;Goods and Services Tax; Event registration that includes booth fees; Events where meetings and pre-identified foreign partners have not been confirmed; andRental and/or installation of a booth for a conference or exhibition.Note: Please see guidelines for a full list of eligible and ineligible expenses. The list above is a selection of most common expenses.Program Details:If a project is approved, the start date of the funding agreement (the date that expenses are eligible) will be the application submission date;The program does not reimburse expenses incurred prior to a project’s start date.A project must focus on only 1 technology per project application;A project can target multiple partners to achieve multiple R&D objectives;Assessment criteria:Applicant eligibility;Technology readiness (TRL 4 and above - beyond ideation stage and into initial prototype creation) and ownership;The methodology used for pursuing partnership;Selection of foreign partners.Must demonstrate:Appropriate skillsExpertiseTechnology compatibility;Ability to make technical contributions.Successful applicants will receive a funding agreement by email, and must sign the agreement within 20 business days. Failure to do so may result in the forfeiture of the funds; Funding recipients must submit a final report no later than 7 days after the completion of the project; andThough all decisions made by CanExport are final and non-negotiable, however, revised applications may be resubmitted.

Any of these types of activities will be rejected.Process Best Practices:CanEx Innovate is a competitive program with limited funding, so the quality of the application is extremely important. andEmployers cannot apply without a candidate. Ineligible Employers:Post-secondary institutions;Banks or large financial sector employers; andFederal or provincial government.Eligible Candidates:Canadian Citizen, permanent resident, or a protected person defined by the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act;Must be a registered student in a post-secondary institution program;Private colleges may be eligible on a case-by-case basis;Pursuing a tech-immersive career;The student must not be an international student with a work permit; andThe student must not be an immediate family member of the employer with the same employer previously.Note: Proof of enrollment in a Canadian post-secondary institution is required, but an unofficial transcript is sufficient.Program Details:IntakesWinter 2025 - January 1, 2025, to March 31, 2025: CLOSED Summer 2025 - May 1, 2025, to August 31, 2025: CLOSEDFall 2025 - September 1- December 31, 2025: CLOSEDWinter 2026 - Launches November 17, 2025.Positions must be IT-related (e.g. software, programming, web/app development) OR Business-related (e.g. sales, business development, or marketing roles that promote tech skills development);Must be no more than 16 weeks in duration;The position can be full- or part-time;Minimum 15 hours per week;Maximum applications per employer: 5;Placements must be "net new," meaning that the SWPP student is incremental to the employer's "baseline" of student hires. andFirst-year students.Turnaround Time: 2 business daysEligible Employers:Be directly or indirectly involved in the aviation/aerospace industry;Ie. aviation/aerospace organization, supplier of goods and services for the aviation/aerospace industry.Have registered business number;Have WorkSafeBC or Workers’ Compensation Board registration;Have General Liability Insurance;Employer Liability Insurance of $2,000,000 minimum; andGeneral Liability Insurance of $2,000,000 minimum.Must have participants on payroll; Cannot be receiving other federal funding for the placement; andEmployers must apply with a candidate.Eligible Participants:Must be a current student enrolled (full-time or part-time) in a recognized Canadian post-secondary institution;Proof of enrollment required.Canadian citizens, Permanent Residents or persons with refugee protection legally entitled to work in their placement province; andMust have a co-op, internship, or practicum as a part of their study plan during the placement term or recognized work-integrated learning in the next semester.Ineligible Participants:Immediate family members of CCAA or employer;Must not be a recipient of Employment Insurance; andApprentices.Placement Details:The position must support the aviation and aerospace industry;Full-time or part-time positions;12 hours/week minimum is encouraged;An 8-week placement minimum is encouraged;1 placement is considered to take place over 4 months;An 8-month contract can result in 2 placements for a student, and a 12-month contract may result in 3 placements.Employers can fund up to 5 participants per term;Work-integrated learning must be in the participant's study plan and span over the duration of the placement;Employers to have identified participants and confirmed placements for the application;All aviation and aerospace businesses and post-secondary institutions can be pre-approved if desired, even before the selection of one or more students, presuming student eligibility.Employers must provide a company description, including the business number, company website, and job description;Employers must develop a learning plan for the participant;Wage subsidies in this program are reimbursements following an agreed payment schedule;Advance payments are possible for small and medium-sized businesses and nonprofits if there are operational cash flow needs.       Grant Criteria 
      This program aims to accelerate technology development and deployment that contribute to the 2030 Innovation Target by funding up to 50% of eligible projects to a maximum of $2 million per project. The funding is open to technology developers industry,  industrial associations, small and medium-sized enterprises, research and development (R&D) organizations, post-secondary institutions, municipalities, not-for-profit organizations,   government research labs, and individuals who are seeking funding to advance innovation-commercialization or knowledge generation.Grant Value: 25-50% of eligible costs to a maximum of $2 millionTurnaround Time: 3-6 months (depends on the project dollar size)Eligible Applicants:Be 1 of the following applicant types:Technology developers;Industry;Industrial associations;Small and medium-sized enterprises;Research and development (R&D) organizations;Post-secondary institutions;Municipalities;Not-for-profit organizations;Government research labs; andIndividuals.Not required to be based in Alberta;Must demonstrate a clear value proposition for the province; andBe in 1 of the 5 technology portfolios:Advanced hydrocarbons:Cleaner hydrocarbon production; andInnovative hydrocarbon products.Clean Technology:Renewable and alternative energy;Bioenergy; andCarbon capture, and utilization.Environmental innovation:Land and biodiversity; andWater innovation.Smart agriculture and food; andBioindustrial materials.Eligible Expenses:Labour;Materials;Capital assets and software;Travel;Sub-contractors; andOther.Note: full breakdown of eligible expenses can be found here.Program Details:The program prioritizes technology or knowledge development projects;Technology  solutions  can  originate  from  anywhere  globally  but  must  address  challenges  and  opportunities of importance to Alberta;Projects that will be researched, piloted, demonstrated, and/or implemented in Alberta with long term Alberta-based infrastructure/resources will be prioritized;Technology projects should demonstrate a Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of 3-7;All applicants are expected to provide a portion of the funding towards a project, which can include cash and in-kind contributions from project partners or other sources of funds;Funding made available through this Process is  provided to support the execution  of  projects  with  well-defined objectives, milestones, deliverables, and timelines;Regular project update meetings will be held with the applicant and the assigned Project Advisor to assess progress towards milestones.There are no restrictions on the number of applications that can be submitted by any applicant; andOnce projects are completed, Alberta Innovates continues to collect information from clients for up to 5-years to assess the economic, environmental, and social benefits realized for Albertans.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Though applicants are not required to have a project partner, the program prefers applicants with strong end-user partnerships and/or funding from other organizations;Letters of support and/or confirmation of contributions from interested end-users are strongly encouraged to accompany the application.Applicants are encouraged to engage Alberta's post-secondary and research institutions in the project consortium where appropriate.Forms:Program website: click hereApplication portal: click here

      The Co-op program offers up to $11,520 over a maximum span of 32 weeks to help employers hire post-secondary co-operative education students at a Nova Scotia university or college. This is in order to benefit from the local talent that is preparing to enter the workforce.  The intent of the program is to help post-secondary students gain valuable work experience while helping employers derisk the building of their talent pipelines.Grant Value:Up to $4,800 ($7.50/hour subsidy) for regular studentsUp to $5,760 ($9/hour subsidy) for designated diversity group students (see Eligible Participants section for eligibility)Note: The maximum subsidy amount could be double the listed amount if the education program has 32-week terms as opposed to the standard 16 weeks.Turnaround Time: 7 weeksEligible Employers:For-profit and non-profit organizations;Charitable organization;Social enterprise;Municipality; Must place participants on payroll; andEmployer can identify candidate after application is approved.Eligible Candidates:Must live in Nova Scotia;Enrolled in a cooperative program at a Nova Scotia post-secondary institution;Students who self-identify in any of the following groups are eligible to receive a diversity bonus of $1.50 per hour:Mi’kmaq or Indigenous;African Nova Scotian;A visible minority; A person
with a disability;A woman in an under-represented occupation; orAn international student.Family members may be eligible if the participant is in an underrepresented group and the employer has followed a fair hiring process.Program Details:Co-op intake periods:FALL 2025 (Sept 1 - Dec 31, 2025): Apply between April 15 and May 15, 2025.Winter 2026 (Jan 1 - March 31, 2026):Apply between 15 August and 15 September 2025Placement duration: 12 - 16 weeksExcept in cases where the academic program requires a longer term of up to 32 weeks, as confirmed by a Co-op Coordinator;Minimum wage: $15 per hour (plus vacation pay and other mandatory employment costs), and will be reimbursed $7.50 for each hour worked by the student;The work placement must be endorsed in advance by a university or college Co-op Coordinator;Organizations that receive funds from the Industrial Research Assistance Program (IRAP) or the Scientific Research & Experimental Development (SR&ED) tax credit may qualify for up to $10 an hour, calculated as 50% of the hourly wage paid to the student;Employers must return the contract within 1 week after approval;To make your reimbursement payment, you will be asked to provide proof of wages paid
to the student; andBoth employers and students must complete a survey at the end of the
agreement period for the grantor to issue payment.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:This program cannot be used in conjunction with other sources of government funding;This program is not retroactive as application deadlines are well in advance of the semester start dates;Preference is given to employers who:Provide challenging, knowledge-intensive work opportunities; Pay above-average wages;Demonstrate commitment to innovation and a culture of learning;Are internationally competitive (export-focused);Operate in Nova Scotia’s growth sectors;Have a commitment to diversity and employment equity;Hire graduates for permanent jobs.Employers must conduct a fair hiring process, including: Advertising the position (which can include language that indicates a preference for candidates from one of the populations above);Interviews; andA rationale for selection.Process Best Practices:If some or all of the positions have not been approved, employers can appeal the decision generally up to 1 week after the notification
emails are sent; andIf appealing, provide additional information about the position and
the tasks the student will be completing, clearly explaining what makes the experience
valuable to a co-op program and transferable to other career-related positions.Forms:Program website: click hereCo-op Coordinators list: click hereEmployer checklist: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Canadian Agricultural Strategic Priorities Program (CASPP) provides funding of up to 75% of eligible expenses up to $1,000,000. Typically only non-profit organizations and Indigenous groups are eligible for the program. However, if for-profit organizations are able to deliver significant benefits to the sector or the public good, they may also be considered for funding. The program's strategic priorities include adopting or commercializing new technology,  advancing environmental sustainability, sector capacity building, and addressing emerging sector-wide issues. The intent of the program is to help the Canadian agricultural sector remain competitive.Grant Value: 50%-75% of eligible expenses up to $1,000,000Note: The program may normally contribute 50% of eligible project costs, but may contribute up to 75% if the project is a high priority for the agricultural sector or for the Canadian public.Turnaround Time: within 100 business days from the date of submissionEligible Applicants:Be either: Non-profit organizations and associations, cooperatives, and marketing boards;Indigenous groups.Be legal entities that can enter into legally binding agreements; andHave relevant projects that are Canadian or sector-wide in scope.Note: For-profit organizations are normally ineligible, but if the project delivers significant benefits to the sector or the public good, they may also be considered for funding.Eligible Activities:Adaptation to new technology:Coordinated approaches to adapt and take full advantage of emerging opportunties;;Test and adopt technology solutions in collaboration with research centres;Solving technical hurdles to overcome barriers to the adoption of new technology in Canadian agriculture;Develop more value-added products.Environmental sustainability:Support the development of environmental initiatives, increase resilency, and projects adopting or demonstrating environmental technology; Complement environmental sustainability and climate change activities under the sustainable Canadian agricultural partnership and other programs.Strategic development and capacity building:Support organizational capacity;Support transformation in the agricultural sector;Develop strategic planning initiatives that complement value chain roundtable, agri-food economic table and other discussions.Addressing emerging issues:Program is available to support the agricultural sector in responding to unforeseen circumstances that require identification and planning for future changes expected in the sector.Eligible Expenses:Administrative CostsOngoing or core activities and overhead expenses (fundamental operational activities) will be calculated at a flat rate of 10% of total project costs.Capital assets with a per-item cost of more than $100,000 will not be included in the calculation of administrative costs.Salaries and benefits;Only the wages and benefits of staff directly related to the project are eligible.Contracted services;Professional or specialized services for which a contract is entered into, such as inspection, consultant/expert services, installation, and Canadian Environmental Assessment Act 2012.Travel costs;Costs directly related to the project, such as: per diems (accommodations, meals, taxis, and incidentals); air, rail and ground transportation (to an out-of-city destination).Capital assets;Costs that are tangible assets that are purchased, constructed, developed, or otherwise required to complete the project;Expenditures for capital assets should not exceed 25% of total project costs.Other direct project costs.Costs that are for project-related deliverables, such as shipping, translation, marketing costs related to the production of materials/documents/knowledge transfer, and other costs that AAFC deems eligible.Note: All costs must be incurred after the Contribution Agreement is signed. A complete breakdown of Eligible expenses can be found hereProgram Details:Applicants may submit and receive funding for more than 1 project;Maximum funding cannot exceed $5 million over 5 years per applicant;The application process is comprised of 2 stages:Stage 1: Pre-screeningMust download and submit CASPP pre-screening summary;Only successful applicants will be invited to Stage 2.Stage 2: Full applicationIf the program requests additional information, applicants must submit the required documents/information within 30 days of the request.Advances in funding may be made available based on the program's assessment of the project risk;Applications must show how the activities support a competitve and market-oriented agriculture, agri-food and agri-based products sector that proactively manages ricks through: Supporting sustainable growth, adaption and sector prosperity; andSupporting the sector to be more innovative, safer and stronger.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Funding from this program may be used in conjunction with other sources of grant funding (Federal, Provincial, municipal, and other sources) so long as combined funding does not exceed 85% of eligible project expenses;This program does not allow funding to be used for costs incurred prior to the signing of the Contribution Agreement; andFor more information on eligible and ineligible costs, please see the Annex B section.Forms:Program webpage: click hereOnline portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This federally funded program offers wage subsidies to employers in the cultural sector who wish to hire students for a work-integrated learning experience. The subsidy covers 70% of the student's salary, up to $7000. The student may be in any field of study, and the work does not need to be artistic or cultural in nature, as long as the employer is in the arts and culture sector (for example, a cultural sector employer can hire a computer science student to build a website). The goals of the program are to support partnerships between post-secondary institutions and the arts and culture sector, and to help students develop work-ready skills that will aid their transition into the workforce.Grant Value:Regular participants: 50% of wages to a maximum of $5,000Underrepresented participants: 70% of wages up to a maximum of $7,000Turnaround Time: 2 weeksEligible Employers:Canadian for-profit and not-for-profit employers in the cultural sector, including but not limited to the following sub-sectors:Digital media;Film and television;Performing arts;Music and sound recording;Visual arts and crafts;Writing and publishing; andHeritage.Employer can identify candidate before or after application. Note: Government institutions (federal, provincial, territorial, and municipal) are not eligible employers. Eligible Participants:Must be enrolled in a recognized Canadian post-secondary institution (part-time or full-time, graduate or undergraduate); Must be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or refugee;International students are NOT eligible;Must be legally entitled to work in Canada; andMust be added to the employer's payroll (not a contractor). Note: Employers are encouraged to prioritize students from under-represented groups, including Indigenous, Black, Persons of Colour, Persons with Disabilities, Official Language Minorities, Newcomers to Canada, and first-year students.Placement Details:There are no minimum or maximum placement lengths;Placements may be full-time or part-time;The placement must allow the student to apply their academic studies in a workplace setting;Remote work is permitted; andBoth the student and the employer must submit reports to the CHRC.

      Grant Criteria 
      The DÉPART program aims to help SMEs in driving economic recovery by providing access to funding and supporting initiatives such as feasibility studies, investment projects, and innovation activities. For feasibility studies, the program offers a non-repayable contribution covering up to 60% of eligible expenses. For other projects, the program offers a non-repayable contribution covering up to 50% of eligible expenses.Turnaround Time: Approximately 50 business days.Grant Value:Feasibility Study:60% between $15,000 and $150,000;Up to $25,000 annually for hiring a professional with a professional, technical, or undergraduate degree; and Up to $35,000 annually for hiring a professional with a graduate or postgraduate degree in the required field for project deployment.Other Projects:50% between $15,000 and $150,000Up to $25,000 annually for hiring a professional with a professional, technical, or undergraduate degree; and Up to $35,000 annually for hiring a professional with a graduate or postgraduate degree in the required field for project deployment.Eligible Applicants:For-profit small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) with 250 employees or fewer, legally constituted under the laws of Quebec or Canada, operating an active establishment in Quebec;Collective enterprises (cooperatives and non-profit organizations) as defined under the Social Economy Act with a primarily commercial activity;For‑profit businesses legally established under Quebec or Canadian law, with 250 employees or fewer;Operating within designated target areas for economic revitalization (specific territories identified by the program);Businesses in the following sectors:Manufacturing;Information and cultural industries (e.g., ICT, media);Accommodation;Tourism;Including accommodation enterprises that provide entertainment and leisure services and projects related to the development of cultural, scientific, recreational, outdoor, or other attractions for a regular tourist clientele with growth potentialWith the exception of tourist residences, bed and breakfasts, and campgroundsIneligible Applicants:Companies in the arts, entertainment, and recreation sector;Businesses in construction (except those tied to the Action Plan for the Construction Sector or productivity improvements);Retail and wholesale trade companies;Professional and financial services (including finance and insurance);Restaurants and food service businesses;Real estate, rental, and leasing companies; andPublic services, including health care, social assistance, education, and public administration;For the full list of eligible and ineligible applicants, click this link (french only).Eligible Projects:Feasibility studies;Investment projects including:Business creation, expansion, or modernization;Technological transition;Post‑acquisition investments;Development or demonstration of innovative products or processes.Technological adoption;Construction and renovation;Business buyouts;Innovation initiatives.Eligible Expenses:Professional fees for external consultants;Travel and accommodation for project implementation, per Quebec government guidelines;Salaries for hiring a new qualified professional in a relevant field, with required credentials; replacements not eligible;Acquisition, construction, development, or expansion of buildings;Purchase and installation of equipment or software for the project;Acquisition of new technology;R&D expenses for products or processes;Costs for approvals, compliance, or certifications;Expenses for real-world demonstrations to potential clients;Purchase of studies, data, or documentation needed for the project.Program Details:The project must be located in one of the targeted territories, such as specific MRCs (french only);The project must correspond to eligible sectors, including secondary/tertiary transformation of primary sector, manufacturing, value-added services (ICT, environmental services, industrial design), and tourism with cultural, scientific, or recreational components;Each business can receive a maximum of $300,000 in total funding. 

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices :This program does not provide retroactive funding; only expenses incurred after the application submission date are eligible;Stacking with other municipal or federal programs is permitted, provided the same expenses are not covered by other Investissement Québec funding; andProjects must be located in targeted territories identified by economic vitality indices or eligibility lists and must align with the eligible sectors defined by the program.Process Best Practices :Applicants must submit their application through ClicSEQUR Entreprises, ensuring all required forms and supporting documents are included;Applications should contain a detailed project description, financial structure, expected outcomes, and a clear demonstration of how the project supports economic revitalization;Supporting materials such as feasibility studies, investment plans, cost estimates, and documentation on innovation or technological adoption should be attached to strengthen the submission; andProjects will be assessed based on their contribution to regional development, innovation, productivity, and the creation or maintenance of skilled jobs.Links : Program Website (french only) : click hereDÉPART Client Kit (french only) : click hereProgram Guide (french only) : click hereFinancial Assistance Table (french only) : click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Development and Commercialization Program supports the development and commercialization of Ontario made products and services that integrate/adopt Critical technologies by providing funding 50% up to $200,000. The program enables SMEs to access technology facilities an capabilities across the province to develop, test, validate and showcase their products and services.Grant Value: 50% of eligible costs to a minimum of $50,000 and a maximum of $200,000Turnaround Time: pendingEligible Applicants:SME with fewer than 500 global full-time employees;Must have registered operations in Ontario and a valid CRA business number;Has the intent and potential to apply, exploit and/or commercialize the results of the project for the economic benefit of Ontario;Has the necessary expertise and resources to put the project into effect within an appropriate time frame;Adoption of critical technologies is part of their long-term product roadmap;All applicants and partners must be in good financial and reporting standing with OCI; andApplicants who have received over $500,000 of funding from OCI-administered programs in their lifetime (excluding TalentEdge) are required to obtain OCI approval before a new application for funding is initiated.Eligible Partners:SME applicant companies may choose to apply in collaboration with a strategic partner
company. (Not mandatory, but preference will be given to SME applicants with strategic
partners involved in their project outcomes);A strategic partner could be a private industry partner and/or public sector organizations such
as but not limited to a municipality, a healthcare facility, or a public utility;The strategic partner company should represent a significant potential commercial
partner/strategic client for the proposed innovative product/service;The SME and strategic partner must have an arm’s-length business relationship; andStrategic Partner must agree to complete the required OCI report.Eligible Project:Projects must support Critical Technology integration, adoption, demonstration, prototyping,
testing by the SME;The solution should involve the acceleration, development, or integration of at least one of the six
Critical Technologies (5G and Advanced networks, AI, blockchain, robotics, cybersecurity and
quantum);Projects should result in the development of a new solution, product, or service with strong
commercial opportunities in one or more of the four Key Sectors.Eligible Expenses:Sub-contractor and consultant fees if approved by OCI management prior to
the start of the project and if procured in accordance with the Broader Public
Sector (BPS) Procurement Directive;Research and Development costs directly related to the project;Project-related computer hardware and software, including specialized
hardware and software;Cost of usage of equipment;Cost of direct materials, necessary for specifically identified activities and
measured as having been used for, the completion of the project;Materials used for prototypes, configuring, testing production processes,
systems, and training employees;Cost of upgrade of project-related equipment;Capital lease of equipment (interest costs are not eligible);Project-related leasehold improvement costs (prior OCI approval required);Sales and marketing costs attributed to the project;Training costs directly attributable to the project; andCost of regulatory compliance (up to a maximum specified by OCI).Program Details:Project activities are to be carried out in Ontario;Minimum 1:1 contribution match from the Applicant;Project length maximum 6 months;Projects must involve the utilization of at least of the Technology development sites for a minimum of 2 hours per test bed; Projects must be the basis for a highly competitive business and must offer a good
return on investment and benefits to Ontario (e.g., new revenues, job creation/retention,
new customers, follow-on investment, and productivity improvement); andProjects must already have all necessary certifications, if required for a project to be executed.

It is intended to provide Canadian youth (aged 15-30 years old) with work experience and valuable skills to increase productivity and competitiveness in the economy's workforce. Grant Value: 80% of wages up to $18,000.Turnaround Time: 15 business daysEligible Employers:For-profit and non-profit organizations;Have fewer than 500 employees;Must be Canadian-owned or a Canadian subsidiary;Is in the environmental sector or has a job that is directly or indirectly environmentally related;Must pay for vacation pay, EI, CPP, and Workers Compensation or equivalent; andEmployers can apply with or without a candidate however they have 30 days once pre-approved to hire a candidate. Eligible Candidates:Age 15-30 inclusive;Recent post-secondary achievement for candidates in provinces (less than 4-5 years since graduation);Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or refugee;Cannot be a recipient of Employment Insurance; andSelf-assess as unemployed or underemployed (i.e. they are employed below their level of education and/or hold part-time employment).Internship Details:Roles related to content creation for websites, social media accounts, or ad campaigns are considered to be tech roles;The role must be environmentally related with a digital component;Must also have a focus on digital skill development.Full- or part-time;Placement duration: 3 months to 1 year;Maximum of 1 DS4Y placement per employer;Placement can be in-person or remote;Must offer reasonable wage rates for the level of experience and position;The employer must provide time for the participant to engage in training (online or in-person);The employer will need to guide and mentor the intern during the work term that adds to their overall development and skills-set and long-term growth; andParticipants must be on payroll.Eligible Training:Soft and technical skills development or enhancement. 

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:The program funding can be combined with other sources of provincial funding provided the total funding does not go over 100% of the candidate's wages;Process Best Practices:Pre-approved employers have 30 days to find a candidate. Once the candidates apply, please send the program an email with the candidates' details to pathways@eco.caAny substantial changes or termination of the work placement must be reported to Eco Canada immediately;Exposing intern(s) to work that enhance marketable skills is encouraged, especially with deliverable results that can be added to a portfolio or resume; andKeep pay stubs for wage claims, frequency of claims can be negotiated based on internship length and business needs.Forms:Application Guidelines: click hereApplication Portal: click here

The goals of the program are to connect employers with up-and-coming talent, and to provide meaningful work experiences for youth candidates. Grant value:Regular participants: 75% of wages and/or 100% of training costs to a maximum of $22,000; andAdditional funding may be available for training that support youth facing barriers such as Indigenous youth, participants with disabilities or participants in the North, rural or remote communities.Turnaround time: 10 business daysEligible Employer:Indigenous organizations, non-profits, for-profit companies, provincial, territorial, regional and municipal governments  and their departments and agencies;Organizations whose primary activity is the generation, transmission and distribution of electricity;Sector support, including renewables, in any of the following areas: R&D;Business development;Energy efficiency;Fuel switching;Clean energy technology;Smart grid;Energy Storage; Sustainable Development of non-renewable resources.Organizations engaged in the manufacturing of equipment or the provision of services necessary for generation, transmission or distribution of electricity;Employers must have a candidate identified before submitting an application. Eligible Candidate:Between 15 and 30 years of age at of the start of the placement or training;A Canadian citizen, or permanent resident, or a protected refugee;Legally entitled to work according to the relevant provincial/territorial legislation and regulations;Unemployed or underemployed at the start of placement;Must not be a full-time student; andParticipants need to be identified at the time of application.

      Grant Criteria 
      The B.C. Employer Training Grant provides funding of 80% of eligible costs to a maximum of $10,000 per employee to employers who support skills training for their new or current employees. Training can be taken at a public post-secondary institution or through a private training provider (additional course syllabus requirements apply), so long as training is in compliance with PTIB (see pages 15/16 of the PTIB Policy Manual here).  The intent of the program is to help British Columbians access the skills training required to adapt to the labour market’s changing job requirements, while also addressing the skills gap in the province.Grant Value: 80% of eligible training costs up to $10,000 per traineeTurnaround Time: Up to 40 business daysEligible Applicants:Be operating in B.C. for at least 1 year;Have a Business BCeID; andBe in good standing with the Province of B.C.Eligible TraineesCanadian citizens, permanent residents, or protected persons;Be either unemployed or employed by the applicant employer;Be at least 16 years at the time of application;Have no real or perceived conflict of interest with the employer.To ensure an application is not denied due to conflict of interest, employers wishing to train family members must email etg@gov.bc.ca with a clear justification for their choice of the participant following the submission of their application.Trainees could be from outside BC, so long as the employer is BC-based, is paying for the training and will continue to employ people who live in BCIneligible TraineesIndividuals employed by a company other than the employer at the time of application;Temporary foreign workers, international students, working holiday visas, or other temporary residents; andParticipants who are receiving Employment Insurance (EI) or Income Assistance (IA) without prior approval from the Ministry of Social Development and Poverty Reduction.EI or IA recipients are advised to seek approval from the Ministry of Social Development and Poverty Reduction prior to training.Eligible TrainingMust be relevant to the immediate needs of the business and the trainee's job;Must lead to a "better job", leading to one of the following results:Increased pay;Promotion or advancement to another position;Move from part-time to full-time employment; ORMove from temporary/casual/seasonal employment to permanent employment.Training with a start date on or after the date of application submission;Training duration must be 52 weeks in duration or less.Ineligible TrainingTraining toward diploma or degree programs;Training needed to maintain current skills/certification;Training that has already been funded for the same participant;Training that is simultaneously funded for the participant by another federal or provincial program;Ineligible training methods:Consulting;Coaching;Coaching may be permitted as part of training toward coaching certification or when coaching is needed to complement a broader skills training program.Mentorships;Trade shows;Annual meetings;Networking;Seminars;Conferences; andPaid practicums.Eligible Training Providers:Be a B.C.-based training provider;Exceptions may be considered in exceptional circumstances.Be arm's length from the employer with no real or perceived conflict of interest;Training providers must deliver training as the main business activity;Includes but not limited to the following types of training providers:B.C. public post-secondary institutions;Trade or technical schools designated by the Industry Training Authority (ITA);Private training institutions certified and designated by the Private Training Institutions Branch (PTIB);Exceptions may apply if the Ministry deems the provider is a qualified instructor and training is competitively priced.Training organizations run by a B.C. school district;Industry associations.Indigenous Elders.Only when the trainee is Indigenous; andThe request for Elder support will be assessed on a case-by-case basis. The application should identify the Elder(s) providing the supports, the associated costs, and a description of the Elder supports.Training providers must be in compliance with Private Training Institutions Branch (PTIB) (see pages 15/16 of the PTIB Policy Manual here);Examples of programs that DO NOT require approval include:A career-related program at a registered institution for which tuition is less than $4,000;  A career-related program at a designated institution for which tuition is less than $1,000; A language program at a designated institution that is no more than six months and lessthan $4,000;Any language program at a registered institution; andA commercial driving instruction program. Programs that DO require approval fall into three categories and include: Class A: Career-related programs with 40 or more hours of instruction, for which tuition is at least $4,000. A career-related program is defined as a program that has the purpose of enhancing students’ employability or ability to carry out a career occupation;Class B: Career-related programs at designated/interim designated institutions, other than Class A programs, for which tuition is at least $1,000; andClass C: Language programs at designated/interim designated institutions that are longer than six months or for which tuition is at least $4,000. A language program is defined as a program that has as its learning objective that students gain or improve proficiency in a language.Eligible ExpensesTuition feesMandatory student feesExamination feesTextbooks, software and other required materialsTravel costs, only under certain circumstances (please see Appendix C for more information)Mandatory unpaid practicums for occupational certificationsIneligible ExpensesMembership fees, subscription fees, annual fees, professional association duesSoftware purchase/license for the businessLaptops, tablets, and other hardwareEquipment (e.g. boots and tools)Participant wages while in trainingProgram Details:Maximum funding per fiscal year (April 1 - March 31): $300,000 per employer;Applications that are not assessed after 60 calendar days will be returned unassessed;Applicants must submit and appeal within 15 days of having an application denied;Applicants can have paid for training prior to applying however cannot have started training prior to applying;Each course must be applied for in a separate application;If separate payments are required for individual courses, the applicant will need to submit separate applications for each course.Employers must pay all costs in full before reimbursement claims can be made;Training should be of no cost to the trainees. If the trainee pays for any training-related expenses.Employers cannot submit Participant Information Form (PIFs) on behalf of participants;Employers must submit an “Employer Completion Report” once all participants have completed or ceased training;Once training is completed, employers must intend to hire or continue to employ participants in B.C.;Employers and participants may be contacted during or after their participation in the program to ensure that training is contributing to the objectives and expected outcomes of the program.Employers who do not submit a Completion Report may become ineligible for future funding.

      Grant Criteria 
      The PRIIME (Programme d’aide à l’intégration en emploi des immigrants et des minorités visibles) provides a wage subsidy of up to 60% of the employee’s gross salary, capped at minimum wage, for a maximum duration of 40 weeks, with an increased subsidy of up to 70% available for individuals with disabilities. The program supports the employment integration of immigrants and visible minorities by funding onboarding, HR adaptations, and job-relevant training. Grant Value:Wage subsidy up to 60% (or 70% for people with disabilities), capped at minimum wage;Up to $2,000 for onboarding;Up to $5,000 for HR adaptations;Up to $5,000 or 80 hours for training;Up to $10,000 for general disability-related expenses.Turnaround Time: pendingEligible Employers:Must be an employer based in Québec;Can be private-sector companies, non-profits, or cooperatives;Must provide:Supervision and onboarding support;Mentorship or accompaniment during the integration period;A workplace environment conducive to skill development.Must commit to long-term employment potential for the candidate beyond the subsidy;Must not be a public organization, government entity, or political body;Must demonstrate:Inclusion and diversity efforts in HR practicesWillingness to adapt HR tools if required (e.g., evaluation processes, onboarding guides)Must agree to submit progress updates and reimbursement documentationEligible Candidates:Must be an immigrant or visible minority, legally authorized to work in Canada;Must reside in Québec;Must be seeking a first significant North American work experience in their trained field;Can be overqualified or under-employed in current job market;Must be hired for a position related to their academic or professional background;Must be employed on payroll (not contractors);Persons with disabilities are eligible and receive additional support;Candidates cannot have previously held significant, long-term work experience in their field in North America; andMust not have previously participated in a similar Emploi-Québec integration subsidy.Eligible Expenses:Onboarding & Mentorship Support:Up to $2,000 to help cover costs of coaching, supervision, or mentoring the new hireAdaptation of HR Tools & Practices:Up to $5,000 to modify internal HR practices or tools to accommodate the new hire (e.g., training materials, evaluation systems)Job-Relevant Training:Up to $5,000, or a maximum of 80 hours, for technical or professional training aligned with the job roleMay include French language training, software skills, or sector-specific upskillingDisability-Related General Costs:Up to $10,000 to support accommodations such as accessible equipment, specialized software, or other services necessary for integrationProgram Details:Maximum funding duration is 40 weeks;Positions must be full-time position (30–40 hrs/week) in the candidate's field of study or expertise;Candidates must be added to official payroll, not freelance or contractor arrangements;Placement maximum duration of 40 weeks;The employer must apply before the candidate starts employment;Job placements must have:A clearly defined training and integration plan;Performance evaluations and tracking.The program promotes:Diversity hiring;Access to meaningful, skilled employment for immigrants and minorities.Applications are assessed based on:Quality of integration plan;Suitability of the job position;Candidate's fit and support mechanisms provided.Reimbursements are conditional on:Completion of surveys and progress reports;Submission of wage records, invoices, and mentorship activity logs.Funding is not stackable with other government wage subsidies (e.g., wage subsidies from Emploi-Québec or federal Youth Employment programs).

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:This program may not be combined with other provincial or federal wage subsidies for the same position;This program is not retroactive — employers must receive approval before the candidate begins employment;Preference may be given to employers who:Demonstrate inclusive hiring practices for immigrants and visible minorities;Offer full-time roles aligned with the candidate’s field of study or expertise;Provide mentorship and structured onboarding aligned with PRIIME expectations;Commit to retaining the employee after the subsidy period ends;Adapt HR tools or training practices to support the candidate’s integration;Include accessibility measures for participants with disabilities where applicable.Process Best Practices:Employers should consult with a program officer early to confirm candidate and project eligibility;Applications must be submitted before the employment start date and include a job description, integration plan, and HR adaptation outline (if relevant);Supporting documents may include the participant’s resume, immigration or minority status confirmation, and proof of residency in Québec;Reimbursement is conditional upon submission of payroll records, onboarding documentation, and mentorship/training activity logs;If applying for disability-related costs, employers should estimate required accommodations and provide justification as part of the application.Links :Program website: click hereProgram guidelines (French only): click here

and Employers can apply without a candidate. Eligible Candidates:Be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or person with refugee protection in CanadaThose on work or student visas are ineligible;Must be enrolled in a science, technology, engineering, mathematics, arts, or business program;Must be legally able to work in Canada according to the laws and regulations of the province or territory;Studying part-time or full-time at an accredited Canadian post-secondary institution;Must provide proof of co-op placement employment;Cannot have received Digital WIL funding with the same employer previously; andNot receiving Employment Insurance (EI) benefits.Ineligible Candidates:Students registered in trade or apprenticeship programs;Students in Canada on work visas or student visas; andReturning students who have been funded by the program previously.The same student will not be eligible for multiple rounds of funding for the same type of employment with the same employer.Program Details: Placements can be part-time or full-time;Maximum 30 hours per week;Maximum duration: 1 year;The program operates on a rolling intake basis;It does not offer funding based on the semester system like the other SWPPs.Placements must be "net new," meaning that the SWPP student is incremental to the employer's "baseline" of student hires. An employer's "baseline" is the number of students they hired without SWPP support the year prior to participating in SWPP;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2022, 2023, or 2024, use the number of students hired in the year prior to that first time you accessed SWPP support;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2024, use the number of students hired in 2023;Net new baselines must be calculated each year (if you participate in SWPP every year, your net new baseline will increase accordingly).Include co-op and non-co-op students in your initial baseline calculation. Do not include high school students, recent graduates, or international students, as they are not included in the SWPP program;If a student placement crosses over the fiscal year (ie: January - April), they count toward the earlier fiscal year;If you hire a student for separate placements in different fiscal years (ie: Summer 2022, Summer 2023), you must count them in both fiscal years.Participants must be on payroll;The placement must be with an employer in the electricity sector or placement must fulfill electricity job function; A Learning Plan outlining the position must be developed by the intern and the employer before the placement starts; andOnce approved, reimbursements occur monthly.

      Grant Criteria 
      SMEs and startup companies can leverage this program to fund up to 40% (to a maximum of $25,000) of the costs of engaging one or more experts to strengthen or revise a business or commercialization plan. The aim of the program is to develop strong business or commercialization plans that demonstrate the growth potential of and attract investment for the eventual market entry of natural products or technologies (TRL 4-9), which must be biologically-based innovations that benefit people, animals and the planet.Grant Value: up to 40% of eligible project costs to a maximum of $25,000Turnaround Time: 1 monthEligible Applicants:Canadian start-ups or SMEs:Must have the potential to achieve 10MM- 15MM in annual revenue within a market-reasonable period; andSole proprietors are ineligible.Research institutes:Products or technologies must address an industry or sector challenge with significant market potential; andNo limit on the number of employees.Be a member of Canada’s Natural Product Innovation Cluster;Have a novel pre-commercial (Technology Readiness Levels(TRL) 4-9) 'natural product or technology';Defined as a biologically-based innovation that benefits people, animals, and the planet, and can be applied to a range of industries, including: Food production and value-added agriculture; Bioproducts and sustainability; Human nutrition, health, and wellness; Animal health and nutrition; and Statement of work(s) and qualifications of the selected expert(s).Program Details:Applicants may have a preferred expert(s) at the time of application or may recruit after the application is submitted;Applicants are required to contribute 60% of project costs unless also leveraging other grants;Contract with NPC will include project scope, reporting requirements, and key deliverables to be achieved;Disbursement of funds takes place through reimbursement of eligible project costs upon approval of quarterly reports; Includes a written and financial claim containing invoices and proof of payment.Annual reporting is required for 5 years following the program period.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Food Safety Program (FSP) provides funding of 70% to a maximum of $25,000 to agriculture, food processing, transportation, warehousing, and distribution businesses funding to improve food safety practices and systems. The program has 2 streams, one for on-farm organizations and one for post-farm organizations. On-farm applicants must be able to demonstrate farm status while post-farm applicants must be provincially or federally licensed to operate. The intent of the program is to enable the agrifood sector to meet existing and new food safety regulatory requirements nationally and internationally.Grant Value: Up to 70% to a maximum of $25,000Turnaround Time: 4-6 weeks after workplace submissionEligible Applicants:Be one of the following organization types:Corporation;Cooperative association;Non-profit;Society; ORIndividual.Have an active 9-digital business registration number or GST number from the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA);File business or farm income taxes in BC;Be based and operating in BC;Operate an agrifood business that produces/processes/handles food, commodities, or beverages for human consumption;Be registered with the BC Premises Identification Program if the applicant raises animals;Stream 1 - On-Farm applicants:Farmers or growers producing crops;Producers or ranchers raising animals;Packers or co-packers handling food.Stream 2 - Post-Farm applicants:Processors, transporters, warehouses, distributors, packers and importers;Processing facilities (beyond basic washing, grading and packaging);May be located on or off a farm premise and not covered by a certified on-farm food safety program.Food hubs (shared-use food and beverage processing facilities that offer food and agriculture businesses.Ineligible Applicants:Health or nutrition supplements;Pet food or food not intended for human consumption;Retail, restaurants, or other food service operations; andAquaculture and seafood production, processing, or handling businesses.Eligible Activities:Category 1- Food safety assessment:Gap assessment of food safety risks and traceability capacity:Impact of the project on improving food safety and traceability and controlling food safety risks;Impact of the project in addressing identified business needs or opportunities;Costs for an onsite gap assessment by third-party accredited auditors to identify opportunities for food safety (including traceability) improvements;Development of a food safety work plan outlining the actions needed to implement a HACCP-based food safety program, including traceability planning.Category 2- Food safety improvement:Develop traceability plans and implement written food safety programs:Equipment purchases and/or facility modification for food hazard reduction;Capped at $20,000 per applicant per term.Third-party consultation/advisory to develop or improve written food safety policies, and procedures;Incremental third-party accredited staff training - online or in-person;Validation of food safety process control measures;Baseline or incremental laboratory analysis; andThird-party audited OFFS/HACCP Certifications.Category 3 - Food Safety Certifications Completing final audits which lead to successful certification or registration in nationally or internationally recognized food safety programs;Final audit and certification costs by a third-party which lead to a certification in the following accredited, national, and internally recognized food safety certification programs are eligible:British Retail Consortium (BRC);Food Safety System Certification (FSSC) 22000;Global Red Meat Standards (GRMS);International Food Safety Standard (IFS version 6);PrimusGFS;Canada G.A.P.;Safe Quality Food (SQF 2000);Global GAP.Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) Recognized Food Safety Plans:Preventive Control Plans (PCPs) as per Safe Food for Canadians Act (SFCA);Food Safety Enhancement Program (CFIA’s FSEP);Canada Grains Council;Canadian Cattlemen’s Association Verified Beef Production;Canadian Cervid Alliance;Canadian Hatching Egg Producers: Canadian Hatching Egg Quality;Canadian Herbs, Spice and Natural Health Products Coalition;Canadian Honey Council;Canadian National Goat Federation: On-Farm Food Safety Program;Canadian On-Farm Food Safety Working Group;Canadian Pork Council: Canadian Quality Assurance Program;Canadian Sheep Federation: Food Safety Farm Practices: Canadian Verified Sheep Program;Canadian Trucking Alliance;Responsible Distribution Canada;Chicken Farmers of Canada: On-Farm Food Safety Assurance Program;Dairy Farmers of Canada: Canadian Quality Milk;Egg Farmers of Canada: Start Clean-Stay Clean;Ontario Veal Association: Veal Quality Assurance Program; andTurkey Farmers of Canada: On-Farm Food Safety Program.Note: Approval for full equipment purchase may be considered if equipment upgrades are more costly than buying new equipment.Program Details:Pre-approved applicants will work with the program's Technical Program Advisor (TPA) to develop a work plan;Project end date: within 5 months of approval;Successful applicants must complete a final report prior to receiving funds from the program;To ensure appropriate acknowledgment, all communications and marketing materials, including public announcements or social media posts, must be pre-approved by the IAF Communications Team.Details on correctly acknowledging funding can be found on the project resource hub;Materials can be submitted via the IAF Client Portal.

      Grant Criteria

The funding covers 50% of eligible training costs, up to $10,000 per business.Grant Value:50% up to $10,000 per business.Turnaround Time: pendingEligible Employers:Must be an SME (fewer than 500 full‑time employees globally);Must operate in Ontario, with a valid CRA business number;Must demonstrate a real need for training in at least one of the critical technologies: 5G (advanced networks), AI, Robotics, Quantum, Cybersecurity, or Blockchain;Must work in, or provide solutions to, at least one of the listed key sectors (Agri-food, Manufacturing, Mining and Construction);Must demonstrate how the training will benefit employees, and how that connects to the company’s long-term strategy;Should be in good financial standing with OCI;If the company has already received over $500,000 from OCI-administered programs (Excluding "Collaborate to Commercialize", "Ready 4 Market", "Life Sciences Innovation Fund", "Talent Development Program"), it will need a special approval; andMust treat technology adoption as part of the long-term roadmap (capacity to implement and sustain new Critical Technologies).Eligible Trainee(s):Must be a current employee(s) of the SME;No limit on the number of employees trained.Eligible Costs:Consultant costs must be directly related to the project, supported by invoices and proof of payment for audit purposes.Ineligible Costs:Any costs incurred outside Ontario are not eligible;Costs not directly tied to the project’s deliverables or milestones;Personal expenses;Ongoing production costs;Interest costs on capital leases;General working capital needs;Staff awards or recognition costs;Bonuses, dividends, or cash incentives;Merger and acquisition costs;Monthly parking fees;Meals, entertainment, gifts, or alcohol;Lobbying or government-relations expenses;Any taxes (e.g., sales tax, income tax, tax filing fees);Interest on invested capital, loans, bonds, or related finance charges;Infrastructure costs; andTangible capital costs such as land, buildings, or vehicles. Eligible Training:Must relate to one of the Critical Technologies;Must be delivered by an external third‑party consultant;Must help with adoption and implementation of the critical technologies within the business; andThe training program (project) must be clearly defined, with milestones and measurable outcomes. Program Details:Employers must contribute at least the same amount (1:1 funding match);The project must start and finish within 3 months;Employers pay for 100% of the training costs and are reimbursed later;All parties must follow the company’s IP rules during the training; The applicant must sign the OCI funding agreement within 30 days of being awarded; andThe grant is not fully retroactive , expenses are only recognized after the project is officially approved.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligibility Best Practices:Funding is limited and the application process is competitive. Applications that provide the greatest economic benefits and contribution based on the program objectives will be prioritized.OCI reviews application for eligibility and completeness;  where applicants can revise issues up to two times before it is withdrawn;Ensure training can be completed within 3 months timeframe;Selection Criteria : Why the business needs Critical Technology training and how it supports long-term growth;Potential economic benefits, such as new jobs, revenue, customers, or productivity gains;Capacity and leadership commitment to adopt Critical Technologies;Clear next steps and the ability to implement the plan;The plan and budget must be realistic and well-designed;The overall application must be complete, clear, and high quality.Process Best Practices:Applicants should connect with OCI through a Business Development Manager (BDM) list here, or Sector Manager; or submit the client intake form;Applicants need to request the Business Development Manager (BDM) to endorse the application at least one week before submission so the submit button becomes available;If your project fits the program, OCI will give AccessOCI login details so employers can complete the application and upload required documents;After internal approval, external experts review it and OCI sends the final decision, with feedback available through the BDM;Applicants must request any project changes through the AccessOCI Project Change Request form as early as possible and get approval before making changes, or they may lose funding.Forms:Program Website: click hereProgram Guidelines: click hereClient Intake Form: click hereProject Proposal Form: click here

Positions lasting longer than 6 months will be prioritized.Grant Value: Up to $3600 wage subsidy + up to $1000 for short-term training.Note: The maximum wage subsidy is negotiated and will be based on the hourly rate paid to the participant, the job duties, the position and hours/week.Turnaround Time:  Within a few business days (Varies depending on the speed of correspondence from applicants).Eligible Employers:In operation for at least one year; andIn good standing with WorkSafeBC.Eligible Candidate:Be a B.C. resident (living in BC as a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, recent immigrant, or a protected person);Legally entitled to work in Canada (student visa, study, or closed permit not eligible);Unemployed or under-employed (working unstable or irregular hours such as on-call work or casual labor, working for unreliable wages, and/or working for earnings that cannot support an individual or their family);Seeking long-term employment; Facing challenges to obtaining employment; andOpen work permits are accepted however student visa, study or closed work permits are not eligible.Program Details: Placements must be a minimum of 3 months;Preference will be given to placements that are 6 months and longer; The program strongly prefers placements with full-time hours (30/week), but may allow for part-time placements on a case-by-case basis;If the placement only provides part-time hours, the program will first speak with the employer and the participant to find out why the role is only part-time. The program will need to know if it is part-time because that is what the employer needs or if that is what the participants want.Placements cannot be for seasonal work; Full time students are not eligible Criteria for training subsidy:The training must be delivered by a third party;Participants must receive a certificate after completion;The training needs to match the participant's job duties; andThe training must receive prior approval by the program before the training start date.Must have identified the candidate before applying;Positions can be in person or remote;Applicants can apply for up to 2 hires; andThe program will complete monthly check-ins with the employer and hire.
