Funding is provided for a one year term, with a possible extension to a second year. The program aims to help Alberta companies scale new technologies, create high skill jobs, and de-risk the commercialization process. Grant Value: 75% of the candidates salary to a maximum of $120,000. Turnaround Time: 6-8 weeks.Eligible Employers: For-profit SME incorporated in Alberta with less than 500 full-time employees;Must have annual revenues less than $50,000,000;Must be developing innovative technologies or knowledge-based solutions;Not have more than 2 active Alberta Innovates-funded associates simultaneously;Applicants are required to have a significant portion of their physical and operational presence in Alberta;Discernible intent for operational benefits to flow primarily within Alberta; andHave up-to-date corporate filings (Alberta Innovates may perform a corporate search including bankruptcy and litigations). Eligible Associates:Cannot be a shareholder of the applicant company with over 15% of total shares;Has no more than 12 months of previous employment with the applicant company; andMust be legally entitled to work in Canada and prepared to live in Alberta for the duration of the internship.Note: Preference will be given to Associates who have formal business education (e.g. BBA, BCom, MBA, etc.).Program Details:Applicant companies should be developing mid-to-late stage technologies*; Early developmental stages will be considered on a case-by-case basis;The application must identify a phase of product development that can be completed and evaluated in 1 year;Successful applicants can reapply for an extension at the end of the first year;The funded position must focus on the commercialization of technology and include activities relating to: business development, product validation, manufacturing analysis, production planning, exploration of new markets, sales, and marketing, financial strategy, etc.;Position must be full-time (min. 30 hours per week);The applicant company must be able to pay 25% of the candidate's salary;       Grant Criteria

Placements must be part- or full-time roles in tech or tech-related roles. The intent of the program is to increase diversity in the tech sector and help B.C.-based businesses fill talent shortages.Grant Value: 100% of eligible costs to a maximum of $10,000 per placementTurnaround Time: 30 calendar daysEligible Employer:Be a B.C.-based organization;Must be either registered in B.C. or has a physical location in B.C.For-profit, non-profit organizations, post-secondaries, local/regional authorities, and Indigenous communities;Only technology businesses or technology non-profits may hire for a business role or tech role;Non-tech organizations must hire for a tech or tech-related role requiring a level of education, certification, or micro-credential to perform.Company must be actively pursuing growth through hiring, fundraising, product expansion, or new market entry and have at least one of the followingOrganizations must have minimum of 5 full time employees;Demonstrated revenue growth, user growth, or market expansion over the past 12 months; ORHave secured investment (seed, angel or VC).Eligible Candidates:A Canadian citizen or permanent resident of Canada or authorized in writing to work in Canada under the federal Immigration and Refugee Protection Act;This includes international students and co-op students.Be a B.C. resident;16 years of age or older;Be a new hire;Must not have worked for the company in the last 6 months before the placement start date.Self-identifies as one of the following underrepresented groups:Indigenous;Black or people of colour;2SLGBTQQIA+;Persons living with a visible or invisible disability;Women;Youth from care;New ImmigrantBe either a current student OR a graduate of a training/education program;Graduates:Must have completed training or education in post-secondary institutes or other recognized pathways;Must have completed the training program on or after December 1, 2022.Students:Must be enrolled at an accredited post-secondary institution in B.C. OR has completed a recognized training program that the employer feels has prepared them for effective employment;Master's, Ph.D. students are also eligible;Be able to provide acceptable proof of education.International students are also eligible.Is not a direct relative or immediate family of the employer and/or principal shareholder.Eligible Expenses:Salary or hourly wages;The employer portion of CPP and EI;WCB premiums;Employer health tax;Vacation paid out;Sick days paid out;Statutory holiday pay; andTermination pay.Once the termination of placement is reported and approved, termination pay is eligible for reimbursement up to a certain amount as defined by the B.C.’s Employment Standards Act.Ineligible Expenses:Bonuses;Commission;Overtime pay;Shift differential pay (e.g. additional pay for night shifts);Allowances (e.g. business use of personal cellphone); andExpense reimbursement.Program Details: Placements must be tech or tech-related (requiring a level of education, certification, or micro-credential to perform);With the exception of tech employers being able to hire for business roles.Part-time or full-time positions;Minimum 15 hours/week (average) for a total minimum of 240 hours during the 4-month placement;In the event hours will change throughout the work term, simply note an average number of hours when asked about hours on the application. As long as the applicant works a minimum of 15 hours a week it is eligible.Be a minimum of 4 months;Placements must have a start date between April 1, 2025, and September 1, 2025;Placements must end by December 31, 2025;Maximum 10 funded placements per employer per program year;Maximum 1 grant per participant.There will be a brief employer Progress Form midway through the placement;There will also be a satisfaction survey for the employer at the final claim stage; andUpon completing the final satisfaction survey, Innovate BC will issue the grant funds within 4-6 weeks.

      Grant Criteria

It is aimed at pre-commercial clean energy technology projects, ecosystem-building, and co-funded partnerships.Grant Value: ICE Fund provides from CAD $50,000 up to $3,000,000, depending on the project;The ICE Fund may offer less than requested, depending on budget and fit.Turnaround Time: 2 weeks.Eligible Applicants:Any Canadian legal entity can apply;Eligible Projects:Projects must be based in British Columbia (application or implementation in BC);The technology should generally be at Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 4–7 (pre-commercial stages);Maximum project duration is 5 years;Total government funding (from ICE Fund and any other government sources) must not exceed 75% of eligible project costs;Projects or parts of projects that have already received ICE Fund funding are ineligible for further funding under the same call — but a new project that meaningfully advances a previously funded one can qualify;Applicants (and consortium partners, if any) must provide at least 25% of eligible project costs (cash and/or in-kind). Eligible Expenses:Goods and services required for the project;Professional and technical costs needed to plan and conduct project activities;Cost of capital items with no residual value beyond the project;Depreciation cost of capital items with residual value beyond the project; andMore than 50% of eligible project costs must be incurred in British Columbia (At a minimum, an amount of eligible project costs equal to the ICE Fund contribution must be incurred in British Columbia).Program details:There are three funding “streams” under this call:Ecosystem: Build up the broader clean‑energy innovation ecosystem (e.g., capacity building, collaborations);Co‑funded Partnership: Projects co-funded with a partner organization to push clean‑tech toward commercialization;Project: Technology demonstration or development projects that advance toward commercialization (e.g., Bioenergy, solar, ocean tidal, geo-exchange, desalination projects).The ICE Fund can cover up to 75% of the project’s eligible costs;Applicants (or their partners) must provide at least 25% of the eligible costs, which can include “in-kind” contributions;Eligible costs are tracked (cash & in-kind) during the project;Background IP remains with its owner; project-developed IP is owned by the applicant, but ICE Fund expects reasonable commercial terms for use in BC;

      Grant Criteria 
      The program provides up to $250,000 in funding to SMEs to commercialize their products, achieve optimal market position, increase revenue and potentially expand into global markets. The program is designed to de-risk the commercialization process by providing funds and coaching to SMEs. Grant Value: Up to $250,000.Turnaround Time: 3-4 weeksEligible Applicants: For-profit organizations that are either:Incorporated;General partnerships registered in Alberta;Limited partnerships registered in Alberta; orLimited liability partnerships registered in Alberta.Be Alberta-based;Have a significant physical and corporate operational presence in Alberta;Have appropriate Alberta ownership; andDiscernible intent that operational benefits will flow primarily within the Province of Alberta;Exist as a corporate person, with up-to-date corporate filings;Be authorized to undertake the proposed project, and execute a grant with Alberta Innovates on the standard terms; Have fewer than 500 full-time employees;Have less than $50,000,000 in annual gross revenue; andMust be in good standing with Alberta Innovates or its subsidiaries (InnoTech Alberta, C-FER Technologies).Eligible Partners: Exist as a corporate person, with up-to-date corporate filings; Be authorized to undertake the proposed project; Demonstrate that the relationship between the Applicant and Partner/ Strategic Partner/ Service Provider/ Collaborator does not create a conflict of interest; Be at arm's length from the Applicant;Must not have a conflict of interest with the applicant.Provide a letter indicating the Partner's/ Service Provider's/ Collaborator's intention to participate in the Project at the time of application; Have the financial capability to purchase or enter into a distribution agreement of the product upon Project completion of a demonstration;Show tangible resources committed to the Project; andMust be in good standing with Alberta Innovates or its subsidiaries (InnoTech Alberta, C-FER Technologies).Eligible Projects: Show that the product is a viable technology at Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 6 to 8; Be stepped with critical "go/no go" milestones with measurable target outcomes; Be completed within an 18-month term; Have the participation of at least 1 International Project Partner(s); Outline the financial contribution required by Applicant; and/or Comply with other criteria that Alberta Innovates may develop from time to time. Eligible Expenses:Labour costs, directly related to the project;Costs of materials;Acquisitions of property;Acquisitions of software or information databases;Direct operating costs;Technology transfer to the Applicant from an Alberta public sector research organization;Travel expenses if they are a necessary part of accomplishing the project and also have to be pre-approved by Alberta Innovates; andAny other expense pre-approved by Alberta Innovates in writing.Ineligible Expenses: Any cost incurred prior to the project start date;Any costs which have been or will be funded by other government funding;Transactions between related persons; Provisions for contingencies;Allowance for interest of debt;Losses on investments, bad debts and expenses for collection charges;Losses on other projects or activities outside the Alberta Portion of the Project;Fines and penalties;Unreasonable compensation for Project labour; Costs for professional training and development;costs related to land and buildings;depreciation and amortization charges;Advertising costs;Costs associated with applying for government grants and programs;Costs of internships or support for students of knowledge institutions;Basic professional services, fees and disbursements, such as ongoing routine accounting, tac and legal business requirements; Routine testing and maintenance; Costs relating to meals, entertainment, hospitality, alcohol and gifts;Federal and provincial income taxes, goods and services taxes; and Any other costs deemed ineligible by Alberta Innovates.Program Details: Funding is provided to support SMEs to find and enter a partnership with an "International Project Partner" for further product development or to pilot the technical and business merits of their product with the goal to prove the product value, and advance commercialization;Objectives of the program include: Have applicants build a relationship with an International Project Partner for collaborative development and testing, leveraging industry knowledge or access to new distribution channels;Establish an early to late-stage pilot;Form long-term business partnerships that extend market access;Provide access to new capital sources;Increased global competitiveness.The support of a technology development advisor is required for the ITP. They provide guidance and coaching and assess the Applicant's ITP readiness;Project Activities may include:Developing and testing technology;Piloting in an operational or test environment to move towards commercialization.Alberta Innovates will match the applicant's contributions for eligible project costs to a maximum investment of $250,000; andThe applicant's matching funds must be in the form of 50% cash and 50% in-kind contributions;E.g. Alberta Innovates investment of $250,000, Alberta SME $250,000 (50% cash and 50% In-Kind) and International project partner $250,000 (50% cash and 50% In-Kind).

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices: This program is not retroactive;This program can be stacked with other government funding however it won't cover any expense funded by another program;SME and International project partners must contribute equal funding to the project. Process Best Practices:Funding will be disbursed based on milestones being met.Forms: Program Webpage: click hereProgram Guidelines: click hereApplication Portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Investment in Forest Industry Transformation (IFIT) program will provide 50% up to $10 million in non-repayable funding to help improve the environmental performance of the forest sector by supporting demonstration and adoption projects that  contribute to the decarbonization of industrial processes, as well as the efficient use of resources that generates more value from the same amount of wood.Grant Value: Stream 1 Capital Investment Projects: 50% of eligible project costs Up to $10 million;Stream 2 Studies: 50% of eligible project costs min $100,000 to a max of $1 million.Turnaround Time: pendingEligible Applicants: Stream 1:For-profit companies;Located in Canada;Must produce either forest products in an existing forest product facility or are/will be new entrants in the forest sector for the purpose of the project;Clusters, joint ventures and consortiums are welcome to apply as long as the lead applicant is a for-profit.Stream 2: For-profit companies;Located in Canada;Must produce either forest products in an existing forest product facility or are/will be new entrants in the forest sector for the purpose of the project;Clusters, joint ventures and consortiums are welcome to apply; ORnot-for profits and industry associations.Eligible Projects:Stream 1: Be primarily based on wood fibre OR integrated within new or existing industrial
processes in the forest sector;Represent an innovative advancement of a technology or process improvement
to ensure the competitiveness of operations in Canada’s forest sector; andDemonstrate a first-in-kind innovation or an early adoption of technology that
requires further de-risking in a range of conditions before widespread
implementation.Stream 2:Advance a concept, technology, process, or product primarily based on wood fibre
OR integrated within new or existing industrial processes in the forest sector;Investigate the feasibility and/or advance a concept within the targeted innovation
categories described in the following section; andDisseminate project learnings beyond the applicant’s corporate structure.Eligible Expenses: Cost of salaries and benefits;Overhead expenditures provided they are directly related and essential to the
conduct of the project, up to 1.5% of eligible expenditures;Professional and technical services, such as, but not limited to research,
consulting, engineering, trades, and laboratory services;Travel expenses, including transportation, accommodation, and meals (based on
National Joint Council rates);Training;Publication, printing, and other media services;Data collection services, including processing, analysis, and management;Licence fees and permits;Capital expenses;Retrofitting and upgrading of existing capital;Material and supplies;Meeting hospitality and space rental;Costs associated with environmental assessments; andTechnical audits associated with project activities.Program Details:The Program will focus on the following innovation categories:Advanced BioMaterials and Biochemicals;Pulp and Paper Diversification;Next Generation Building Projects;Advanced Biofuels;Process Efficiency and Decarbonization; andImproved Fibre Utilization.Any costs associated with the production or exports of softwood lumber products are ineligible under this program; andInitially EOI must be submitted, if successful will be invited to submit full project proposal.

      Grant Criteria 
      This program puts teams of BCIT students to work on IT projects of various sizes and scopes. Employers can submit projects throughout the year. If selected, they will be assigned a team of computing science students who will dedicate 400 hours of work to their project. Any software or IT project that is not too time-sensitive and that can provide a good learning opportunity for students is suitable for the program. Non-profits and charities can participate for free; for-profit companies are required to contribute a $500 participation fee. The goal of the program is to provide work experience for students and to connect employers to up-and-coming talent. Grant Value: The grant value is an estimate based on approximately 400 hours of work by computing science students.Turnaround Time: 4-7 weeksEligible Applicants:For-profit, not-for-profit, and charitable organizations of any size are eligible to submit a project;Applicants whose projects are selected must be available on a weekly basis during the project term to provide feedback and guidance to the students;Must endeavour to attend the end-of-term project presentation, and give an evaluation of the students' performance; andIf applicable, negotiate an intellectual property and/or non-disclosure agreement with the student team (templates available from BCIT).Eligible Projects:Project scope: 400 hours;Participation fee: $500;The participation fee is waived for non-profit employers.Any IT or software project that can provide learning opportunities to computing science students;Examples of suitable projects in each of the program's focus areas are:Computing Systems Technology:Web application using a framework such as React or Angular and a programming language such as Node js, Python, Java, PHP, or GO;Mobile application for Android or iOS using a framework such as Flutter;Scalable Cloud Application with public cloud providers such as AWS or Azure;Web or Mobile game.Computer Information Technology:Projects involving DevOps, Scripting, Cloud Integration, Machine Learning, and/or Web Development.Systems Software Developer:Web or Mobile projects with a database backend.Full Stack Web Development:Web development projects. Projects that are time-sensitive or mission-critical are not suitable for the program, since students are still in training;Applicants may submit projects throughout the year, but the cut-off for consideration for each semester is as follows:Fall semester: submit by August 11;Winter semester: submit by December 1;Spring semester: submit by March 23.Projects received after the deadlines will be saved for the next term;Large projects may be divided into phases for students to work on over several consecutive terms; andEmployers seeking to hire a student intern can contact BCIT about adding an internship to the project. Note: If your project includes a significant R&D component, contact BCIT to explore the possibility of funding the project through an NSERC Alliance Grant.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices: It is possible to combine this program with other sources of funding for a project;Since the program does not issue funds directly to the employer, it cannot be used retroactively to fund student work that has already taken place;Process Best Practices: Projects are selected by student teams. To increase the likelihood of being selected, BCIT recommends that employers consider the following when drafting their proposal:Use laymen's terms when describing the project;Add details and/or examples of what you're looking for (ie: list desired components, features, and functions);Clarify the scope of the project as much as possible, and/or state your willingness to divide the project into smaller parts as required once the students begin working;Specify the technologies to be used, or suggest options;Indicate that you have staff with the appropriate domain and technical knowledge to support the students. Forms:Program website: click hereProgram FAQ: click hereApplication form: click here

The intent of the program is to increase diversity in the tech sector and help B.C.-based businesses fill talent shortages.Grant Value: 100% of eligible costs to a maximum of $10,000 per placementTurnaround Time: 30 calendar daysEligible Employer:Be a B.C.-based organization;Must be either registered in B.C. or has a physical location in B.C.For-profit, non-profit organizations, post-secondaries, local/regional authorities, and Indigenous communities;Only technology businesses or technology non-profits may hire for a business role or tech role;Non-tech organizations must hire for a tech or tech-related role requiring a level of education, certification, or micro-credential to perform.Company must be actively pursuing growth through hiring, fundraising, product expansion, or new market entry and have at least one of the followingOrganizations must have minimum of 5 full time employees;Demonstrated revenue growth, user growth, or market expansion over the past 12 months; ORHave secured investment (seed, angel or VC).Eligible Candidates:A Canadian citizen or permanent resident of Canada or authorized in writing to work in Canada under the federal Immigration and Refugee Protection Act;This includes international students and co-op students.Be a B.C. resident;16 years of age or older;Be a new hire;Must not have worked for the company in the last 6 months before the placement start date.Self-identifies as one of the following underrepresented groups:Indigenous;Black or people of colour;2SLGBTQQIA+;Persons living with a visible or invisible disability;Women;Youth from care;New ImmigrantBe either a current student OR a graduate of a training/education program;Graduates:Must have completed training or education in post-secondary institutes or other recognized pathways;Must have completed the training program on or after December 1, 2022.Students:Must be enrolled at an accredited post-secondary institution in B.C.       Grant Criteria 
      The ICE Fund -Call for Innovation and Partnerhsips is a BC provincial fund to support clean energy innovations aligned with economic, environmental, and greenhouse-gas (GHG) reduction goals. It is aimed at pre-commercial clean energy technology projects, ecosystem-building, and co-funded partnerships.Grant Value: ICE Fund provides from CAD $50,000 up to $3,000,000, depending on the project;The ICE Fund may offer less than requested, depending on budget and fit.Turnaround Time: 2 weeks.Eligible Applicants:Any Canadian legal entity can apply;Eligible Projects:Projects must be based in British Columbia (application or implementation in BC);The technology should generally be at Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 4–7 (pre-commercial stages);Maximum project duration is 5 years;Total government funding (from ICE Fund and any other government sources) must not exceed 75% of eligible project costs;Projects or parts of projects that have already received ICE Fund funding are ineligible for further funding under the same call — but a new project that meaningfully advances a previously funded one can qualify;Applicants (and consortium partners, if any) must provide at least 25% of eligible project costs (cash and/or in-kind). Eligible Expenses:Goods and services required for the project;Professional and technical costs needed to plan and conduct project activities;Cost of capital items with no residual value beyond the project;Depreciation cost of capital items with residual value beyond the project;       Grant Criteria 
      The program provides up to $250,000 in funding to SMEs to commercialize their products, achieve optimal market position, increase revenue and potentially expand into global markets. The program is designed to de-risk the commercialization process by providing funds and coaching to SMEs. Grant Value: Up to $250,000.Turnaround Time: 3-4 weeksEligible Applicants: For-profit organizations that are either:Incorporated;General partnerships registered in Alberta;Limited partnerships registered in Alberta; orLimited liability partnerships registered in Alberta.Be Alberta-based;Have a significant physical and corporate operational presence in Alberta;Have appropriate Alberta ownership; andDiscernible intent that operational benefits will flow primarily within the Province of Alberta;Exist as a corporate person, with up-to-date corporate filings;Be authorized to undertake the proposed project, and execute a grant with Alberta Innovates on the standard terms; Have fewer than 500 full-time employees;Have less than $50,000,000 in annual gross revenue; andMust be in good standing with Alberta Innovates or its subsidiaries (InnoTech Alberta, C-FER Technologies).Eligible Partners: Exist as a corporate person, with up-to-date corporate filings; Be authorized to undertake the proposed project; Demonstrate that the relationship between the Applicant and Partner/ Strategic Partner/ Service Provider/ Collaborator does not create a conflict of interest; Be at arm's length from the Applicant;Must not have a conflict of interest with the applicant.Provide a letter indicating the Partner's/ Service Provider's/ Collaborator's intention to participate in the Project at the time of application; Have the financial capability to purchase or enter into a distribution agreement of the product upon Project completion of a demonstration;Show tangible resources committed to the Project; andMust be in good standing with Alberta Innovates or its subsidiaries (InnoTech Alberta, C-FER Technologies).Eligible Projects: Show that the product is a viable technology at Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 6 to 8; Be stepped with critical "go/no go" milestones with measurable target outcomes; Be completed within an 18-month term; Have the participation of at least 1 International Project Partner(s); Outline the financial contribution required by Applicant; and/or Comply with other criteria that Alberta Innovates may develop from time to time. Eligible Expenses:Labour costs, directly related to the project;Costs of materials;Acquisitions of property;Acquisitions of software or information databases;Direct operating costs;Technology transfer to the Applicant from an Alberta public sector research organization;Travel expenses if they are a necessary part of accomplishing the project and also have to be pre-approved by Alberta Innovates; andAny other expense pre-approved by Alberta Innovates in writing.Ineligible Expenses: Any cost incurred prior to the project start date;Any costs which have been or will be funded by other government funding;Transactions between related persons; Provisions for contingencies;Allowance for interest of debt;Losses on investments, bad debts and expenses for collection charges;Losses on other projects or activities outside the Alberta Portion of the Project;Fines and penalties;Unreasonable compensation for Project labour; Costs for professional training and development;costs related to land and buildings;depreciation and amortization charges;Advertising costs;Costs associated with applying for government grants and programs;Costs of internships or support for students of knowledge institutions;Basic professional services, fees and disbursements, such as ongoing routine accounting, tac and legal business requirements; Routine testing and maintenance; Costs relating to meals, entertainment, hospitality, alcohol and gifts;Federal and provincial income taxes, goods and services taxes; and Any other costs deemed ineligible by Alberta Innovates.Program Details: Funding is provided to support SMEs to find and enter a partnership with an "International Project Partner" for further product development or to pilot the technical and business merits of their product with the goal to prove the product value, and advance commercialization;Objectives of the program include: Have applicants build a relationship with an International Project Partner for collaborative development and testing, leveraging industry knowledge or access to new distribution channels;Establish an early to late-stage pilot;Form long-term business partnerships that extend market access;Provide access to new capital sources;Increased global competitiveness.The support of a technology development advisor is required for the ITP. They provide guidance and coaching and assess the Applicant's ITP readiness;Project Activities may include:Developing and testing technology;Piloting in an operational or test environment to move towards commercialization.Alberta Innovates will match the applicant's contributions for eligible project costs to a maximum investment of $250,000; andThe applicant's matching funds must be in the form of 50% cash and 50% in-kind contributions;E.g. Alberta Innovates investment of $250,000, Alberta SME $250,000 (50% cash and 50% In-Kind) and International project partner $250,000 (50% cash and 50% In-Kind).

        January 7, 2026As part of its 2026 renewal, the IFIT program will support projects that advance forest bioproducts, advanced biofuels, and low-carbon building materials.The funding cap for the capital investment stream has increased to up to $20 million, doubling the previous $10 million limit.
      

      Grant Criteria 
      The Investment in Forest Industry Transformation (IFIT) program will provide 50% up to $10 million in non-repayable funding to help improve the environmental performance of the forest sector by supporting demonstration and adoption projects that  contribute to the decarbonization of industrial processes, as well as the efficient use of resources that generates more value from the same amount of wood.Grant Value: Stream 1 Capital Investment Projects: 50% of eligible project costs Up to $10 million;Stream 2 Studies: 50% of eligible project costs min $100,000 to a max of $1 million.Turnaround Time: pendingEligible Applicants: Stream 1:For-profit companies;Located in Canada;Must produce either forest products in an existing forest product facility or are/will be new entrants in the forest sector for the purpose of the project;Clusters, joint ventures and consortiums are welcome to apply as long as the lead applicant is a for-profit.Stream 2: For-profit companies;Located in Canada;Must produce either forest products in an existing forest product facility or are/will be new entrants in the forest sector for the purpose of the project;Clusters, joint ventures and consortiums are welcome to apply; ORnot-for profits and industry associations.Eligible Projects:Stream 1: Be primarily based on wood fibre OR integrated within new or existing industrial
processes in the forest sector;Represent an innovative advancement of a technology or process improvement
to ensure the competitiveness of operations in Canada’s forest sector; andDemonstrate a first-in-kind innovation or an early adoption of technology that
requires further de-risking in a range of conditions before widespread
implementation.Stream 2:Advance a concept, technology, process, or product primarily based on wood fibre
OR integrated within new or existing industrial processes in the forest sector;Investigate the feasibility and/or advance a concept within the targeted innovation
categories described in the following section; andDisseminate project learnings beyond the applicant’s corporate structure.Eligible Expenses: Cost of salaries and benefits;Overhead expenditures provided they are directly related and essential to the
conduct of the project, up to 1.5% of eligible expenditures;Professional and technical services, such as, but not limited to research,
consulting, engineering, trades, and laboratory services;Travel expenses, including transportation, accommodation, and meals (based on
National Joint Council rates);Training;Publication, printing, and other media services;Data collection services, including processing, analysis, and management;Licence fees and permits;Capital expenses;Retrofitting and upgrading of existing capital;Material and supplies;Meeting hospitality and space rental;Costs associated with environmental assessments; andTechnical audits associated with project activities.Program Details:The Program will focus on the following innovation categories:Advanced BioMaterials and Biochemicals;Pulp and Paper Diversification;Next Generation Building Projects;Advanced Biofuels;Process Efficiency and Decarbonization; andImproved Fibre Utilization.Any costs associated with the production or exports of softwood lumber products are ineligible under this program; andInitially EOI must be submitted, if successful will be invited to submit full project proposal.

      Grant Criteria 
      This stream of the Invest North Program offers multiple funding options to supply a grant contribution of up to 20% of total eligible costs to a maximum of $400,000 for businesses to grow their existing operations in Northern Ontario. This contribution may also be accompanied or replaced by a repayable contribution in the form of a term loan. The goal of this program is to support projects that will result in full-time job creation or retention, and benefit the overall economic development of the region.Grant Value: 20% of costs up to $400,000Turnaround Time: 6 weeksEligible Applicants:Businesses based anywhere in Ontario who are seeking to expand existing operations in Northern Ontario; andMinimum 1 year of incorporation.Ineligible Applicants:Retail and consumer service businesses that primarily earn revenue by providing products and services directly to individuals;Accommodation & food service businesses and related business activities; andBusinesses that are primarily involved in wholesale activities.Eligible Expenses:Capital construction;Leasehold improvements;New or used equipment including capital leases;Land servicing costs;Information & communications technology (ICT) investments;Marketing for new products and business initiatives (limited to a maximum of 20% of all other eligible project costs, or $75,000, whichever is less); andTraining costs incurred with third parties (limited to a maximum of 20% of all other eligible project costs).Ineligible Expenses:They include but are not limited to the following projects, costs, and activities (some exceptions may be made where projects address a priority economic need in Northern Ontario):Ongoing operating costs including maintenance;In-kind contributions;Restructuring or refinancing of existing business operations;Business plans, strategic plans, feasibility studies, etc.;Assets acquired through operating leases;Research and development;Land purchase/lease;Rolling stock (e.g. cars, trucks & boats and motors);Project management, consulting, and administration costs;Mineral exploration, mine development, and milling operations;Working capital;Cost of inventory;Cellular and internet service projects;Capital projects or leasehold improvements to residential or personal properties;Acquisitions and buy-outs of existing businesses; andElectricity generation projects.Program Details:Funding can be provided through three options:A conditional contribution only of up to 20% of total eligible costs to a maximum of $400,000.A conditional contribution of up to 20% of total eligible costs to a maximum of $400,000, plus a term loan of up to 30% of total eligible costs to a maximum of $600,000.A term loan only of up to 50% of total eligible costs to a maximum of $1,000,000.The applicant is expected to secure the balance of funding or financing necessary to implement the project;The applicant may be required to reimburse NOHFC if assets financed by NOHFC are sold after project completion;The combined federal and provincial government funding (including any contribution from NOHFC) may not exceed 50% of eligible project costs for private sector projects;Agencies that are arms-length from government, with an independent Board of Directors, are not considered “government funding.”If the funding offer involves a secured loan over $100,000, approved applicants are required to retain the services of a lawyer; andApplications will be evaluated in 4 competitive rounds on the following submission deadlines for a detailed business plan:Round 1: April 30;Round 2: July 31;Round 3: October 31; andRound 4: January 31.Evaluation Criteria:Factors that will be considered during evaluation of applications will include but are not limited to:Job creation;Level of investment from other sources to be secured by the applicant;Strength of the applicant’s detailed business plan;Does not unreasonably impact existing Northern Ontario businesses;Net economic benefits for Northern Ontario; andOther business activities that will result in an economic development advantage for Northern Ontario.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Applicants can only submit one application to the Grow stream at a time;Tourism businesses that provide accommodation services and operate as a tourist destination for local, regional and international visitors for extended stays (e.g., remote outfitter, family vacation resort) are potentially eligible;Businesses that only serve the overnight travelling public are considered ineligible (e.g. hotels and motels).Eligible activities incurred can be retroactive to the date of submitting a complete application; andLimited funding is available. Not all projects meeting the criteria will necessarily receive funding;Process Best Practices:To apply, a screening form is first filled out on the website, which will then prompt the applicant to prepare a robust business case with documentation on current financial and business operations;Recommended to have bridge funding between start of project and reimbursement payments, which are negotiated during project approval.Forms:Program website: click here

andResearch and development services provided by public sector partners.Demonstration and commercialization activities:Direct internal technical labour costs performed in Northern Ontario;Building or renovation costs specifically related to the commercialization of the new technology;Prototype demonstration costs (i.e., engineering and design services and equipment purchases, fabrication and installation costs);Material costs;Product certification costs;Research and development services provided by public sector partners; andBe able to demonstrate that the technology has been tested and fully validated.Evaluation Criteria:Factors that will be considered during the evaluation of applications will include but are not limited to:Innovation meets the NOHFC’s definition of Innovation;Strength of the project’s detailed business plan;Net economic benefits for Northern Ontario;Demonstrated market need and demand;Management capacity;Business’ financial position;Supply chain impacts; and"Hobby businesses" where the owner intends to work at the business full-time and transition to a full-time sustainable and commercially viable business.Ineligible Applicants:Retail and consumer service businesses that primarily earn revenue by providing products and services directly to individuals;Accommodation & food service businesses and related business activities; andBusinesses that are primarily involved in wholesale activities.Eligible Expenses:Capital construction;Leasehold improvements;New or used equipment including capital leases;Land servicing costs;Information & communications technology (ICT) investments;Marketing for new products and business initiatives (limited to a maximum of 20% of all other eligible project costs, or $75,000, whichever is less); andTraining costs incurred with third parties (limited to a maximum of 20% of all other eligible project costs).Ineligible Expenses:They include but are not limited to the following projects, costs, and activities (some exceptions may be made where projects address a priority economic need in Northern Ontario):Ongoing operating costs including maintenance;In-kind contributions;Restructuring or refinancing of existing business operations;Business plans, strategic plans, feasibility studies, etc.;Assets acquired through operating leases;Research and development;Land purchase/lease;Rolling stock (e.g. cars, trucks & boats and motors);Project management, consulting, and administration costs;Mineral exploration, mine development, and milling operations;Working capital;Cost of inventory;Cellular and internet service projects;Capital projects or leasehold improvements to residential or personal properties;Acquisitions and buy-outs of existing businesses; andElectricity generation projects.Program Details:A new business will be expected to operate on a full-time basis;The entrepreneur/owner must work at the business on a full-time basis;Applicant is expected to secure the balance of funding or financing necessary to implement the project;They are required to contribute (from their own resources) an amount equal to at least 15% of total eligible project costs towards the project.Applicant may be required to reimburse NOHFC if assets financed by NOHFC are sold after project completion;They must retain the assets acquired with program funding for 3 years, or receive prior approval to dispose or move assets outside of Northern Ontario.Combined federal and provincial government funding (including any contribution from NOHFC) may not exceed 50% of eligible project costs for private sector projects;Agencies that are arms-length from government, with an independent Board of Directors, are not considered “government funding.”Evaluation Criteria:Factors that will be considered during evaluation of applications will include but are not limited to:Job creation;Level of investment from other sources to be secured by the applicant;Strength of the applicant’s detailed business plan;Does not unreasonably impact existing Northern Ontario businesses;Net economic benefits for Northern Ontario; andOther business activities that will result in an economic development advantage for Northern Ontario.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Funding from this program may be combined with federal and provincial government funding. However, funding may not exceed 50% of eligible project costs;Tourism businesses that provide accommodation services and operate as a tourist destination for local, regional and international visitors for extended stays (e.g., remote outfitter, family vacation resort) are potentially eligible;Businesses that only serve the overnight travelling public are considered ineligible (e.g. hotels and motels).Process Best Practices:To apply, a screening form is first filled out on the website, which will then prompt the applicant to prepare a robust business case with documentation on current financial and business operations;Recommended to have bridge funding between start of project and reimbursement payments, which are negotiated during project approval.Forms:Program website: click hereApplication form: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This provincial program offers employers a maximum of $13,440 wage subsidy to create new positions. Positions with 52 weeks of continuous employment will receive a bonus of $2,000 to the employer and $1,000 to the employee. This program is intended to promote sustainable long-term employment or seasonable employment by offsetting the costs associated with training and managing new employees.Grant Value: a maximum of 80% up to $13,440 wage subsidy + $2,000 completion bonusTurnaround Time: 20 daysEligible Employers:Be in Newfoundland and Labrador;For-profit and non-profit employers that are incorporated or sole proprietorships;Maintains a Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) business number; andBe in good standing with the Registry of Companies and Deeds.Note: Federal and provincial government departments, crown agencies and corporations, boards and commissions, municipalities, and political parties are ineligible for this program.Eligible Candidates:Be residents of Newfoundland and Labrador;Be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or person granted refugee status in Canada; ORBe an international graduate of Memorial University of College of the North Atlantic with a Post-Graduate Work Permit and a resident of the province;Be a recent post-secondary graduate;Be unemployed or underemployed (averages less than 20 hours per week or in a field unrelated to their training);Is not receiving any federal or provincial government pension, Workplace NL benefits or other benefits prescribed by the Minister.Note: Individuals on a temporary work permit are ineligible.Ineligible Candidates:Individuals on temporary work permits;Members of the immediate family of the employer; andUnless in exceptional circumstances.Students in work-term or co-op as they are considered full-time students.Program Details:2 streams:JobsNL 42 - provides a 28-week wage subsidy in a 42-week period of employment:1st 14 week period: 60% subsidy up to $12/hour;2nd 14 week period: 0% subsidy;3rd 14 week period: 80% subsidy up to $12/hour; andCompletion bonus of $2,000 to the employer and $1,000 to the participant for a total of 52 weeks of continuous employment.JobsNL 28 - provides a subsidy in a 10-28 week period of employment:60% subsidy up to $12/hour; andCompletion bonus of $2,000 to the employer and $1,000 to the participant for a total of 38 weeks of continuous employment.Completion bonuses do not apply to seasonal or short-term employment (28 weeks or less);Hours per week: 30-40;Part-time (few than 30 hours/week) may be considered for participants with disabilities.Separate applications are required for each participant; andUpon approval, the participant must be hired within 30 business days, and the employer must submit the consent form.Eligible Positions:Be created in addition to existing staff;Be in compliance with provincial employment standards legislation;Not be part of the regular staff or be a result of lay-offs, paternal/maternity leave replacements;Not be filled by promoting or reassigning an existing employee;Not be vacant as a result of labour stoppage or labour-management dispute;Not be paid solely by commission or output; andNot be a position the employer would have created in the absence of this subsidy.

Master's, Ph.D.) are also eligible.Be legally entitled to work in Canada in accordance with provincial or territorial legislation and regulations.Program Details:Work placements are fully remote;Maximum duration per participant per project: 80 hours;No maximum number of participants employers can hire per project;I.e. employers can have a group of participants working on the same projectNo maximum number of projects employers can post on the Riipen job board;I.e. employers can have multiple simultaneous projectsProjects posted by employers must be distinct;Participants cannot apply to the same project once the placement concludes;Riipen will pay participants directly after placement concludes;Participants will only receive the stipend if the hours committed are completed;Employment contracts will not be required for this program.

      Grant Criteria 
      This federal program offers wage subsidies to hire current post-secondary students part-time or full-time. Undergraduate students and graduate students are eligible to apply. Employers must be willing to provide a quality learning experience to a student and have the financial capacity to pay the student for the duration of the placement in full. Students from under-represented groups are eligible for a 70% subsidy up to a maximum of $7000, while others will be eligible for 50% subsidy up to a maximum of $5000. Grant Value:50% of wages up to a maximum of $5000; or 70% of wages up to a maximum of $7000 for students from any of the following under-represented groups:Women in STEM;Indigenous persons;Newcomers to Canada;Persons with disabilities;Visible minorities; andFirst-year students.Turnaround time: 20-25 business daysEligible Employer:Registered for-profit businesses;Not-for-profit organizations;Must have the capacity (financially and otherwise) to hire and supervise a student.Ineligible Employer:Post-secondary institutions, hospitals, and long-term care facilities;Non-secular institutions; Federal, provincial, territorial and municipal governments; andFinancial institutions: click here to see the list of ineligible financial sector employers.Eligible Candidates:Must be a current student enrolled (full-time or part-time) in a recognized Canadian post-secondary institution;Graduate students (ie. Master's and  Doctoral students) are also eligible.Undertaking the work opportunity as a work-integrated learning experience in connection with a course, degree, certificate, or diploma;Mentorships, co-ops, internships, practicums, and applied research projects are all considered eligible work-integrated learning experiences;The WIL component may be optional or required by the student's program. It may be for credit or not for credit;Magnet will send a letter template to pre-approved applicants. The student can use the template to request the required letter from a representative of their post-secondary institution, such as the Office of the Registrar, Career and Co-op Office, or Dean's office;For non co-op placements the letter must be signed by the Associate Dean of the relevant faculty or Program Director if applicable.Must be Canadian citizens, Permanent Residents, or persons with refugee protection legally entitled to work in their placement province; andInternational students are not eligible for the subsidy. Note: Only when the placement is considered "articling" would this be deemed ineligible (ie. student working towards their CPA, OBA, realtor license, etc)Program Details: Full-time or part-time positions;No maximum or minimum duration;Any industry and focus are accepted;Wage subsidy will apply to gross wages between;Winter Semester 2025 (January 1 - March 31, 2024) - CLOSED.Summer Semester 2025 (May 1 to August 31, 2025) - CLOSEDFall Semester 2025 (September 1 - December 31, 2025) - Opening August 1, 2025.Placements must be "net new," meaning that the SWPP student is incremental to the employer's "baseline" of student hires. An employer's "baseline" is the number of students they hired without SWPP support the year prior to participating in SWPP;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2022, 2023, or 2024, use the number of students hired in the year prior to that first time you accessed SWPP support;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2024, use the number of students hired in 2023;Net new baselines must be calculated each year (if you participate in SWPP every year, your net new baseline will increase accordingly).Include co-op and non-co-op students in your initial baseline calculation. Do not include high school students, recent graduates, or international students, as they are not included in the SWPP program;If a student placement crosses over the fiscal year (ie: January - April), they count toward the earlier fiscal year;If you hire a student for separate placements in different fiscal years (ie: Summer 2022, Summer 2023), you must count them in both fiscal years.Back-to-back placements are eligible only if the participant has 2 separate co-op requirements from their post-secondary institution;The employer must provide on-the-job supervision; The employer must ensure student hires are placed on payroll and are not contractors;Work-integrated learning must be in the participant's study plan and span over the duration of the placement;Employers will have the flexibility to postpone placement start dates to avoid rescinding placements; Employers will be able to apply for funding before they finalize their selection of students to hire; andThe program provides 1 reimbursement payment at the end of the placement.Note: Placements can begin earlier and end later than the funded semester, however only the placement between the semester start dates and end dates are eligible for funding.

      Best Practices & Forms

      Grant Type
      Business Assessments, Planning & Coaching, Capital Costs
    
    
      Grant Amount
      $10,000,000
    
    
      Regions
      British Columbia
    
    
      Industries
      Engineering, Environmental - Green Technologies, Food Processing, Forestry , Manufacturing, Tech - Biotechnology
    
    
      Program provided by
      The Government of B.C.
     

    
      Deadline
      
        

          Open until filled
      
    
    
  





    
      




  
      
        Recently Changed 
        June 28, 2024New proposals are due August 15, 2024 at 4pm PST;If a project has been invited to submit a detailed application, the deadline to submit is November 15, 2024 at 4pm PST.
      

      Grant Criteria 
      The BC Manufacturing Job Fund provides funding of up to $10 million to manufacturers to conduct business/project planning as well as invest in new manufacturing infrastructure, technology, and processes. The program has 2 funding streams: the Project Readiness stream and the Capital Investment stream.  The intent of the program is to boost productivity, increase competitiveness and support clean and inclusive growth.Grant Value:Project Readiness stream: Up to 50% of eligible costs to a maximum of $50,000Capital Investment stream: Average of 20% of eligible costs to a maximum of $10,000,000Turnaround Time: 4 weeks after the initial proposalEligible Applicants:Registered for-profit manufacturing businesses in BC;Have established operations (at a proposed project location or elsewhere);Have an established employee base;Be in a viable financial position.Have a business plan and/or financial records demonstrating the ability to pay off short-term debts;Not in foreclosure or for sale;Paid taxes in the last fiscal year.Eligible Projects:Be located in B.C.;Contribute to long-term regional economic growth, sustainability, and/or diversity;Be financially viable and leverage market demand;Create, maintain, or diversify job opportunities for local workers;Have a high degree of readiness and bring direct benefits to communities; andDemonstrate alignment with program goals (see Best Practices section below).Eligible Expenses:Stream 1 - must be related to business and project planning to prepare for investment:Business plans;Market assessments;Operational plans;Financial plans and costing;Risk analyses; andOperational technical assessments.Stream 2 - must be essential to project delivery:Capital expenditures including equipment, machinery, technology, and construction materials;Wage or contract costs for net new and project-specific labour;Material transportation costs;Installation and implementation costs; andOther time-limited costs directly related to project implementation.Ineligible Expenses:Costs unrelated to the project;Operating costs (core staff salaries, bonuses, repayment loans, fines/penalties, etc.);Acquisition of land and existing buildings;With the exception of First Nations/Indigenous-owned enterprises acquiring or buying into existing manufacturing operations).Early research, concept development, scoping, prototyping, and feasibility studies (Technology Readiness Level 1-7); andCosts eligible for tax rebates and other rebates.Program Details:Stream 1 - Project Readiness StreamFocus on final-stage business, project planning, and operational & technical assessments;Early-stage R&D, concept development, and scoping are not eligible; andShould ideally begin the project within 3 months of funding approval.Stream 2 - Capital Investment StreamFocus on investing in new or renovated manufacturing equipment, infrastructure, technology, and processes;Projects must be initiated within 1 year of project approval; andApplicants in this stream will be asked to submit project documentation that outlines the project budget, and other potential and secured funding sources, and demonstrates project viability.Successful recipients of Stream 1 may apply for Stream 2 when ready;Receipt of Stream 1 funding does not guarantee approval through Stream 2.Process and timelines:Submit high-level proposal - 4-week turnaroundSubmit a detailed application - turnaround time will vary depending on the funding stream and complexity of the projectFunding Decision - within 12 weeks of the submission of the full application, depending on project complexity and applicant readinessFunding Agreement and project implementationSuccessful applicants will be required to report on progress and provide documentation throughout the term of the Agreement using templates provided by the program:Progress updates tied to funding release, including activities completed and progress made toward deliverables and program outcomes;Financial reports provide information to ensure funding is being applied to eligible costs;The final Report will describe the process, performance, outcomes, impacts, and key learning from the project.The program will prioritize projects that meet the following criteria:Projects within the forestry sector;Projects located in rural, remote, or forestry-dependent communities;Projects that have a high degree of readiness, need, and direct impact; andProjects that are Indigenous-led or benefit Indigenous peoples.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:This program allows funding to be used in conjunction with a variety of other funding sources (private investment, loans, federal grants, etc.)Applicants should have at least 25% of project costs secured from the applicant organization or partner;Projects with other confirmed funding sources may be prioritized.Process Best Practices:The program will assess alignment with the program's goals, such as:Clean and inclusive growth:Inclusive and high-quality employment opportunities;Supports reconciliation with Indigenous peoples;Environmental responsibility, clean manufacturing, and circular economies;Contributes to sustainable growth in sector and supply chains.Economic impact and viability:Demonstrates sufficient operational capacity, workforce, and sustainable access to supplies and materials;Demonstrates market demand;Financial viability and sustainable business plan with a high degree of readiness;Contributes to economic resilience, diversification, and growth in the region.If the applicant has project partners, it is advised that applicant apply with the letter(s) of support from the partners right away for the initial proposal;Applicants are also advised to have a business plan ready at the time of application; andPlease keep all receipts and budget documentation for the financial reports.Forms:Program webpage: click hereProgram guidelines: click hereFAQs: click hereStream 1 proposal form: click hereStream 2 proposal form: click here

    Updated on 2025/04/01

      Grant Criteria 
      The Food Processing Program - Stream 2 supports the growth, innovation, and modernization of Quebec’s food transformation and distribution sector by providing up to $500,000 in non-repayable funding for projects that automate operations, improve productivity, integrate advanced technologies, or enhance food quality, safety, and competitiveness.Grant Value:Up to 60% of eligible project costs to a maximum of $150,000.Note: Funding is provided as a non-repayable contribution for eligible modernization and productivity projects.Turnaround Time: pendingEligible Applicants:Quebec-based SMEs in the food processing or food distribution sectors;Cooperatives and non-profit organizations engaged in food transformation or distribution;Businesses registered and compliant with Quebec tax authorities; andCompanies demonstrating financial capacity to complete the project.Ineligible Applicants:Businesses outside Quebec;Projects primarily related to retail or restaurant services;Entities in bankruptcy or under protection from creditors; andApplicants that have not met requirements of previous government financial assistance.Eligible Activities:Acquisition and installation of automation or digital technologies to modernize operations;Process optimization and productivity improvement initiatives;Implementation of food safety, traceability, or quality control systems;Integration of advanced equipment or sustainable production methods; andProjects supporting distribution efficiency or cold chain enhancement.Ineligible Activities:Routine maintenance or repair work;General operating or administrative activities;Purely commercial or marketing initiatives without production impact; andResearch or product development unrelated to transformation or distribution capacity.Eligible Expenses:Purchase and installation of production and automation equipment;Consulting, engineering, and professional services directly tied to the project;Software, digital systems, and training related to new technologies;Infrastructure improvements directly required for equipment operation; andProject management and implementation costs (within reasonable limits).Ineligible Expenses:Operating wages and ongoing overhead;Expenses incurred before application approval;Land or building acquisition; andNon-essential or luxury equipment not linked to productivity.Program Details:Funding is non-repayable;Minimum project cost threshold applies (based on project scale and applicant type);Projects must be completed within 24 months of approval;Applicants must obtain all necessary permits and comply with Quebec regulatory standards; andProgram administered by the Ministère de l’Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l’Alimentation du Québec (MAPAQ).

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Program does not allow funding to be used retroactively;All applicants must demonstrate financial capacity to carry out the project.Process Best Practices:Projects are evaluated based on innovation, productivity gains, and sectoral impact;Supporting documents such as quotes, financial statements, and project plans are required.Links :Program Website (French only) : click hereFAQ (French only) : click hereEligible Projects list (French Only) : click hereApplication Guide (French Only) : click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This funding program supports small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the Southern Interior of BC that are already exporting or are export-ready. The program provides funding up to $10,000 to fuel expansion into other provinces and international markets (outside the United States). Grant Value:50% up to $10,000 per project with 1:1 matching requirement.Turnaround Time: 1-2 weeksEligible Applicants:Must be small- to medium-sized businesses headquartered in the Southern Interior of British Columbia.Be legally registered and operating in BC;Demonstrate market-readiness and capacity to expand into new regions or countries outside of the US; andBe an export-ready company that already has a documented plan to expand extra-provincially or into international markets; and Ideally a company that is already doing business outside BC and the United States.Eligible Activities:Projects must focus on market expansion activities, including:Participation in inter-provincial or international trade shows;Attendance at trade missions and export-focused events;Conducting primary market research;Travel expenses to reach potential buyers, distributors and/or partners;Visa or entry permit application fees;Intellectual property or trademark protection fees;Certification, licensing, or permit fees; andInspections or regulatory approvals.Product compliance testing;Language translation or interpretation services;Labelling and packaging to meet market requirements.Program Details:The program will enable successful applicants to:Find new customers and channels to market;Establish international partnerships & attract foreign investments;Overcome common export-related barriers and incremental costs; andBoost economic resilience across the Southern Interior region.Applications are accepted on a rolling basis until funds are fully committed;Maximum of one application per company;Applicants must be in good standing with provincial and federal business regulations;Applicants must demonstrate market readiness and the capacity to execute proposed expansion activities;Funding is reimbursed upon proof of completion and eligible expense documentation.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices :The program does not allow funding to be used retroactively;Stacking with other government funding is permitted, provided the total government contribution does not exceed 75% of eligible project costs.Process Best Practices : Applicants are encouraged to submit a detailed plan outlining market entry goals, activities, and expected outcomes;Applicants are required to submit a detailed application outlining market objectives and planned activities;Due to high interest, early application submission is strongly recommended.Forms : Program Website : click hereApplication Portal : click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Market Entry Development Program provides access to an in-market business development consultant (valued at $24,000) for up to 20 days. Eligible applicants must be Atlantic Canadian Food and Beverage companies with an interest in expanding their export sales to Europe. The intent of the program is to establish a virtual presence for Atlantic Canadian companies in Europe or Asia and to grow export sales and establish new business relationships.Grant Value:  Consultant services valued at $26,000 (applicants to contribute $2500)Turnaround Time: pendingEligible Applicants:Be headquartered in Atlantic Canada (Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, PEI, Newfoundland & Labrador);Possess a fully-developed, exportable product and/or service that can be sold into European and Asian markets;Interested in creating or expanding their international footprint, meaning a move to new markets or increasing their total sales volume in Europe or Asia;Possess a proven record or strong potential of revenue growth;Demonstrate the financial capacity to execute their strategy and support potential in-market activities;Have senior management commitment and the human resource capacity to execute the strategy, including internal and external sales and marketing support who will lead implementation including the potential of travel to market;Have the production and service capacity to meet projected increases in demand;Have considered their expected outcomes in international markets including anticipated sales growth;Have an understanding of factors that may need to be addressed (e.g., competition, cultural competencies, import controls, intellectual property status, certifications, and regulatory, legal, taxation issues); andDemonstrate how participation in this program is linked to the export planning and goals.Ineligible Applicants:Games of chance operations, bingo halls, small-scale gaming operations;Real estate developers;Retailers, franchises, distributors, agents, or associations;Creative industries companies;Publicly funded organizations.Program Details:Successful applicants will be required to work collaboratively with the consultant, participate regularly in virtual development and sales meetings, and be willing to travel and spend time in-market;Participating companies will be required to commit the financial resources necessary to execute on their market strategy, as agreed to between the company and the programParticipating companies will be required to report on progress/activities undertaken as per the agreed upon Statement of Work and may be asked to complete mandatory evaluations on the overall service delivery for up to a year following the MEDP end date.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Market Readiness Program funds up to $250,000 to early-stage technology companies that are incorporated and are at the commercialization stage. Applicant companies will be evaluated based on the potential long-term competitiveness, value proposition, capacity to scale as well as strong Intellectual Property rights. The intent of the program is to attract additional private investment, support scalable business growth, and support innovation in Ontario.Grant Value:MR125 Stream: $125,000MR250 Stream: $250,000Turnaround Time: 3 monthsEligible Applicants:Be based in Ontario;Headquartered in the province and have at least 50% of the current company headcount in the province.Have been incorporated within the last 5 years;Have raised less than $1 million in third-party capital, excluding friends and family;Currently or previously affiliated with a university, college or research hospital campus linked accelerator or incubator, in Ontario;Be an early-stage technology company in sectors including, but not limited to:IT;Robotics;AI;Health technology;Cleantech; andAdvanced manufacturing.Has a minimum addressable market size of $100M;Has a product built;Have early market traction;Close to commercialization;Meet the stream specific eligibility criteria below:MR125 for $125,000 Investments:Be prepared to discuss the proposed terms of the current round which is being led by third party investors (Not OCE);Be past the internal beta design and development stages and work with prospective market customers to improve the offering;Be developing proprietary technology;Be defining its primary product/ market fit and establishing reasonable pricing models with a sales strategy/pipeline;Have a defined business model and financial forecasts (1-2 years); andBe raising sufficient investment to reach the next defined significant milestone(s).MR250 for $250,000 Investments:Have already raised a pre-seed or seed round and are looking for additional growth capital;Be advanced in their growth and sales strategy, showing early but consistent traction and a sales strategy that is repeatable and scalable;Have potential to redefine or disrupt a targeted industry (ie. strong IP and a differentiated offering);Be pivoting to target growth with higher momentum;Have a business model and financial forecasts (2-4 years); andHave milestones that drive a Seed extension or Series A round in the near-term future (1-2 years).Eligible Activities:Customer creation and development of scalable sales processes;Business model development activities; andInvestments for the round to be used for significant milestones for a runway up to 12 months.Program Details:Companies are reviewed through a rigorous internal pre-vetting process before being selected to proceed to an investment advisory committee for consideration;Due diligence documents will be evaluated by the IAC against assessment criteria, including:Product Offering: core value proposition, ability to address customer challenges, appropriateness of stage of development, and commercializationTarget Customers: identification and plan to access customers, willingness to pay, marketing strategyMarket and Competition: appropriateness and feasibility of the business model and pricing structure, plan to address competition and barriers to entry (e.g. regulatory), potential exit strategyTeam: ability and resources to achieve the milestones and deliver a repeatable sales processMilestones: suitability to grow customer base and/or attract follow-on investment, risk mitigation plan, clarity and feasibility of next stepsSuccessful companies must complete the following activation requirements within 30 days of investment approval:Execution of OCE’s standard funding agreement.Do not fill out this template. A copy of the agreement will be generated through AccessOCE and sent to the Company upon approval of the investment);Proof of Matching Funds: Please note that the proof of matching contribution in the form of a current bank statement (dated within 30 days approval notification) is required before the OCE investment can be released;Electronic Fund Transfer (EFT)/ Direct Deposit form and void cheque;Execution of OCE's standard Convertible Debenture or other financial instrument approved by OCE prior to submission; andCompany's profile.The program will not release any funds until the investment is activated;If for any reason the requirements for activation are not met within 30 days from the date of release of the approval notification, the investment offer may be retracted.Successful applicants will be required to provide:An annual investor update:With annual metrics survey each April for 5 years following investment date;A final report:Including progress, performance metrics, proof of expenditures, and a financial attestation;Be submitted within 30 days of completion of the milestones.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Process Best Practices:Applicants are advised to have the most up-to-date financials as well as an investor pitch deck ready for the initial eligibility and suitability questionnaire;Note that completion of the eligibility and suitability questionnaire does not constitute an application for financing. For further eligibility questions, please email the program manager at Jennifer.Moles@oce-ontario.org; andIf the applicant does not have a Business Development Manager assigned to them, the first place to go is the right-hand side of the programs page in the “Ready to take the next step?” box.Forms:Program website: click hereEligibility and suitability questionnaire: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This program allows student entrepreneurs to grow their businesses with the intention of bringing new technology or goods to the market. It will fund 50% of a research-based internship for the student entrepreneur to expedite research and development efforts that align with the company and their graduate work. Students will receive a minimum of $7,500 for a 4-month project—duration and grant value may increase based on the needs of the startup.Note: This program is different from the Mitacs Accelerate program. It allows student entrepreneurs to work at their own companies.Grant Value: For 1 internship unit (4-6 months), Mitacs will provide 50% of wage subsidies up to $7,500. For projects less than 6 internship units, Mitacs and the employer will contribute $7,500 each ($10,000 for the internship and $5,000 for business and R&D costs). After 6 internship units, Mitacs will contribute $7,333 and the employer will contribute $6,000 ($10,000 for the internship and $3,333 for business and R&D costs).Turnaround time: 6-8 weeksEligible Employers:Early-stage businesses in approved incubators that are: Testing a new product, service, or technology; orRe-iterating an existing product, service, or technology; The participant's startup must be affiliated with an incubator for the entire duration of the placement; If a business drops out of their incubator, they can apply to the regular Mitacs Accelerate program; andMust be incorporated.Note: The applicant is both the employer and the participant.Eligible Candidates:Current undergraduate, graduate students, or post-doc startup founders.Eligible Activities:Research activities pertaining to a new project for the startup that: Addresses "the unknown" - an artifact in computer science that needs solving; Makes a new contribution to the body of knowledge in a field; Is broadly applicable;Is defined by the research community;The results are publishable in a peer-reviewed journal or conference;Builds on previous research; The level of research expected is appropriate for the level of education of the applicant (undergraduate vs. post-grad); andOther activities related to the business are welcome, but the application should focus on research and development efforts.Note: Projects in which the intern develops novel software to answer a research question or test a hypothesis are also eligible. It is important to be clear how the results will be evaluated by the student.Ineligible Activities:Non-research activities; Research that is not pertaining to the new project; or Marketing activities for company promotion.Program Details:Must take place at the participant's own company; Must contribute to both the company and their graduate work; Must focus on a specific research project;Minimum of 4 months; andCan apply for extensions (no maximum limit) and more funding (no maximum limit).
