grants.grant_criteria: The New Entrant Farm Business Accelerator Program supports beginning farmers and ranchers in British Columbia by providing up to $15,000 in cost-shared funding (covering up to 75% of eligible project costs) to help develop business plans, implement farm infrastructure, and accelerate the growth and financial viability of new agricultural enterprises. The aim of this program is to enable new entrants to strengthen business management capacity, improve productivity, and transition their operations toward long-term commercial success within B.C.’s agri-food sector.
grants.best_practices: Eligible Best Practices :Applicants can combine this program funding with other government cost-share programs up to a maximum of 75% of total eligible project costs;The program does not provide retroactive funding for expenses incurred before the contribution agreement is signed;Applicants should:Be new entrants who have reported farm income for five years or fewer;Demonstrate a clear business concept with potential for long-term commercial viability;Possess or plan to develop a comprehensive business plan and marketing strategy;Show readiness to invest in on-farm infrastructure, equipment, or technology that improves productivity and profitability;Contribute a minimum of 25% of total project costs through cash or in-kind resources;Maintain a valid Business Registration Number and Premises ID;\Meeting the eligibility criteria does not guarantee funding approval;Funding may only be used for projects that align with program objectives and are completed within the approved timeframe.Process Best Practices :Applications are reviewed on a merit basis, considering project feasibility, financial capacity, and potential for business growth and economic impact within B.C.’s agriculture sector;Applicants are encouraged to apply well in advance of their planned project start date, as costs incurred prior to approval will not be eligible;Approved applicants must complete projects within the designated Phase 1 or Phase 2 timelines;Funding is reimbursed upon project completion and submission of required documentation;Projects are monitored for compliance, and applicants may be asked to provide proof of expenditures, progress updates, and results achieved.

The aim of this program is to enable new entrants to strengthen business management capacity, improve productivity, and transition their operations toward long-term commercial success within B.C.’s agri-food sector.Grant Value:Phase 1 – Business Planning: Up to $3,000 (consultant-assisted) or $1,250 (self-developed);Phase 2 – Implementation: Up to $15,000 (75% reimbursement).Turnaround Time: Approximately 25–30 business days.Eligible Applicants:Individuals or farm businesses located and operating in British Columbia;Have reported farm income to the Canada Revenue Agency for five years or fewer (or none to date);Intend to operate a commercial, for-profit agricultural enterprise;Possess or plan to acquire a valid Business Registration Number and Premises ID;Have not received funding from the program in a previous intake;Be in good standing with the B.C. Ministry of Agriculture and Food.Eligible Activities:Development of a business plan or market strategy;Investment in on-farm infrastructure, equipment, or technology that supports productivity and efficiency;Adoption of financial, production, or marketing systems that enhance growth and profitability;Projects that demonstrate readiness to scale operations and generate sustainable farm income.Eligible Expenses:Consultant or advisory fees for business planning;Costs of infrastructure materials and equipment purchases;Labour and professional services directly tied to approved projects;Marketing and branding activities associated with farm expansion;Other direct project expenses pre-approved by the Ministry.Program Details:Applicants must contribute a minimum of 25% of total eligible project costs;All projects must be completed within program timelines;Funding is reimbursed after project completion and submission of required documentation;Projects must align with program objectives of business growth, economic sustainability, and local food system development;Administered by the B.C. Ministry of Agriculture and Food under the Sustainable Agriculture Strategy.

      Best Practices & Forms

      Grant Criteria 
      The On-Farm Value-Added grant program offers funding of up to $250,000 to support primary producers in adding value to their agricultural products to grow sales, expand production capacity, explore market opportunities and create jobs in Alberta.Grant Value:Stream A: Up to $50,000;Stream B: Up to $250,000.Turnaround Time: 2-3 monthsEligible Applicants: Be a primary producer;Be an individual or corporation registered in Alberta and operating in Alberta;Be responsible for input costs for crops, bees or livestock;Produce at least $25,000 worth of commercial agriculture production annually;Not be a landlord whose only interest in crop, bee, cattle operation is ownership of the land; andBe adding value past harvest or slaughter of the agricultural product. An applicant that has an active application to the On-Farm Value-Added Program or Emerging OpportunitiesIneligible Applicants: Processors;Industry organizations;Applied research organizations;Post-secondary institutions;Federal, provincial, and municipal governments agencies and institutions;Retail businesses, restaurants and food establishments; andAny other person deemed by the Minister to be ineligible.Eligible Activities: Applicants may apply for funding under one of the following:Processing Capacity Expansion;Food Safety Improvement;New Product and Process Development; andMarket Development and Access.Ineligible Activities: Activities related to cleaning, bagging, handling and/or storing of primary products;Construction of walls, floors, ceilings, or ancillary buildings;Labels and packaging design that is not in relation to new products or for new markets;Advertising;Promotions;Activities associated with aquaculture, aquaponics, or seafood processing, with the exception of actitivies related to the international marketing of fish and seafood products which are eligible and may be included in the application; andActivities that provide support for province-specific branding, promotion or marketing activities that are detrimental to another province or territory.Eligible Expenses: 25% of eligible capital expenses are covered by the program and the remainder by the applicant;50% of eligible non-capital expenses are covered by the program and the remainder by the applicant;Eligible expenses vary depending on which area the applicant is applying underProcessing Capacity Expansion:Eligible Capital Expenses:Processing Equipment;Food Safety Equipment;Software systems to assist in processing;Third party engineering related to purchase, and configuration of eligible equipment.NOTE: Leased equipment is ineligible.Eligible Non-Capital Expenses: Training costs associated with adopting new technologies, new equipment and/or new automation processes as related to processing.Food Safety Improvement:Eligible Non-Capital Expenses:Development and implementation of a food safety system;Training costs associated with adopting new technologies, new equipment and/or new food safety food processes related to food safety improvement.New Product and Process Development:Eligible Non-Capital Expenses:Sensory and shelf-life testing;Validation of nutritional or health claims;Attribute identification;Environmental product declaration;Non-food product regulation studies;Scale-up trials;Formulation development, including ingredient costs for trials;Process improvement;First run of labels and/or package printing used for new product launch to a max of 2500 units per new product; andFirst-time brand design and development. Market Development and Access:Eligible Non-Capital Expenses:Feasibility studies;Market readiness assessments;Marketing and export plans for local, domestic, or international market opportunities;Design of market support materials for new product and new market launch;Capital investment strategy development;First-time certification audit;Development of initial online presence for the purpose of e-commerce, including translation for new markets;Enhancement and expansion of an online marketing/sales platform;In-store or in-market product demonstrations, excluding the cost of product samples and shipping, and Trade shows and conference registration fees for events directly related to accessing new markets and/or launch of new products (max of two people per event) virtual events are included.Ineligible Expenses: Travel expenses not in compliance with the Travel Expense Policy;Expenses not incurred by the Eligible Applicant in carrying out the Eligible Activity;Installation and labour costs;Shipping and commissioning costs for equipment;Costs of lease of office furniture, space and equipment;Fixture that are not an eligible capital expense;Costs of equipment for storage purposes, not directly related to the eligible activity;Costs associated with the building such as plumbing, framing, flooring, electrical and insulation;On-going business operational activities and overhead expenses;Staff or consulting expenses for product sale activities, or in market representation for existing products;Advertising expenses;Sponsorship;Donation of product;Listing dess, distribution fees or shelf stocking fees;Website hosting, domain registration or ongoing website maintenance;Vehicles of any kind; andGoods and Services Tax.Program Details: Project activities can take place between January 1, 2025 and March 15, 2026;Funding is granted on a case-by-case basis and not on a first come, first served basis;The eligible applicant will also be required to submit a final report to the Minister;Additional reports may be requested throughout the project duration;Stream A application must include: A completed application form, signed by an authorized representative, and all documents required to be submitted pursuant to that form;Quotations or invoices for capital expenses over $10,000; andAny additional supplementary documentation requested by the Minister.Stream B application must include:A completed application form, signed by an authorized representative, and all documents required to be submitted pursuant to that form;Documents to demonstrate the applicant has the necessary capacity to complete the activities included in the applications; andAny additional supplementary documentation requested by the Minister.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Ontario Food Technology Pilot offers non-repayable funding of up to $100,000 (covering 50% of project costs) to help early-stage businesses in southern Ontario test and validate innovative food technologies. By supporting real-world pilot projects across the food value chain, the program reduces risk, accelerates commercialization, and encourages industry collaboration.Grant Value: 50% of project costs up to $100,000. Turnaround Time: Within 60 Business Days. Eligible Applicants:Incorporated businesses in southern Ontario working in food technology innovation;Must be located in one of the eligible catchment areas (See page 6 of the application guidelines)Must register for a free Canadian Food Innovation Network (CFIN) membership before applying;Annual revenue in the most recent fiscal year must be ≤ $5 million;Must have or be developing an Intellectual Property (IP) strategy for the innovation;Priority is given to B2B solutions that support the food processing, foodservice, distribution, or retail sectors.Eligible Projects:Projects must focus on B2B technology solutions, not just food product creation or reformulation;Projects must validate and demonstrate an innovative food technology that is not yet commercialized, which is at mid-to-late stages of development (TRL 6-7 aiming toward TRL 8–9);Must address post-farmgate challenges (processing, distribution, retail, foodservice) — projects focused mainly on farming/agriculture are not eligible;Must align with innovation priorities such as food safety & traceability, digital supply chains, cleantech, circular economy, next-gen ingredients, packaging, kitchen/restaurant tech, and consumer apps;Must involve at least one partner in the food sector who will participate or enable the pilot.Eligible Expenses:Expenses must be directly related to the project;Direct labour;Subcontractors and consulting;Direct materials;Equipment; andTravel and outreach (if related to project activities)Reasonable and outlined in the budget;Incurred during the eligible project period; andForeign eligible costs must be identified in the application and approved by CFIN in advance, as only limited foreign expenses can be supported.Ineligible Expenses:Land, buildings, vehicles;Interest, refinancing debt;Depreciation/amortization;Hospitality, entertainment, non-project marketing;Recruiting fees;In-kind costs.Note: A complete list of  ineligible expenses is provided in page 11-12 of  the guidelines.Program Details:The program is delivered by the Canadian Food Innovation Network (CFIN) and funded partly by the Government of Canada / FedDev Ontario;Projects are expected to demonstrate technologies in real-world or operational environments, helping innovators validate performance and market readiness;Applications must be submitted online via the CFIN Smart Simple portal after membership registration;The application typically includes pre-screening questions and a short video pitch;The project must start at least 60 days after the application deadline and finish within 12 months (no later than March 31, 2027);Project budget must be between $20,000 and $200,000 total costs;Funding is provided on a reimbursement basis and a non-refundable 5% project management fee applies;Application questions and scoring criteria are provided in pages 15-18 of the guidelines; andFunding claims are accepted quarterly on March 31, June 30, September 30, and December 31. 

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices: Having partners (e.g., testbeds or adopters in the food sector) helps ensure demonstrations occur in operational settings;Industry partners are encouraged to provide cash contributions to the lead applicant under the OFTP program, with contributions clearly outlined in the application;If an applicant does not have a partner, CFIN may help identify a testbed from its membership, though securing one is not guaranteed.Showing strong industry relevance by selecting appropriate innovation priorities (e.g., food safety, packaging, digital supply chain);Clearly demonstrating how the project will advance the technology from TRL 6–7 to TRL 8–9;Stacking with other government programs is possible up to 75% of total eligible costs, but any additional support must be disclosed in the application;Projects must be located in an eligible Ontario census catchment area (see Page 6 of the Application Guidelines); andThe lead applicant must be the technology or solution developer. Process Best Practices: Clear IP strategy or budget for IP work if not yet started;Measurable commercial outcomes (e.g., pilot results, customer adoption);Letters of support from partners or testbeds to strengthen your case;Finances must show capacity to carry project costs until reimbursement;Assessment criteria closely for narrative responses (innovation, fit, scalability...); Project partners can claim reimbursable expenses under an OFTP project, provided these costs are clearly included in the application and approved by CFIN before the project begins; Projects start at least 60 days after intake; costs before the start date aren’t eligible; Funding claims are accepted quarterly on March 31, June 30, September 30, and December 31.andCFIN project management fee: 5% of total eligible CFIN funding (not reimbursable);FormsProgram Webpage : click hereProgram Guidelines: click hereProgram FAQ: click hereApplication Link: click here

grants.grant_criteria: This program provides funding of up to $5,000,000 to for-profit Ontario businesses undertaking projects that respond to U.S. trade disruptions. Funding supports initiatives that strengthen domestic manufacturing capacity, reshore production, or diversify export markets. The program is intended to help businesses mitigate risks caused by tariffs, supply chain instability, and protectionist trade measures.Grant Value:Business Projects:Interest-Free Loans for up to 75% of eligible project costs, to a maximum of $5,000,000 per project; andLoan Forgiveness: Up to 30% of the loan (max $1,500,000) may be forgiven if the project meets defined investment and job creation targets.Grants are available for qualifying applicants but are assessed on a case-by-case basis based on project impact and regional needs.Turnaround Time: Approximately 45 business days.Eligible Applicants:Business Projects:Must be for-profit and incorporated in Ontario;Must have a minimum of 3 years in operation with financial statements;Must employ at least 5 full-time employees in Ontario;Must be able to demonstrate economic harm caused by U.S. trade disruptions, such as tariffs or export barriers; andProjects must have a minimum eligible cost of $200,000.Ineligible applicants :Not-for-profit organizations/associations/charities;Sole proprietors;Retail;Construction companies providing primary construction services (production of construction products is eligible);Providers of personal services; andConsulting firms.Eligible Projects:Projects must demonstrate how they will enhance domestic resilience and competitiveness by:Expanding domestic manufacturing or processing capacity;Reshoring or onshoring key operations previously outsourced abroad;Diversifying into new export markets or supply chain routes; andIntroducing equipment, technology, or facility upgrades to support these objectives.Ineligible projects :Ongoing operations including maintenance and capital replacement (exact replacements are not eligible, upgraded technology/equipment would be considered eligible);Refinancing of existing business operations;Acquisitions and buyout;Restructuring, or relocating to other jurisdictions within Ontario;Electricity projects;Waste management/primary recycling; andHospitality projects (hotels and restaurants).Eligible Expenses:Capital equipment and advanced manufacturing technology;Facility upgrades and retrofits;Labour and training costs directly related to project implementation;Consulting or third-party expertise required to complete the project; andDomestic market entry or export diversification costs.Please see program guidelines for details on eligible and ineligible costs.Program Details:Projects may be up to 4 years in length, with funding disbursed over multiple fiscal years;Applicants must complete an eligibility self-assessment and connect with a program advisor before submitting a full application;Applications must be submitted through Transfer Payment Ontario (TPON);A complete application includes:Eligibility checklist;Project plan and detailed budget;Financial statements (minimum 3 years);Articles of Incorporation and corporate structure; andMust not be immediate family members or relatives of owners and directors.Exceptions may be made in smaller, Northern communities with a limited labour base.Eligible Expenses:Intern salary; andMandatory employment-related costs (Canada Pension Plan, Employment Insurance, and mandatory minimum vacation pay)Ineligible Expenses:Discretionary benefits paid by the employer (i.e. sick pay, group medical or dental plans);Training expenses;Computers and equipment;       Grant Criteria 
      The Poultry and Egg On-Farm Investment program provide over $250,000 in funding to chicken, turkey, egg, and broiler hatching eff producers. The funding can be used to hire contractors, constructing new infrastructure, purchasing equipment, and other related expenses. The intent of the program is to improve on-farm efficiency, food safety and environmental sustainability.Grant Value:Up to 85% of eligible costs for Youth ProducersUp to 70% of eligible costs for regular applicantsTurnaround Time: 100 business daysEligible Applicants:Be one of the following:Chicken producers;Turkey producers;Turkey breeders;Egg producers; andBroiler hatching egg producers.Be an individual and/or legal entity capable of entering into legally binding agreements or contracts;Have held quota/shares of provincial production on January 1, 2021;Be one of the following types:Poultry and/or egg producers holding quota;Poultry and/or egg producers licensed, or equivalent, by a provincial marketing agency;Atlantic Canada Hatching Egg Producers; andPoultry and/or egg producers under new entrants programs with loaned quota and/or whole-farm leases with loaned quota at the time of the calculation.Eligibility for Young Producer:Is 35 years old or younger on January 1, 2021;Is actively engaged in farming in Canada;Is either:A majority owner:Is a sole proprietor;Has majority ownership or more than 50% of the business;Led by a young producer who has:Managed the business for more than 2 years;Is working towards acquisition/successionHas an active role in strategic decision-making;Be a child's spouse or grandchild of the majority; andBe currently developing or has developed a succession plan to acquire the farm.Eligible Activities:Meet 1 or more of the following objectives:Increasing efficiency or productivity;Improving on-farm food safety and biosecurity;Improving environmental sustainability;Responding to consumer preferences (improving animal welfare, adopting alternative housing systems, transitioning to organic production, etc.)Examples include but are not limited to:The hiring of external expertise;Construction of new infrastructure or expansion of infrastructure;Building retrofits;Purchasing equipment;Shipping and installation of eligible assets, equipment, and materials; andTraining related to other eligible project activities.Eligible Expenses:Capital assets;Contracted services;Salaries and benefits pertaining to:Transportation and installation of eligible assets/materials;New infrastructure and retrofits.Non-recurring costs for equipment and operational upgrades.Note: Eligible costs must be incurred on or after March 19, 2019.Ineligible Expenses:The purchase of quota;Animal purchases (replacing or increasing flock);The refundable portion of Goods and Services Tax/Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/ HST);Acquisition of land or existing buildings;Marketing costs;Legal fees;On-going support costs for items such as software licenses, troubleshooting, and upgrades; and machinery maintenance or repair;Banking/credit card fees and interest charges.Note: Please see the program guide for the complete list of ineligible expenses.Program Details:Maximum funding is based on the share of provincial quota/production on January 1, 2021, as identified by the respective provincial marketing board;Applicants must register with the program prior to the application submission here;Applicants with multiple licenses will have the option to register all their licenses together, rather than registering each license separately with the program.Applicants may submit more than 1 application at a time so long as the total of funding requested does not exceed the maximum funding amount;It can take up to 3 business days to receive an acknowledgment from PEFIP that the submission has been received.Funding allocation is not transferrable to a producer that did not hold quota/share of production on January 1, 2021;Applicants are required to provide:Copies of the receipts or invoices;Copies of proof of payment;A copy of the organization's Articles of Incorporation;Proof of financing including documents or bank statements detailing an applicant's contribution towards the total project costs;Proof of activity is required when the applicant is applying for activities already completed at the Project Application submission;Copies of authorizations or permits might be required by AAFC during the application assessment or at the claim stage.The program will assess the applications based on the following:The project completion date, with the aim of providing successful applicants with their reimbursements as close as possible as to when their project was/is due to be completedProvincial and sectoral distribution, to help ensure the fair distribution of funding across all provinces and sub-sectors for each of the program's 10 yearsProject size, to help ensure the fair distribution of funding across both small and large producers for each of the program's 10 yearsPayments under $250,000 will be made in 1 payment within 30 business days;Projects with payments greater than $250,000 may require more than 1 payment per project.The program require that applicants retain records for 7 years after the date of expiration or early termination of the funding agreement with AAFC, whichever comes later.

It funds product demonstrations to support SMEs in commercializing their products and achieving an optimal market position to increase revenue and expand into global markets.Grant Value: 50% up to $150,000Turnaround time: 3-4 weeksEligible Applicants:For-profit small and medium-sized enterprise;Incorporated or General Partnership registered in Alberta;Have a significant physical and corporate operational presence in Alberta;Have appropriate Alberta ownership;Have discernible intent that operational benefits will flow primarily within Alberta;Less than 500 full-time employees;Less than $50 Million in annual gross revenue; Have a product(s) that no longer requires refinement to the core technology (product is ready to pilot in an operational setting to verify product value and reduce its uncertainty);Have product(s) that are looking to expand sales or broaden market segments (product is ready for demonstration in an operational environment and may need to extend product core technology and/or capability);Have a relationship with a Strategic Partner (i.e. an organization willing to purchase, deliver and/or distribute product);Note: testing and strategic partners can be based in any country that Canada does business with.Have the financial capability to fund the required Applicant contribution;Be in good financial standing with Alberta Innovates, and its subsidiaries InnoTech Alberta and C-Fer Technologies; andAgree to proactively work with Alberta Innovates Project Advisor.Eligible Projects:Have at least 1 Strategic Partner at Expression of Interest, and need a signed Letter of Intent from the strategic partner(s) at the full proposal;Letter of Interest signed by the Strategic Partner should include how they will participate in the project such as any of the following:How the product is adopted and evaluated;Intention to work with the Applicant to resolve issues;Intention to purchase the SME product based on success criteria being met; and/orIntention to enter into a distribution agreement of the demonstrated product upon Project completion.Prototype or product demonstration should be at a Technical Readiness Level (TRL) of 7, 8 or 9 (see here);The maximum project duration is 1 year;Demonstrate a strong pilot product demonstration plan with clear acceptance criteria;Can reasonably expect a first sale or distribution agreement within 18 months if the pilot is successful;Can reasonably expect expanded sales or distribution agreements if the demonstration is successful within 18 months;Demonstrate that the product has a high likelihood of the Strategic Partner being a first customer/distributor
or accelerated commercialization success within 18 months of the project start;Must be planned with “go/no go” milestones and performance indicators (see diagram below).Eligible Partners:Be Arm’s Length from the Applicant (cannot have any legal relationship with the Applicant);Provide a Letter of Intent indicating the intention to purchase or enter into a distribution agreement of the demonstrated product upon Project completion at the time of the full proposal submission;Have the financial capability to purchase/ or enter into a distribution agreement of the product upon Project completion;Demonstrates tangible resources committed to the Project; Be a legal entity with up to date corporate filings as Alberta Innovates may seek bankruptcy and litigation searches; andBe in good financial standing with Alberta Innovates and its subsidiaries InnoTech Alberta and C-Fer Technologies.Eligible Expenses:Salaries of employees working on the project;Any direct operating costs at reasonable market rates;Materials for the project;Capital assets and software (improvements, equipment, information databases);Contracted service/product providers;Travel, accommodation and meals at reasonable rates; andIn-kind expenses.Note: this list is not exhaustive, the funder may allow other costs on a discretionary basis.Ineligible Expenses:Training & development costs;Sales, marketing, and advertising costs;Costs associated with applying for grants;Routine testing and maintenance;Costs incurred prior to signing the Investment Agreement; andFederal and Provincial income taxes and GST.Note: this list is not exhaustive, the funder may restrict other costs on a discretionary basis

      Grant Criteria 
      This provincial program provides up to $10,000 for for-profit food and beverage businesses in Saskatchewan developing new or improved products that use Canadian-grown agricultural inputs.Grant Value:50% of eligible costs between $1,000 to $10,000 per project.Turnaround Time: Approximately 5 business days.Eligible Applicants:Agriculture value-added processors who meet the following criteria:A value-added product is defined as the upgrading of a raw primary agricultural product(s), or further upgrading of a processed product or derivative (includes co-product, by-product) into a new product;Processors must use an identifiable portion of inputs originating from primary agricultural commodities grown or raised in Canada;Operations and tax payments must be within the Province of Saskatchewan; andApplicants must be for-profit organizations.Eligible Activities:Technical service costs;Product development and demo costs;Test processing costs;Assessment and development of process & manufacturing technology costs; andSpecification development costs.NOTE:  Activities must be conducted at a third party facility and/or by a contracted service provider:Ineligible Activities:Activities already receiving funding from other Government of Saskatchewan sources or the Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada Agri-Marketing program;Training and wages/salaries for employees;Expenses for ongoing activities or other typical operating expenses;Per diems and meals domestically and internationally;Equipment purchases or other capital expenditures not explicitly identified as eligible;Administration costs and other activities not directly related specifically to the project;Cost of production for saleable products;Taxes, legal fees, and/or financing fees; andMembership in trade organizations.Program Details:Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and reviewed first-come, first-served;Only one PDP project can be active per business at a time;The proposal/product must demonstrate substantial use of Canadian-grown agricultural products; The program is part of a $5 million investment under the Sustainable Canadian Agricultural Partnership running until 2028;Projects must demonstrate commercial potential, include Canadian-grown inputs, and align with the goals of value-added food or beverage product development;The main objectives of the program include:Increase Value-Added Revenues;Enhance Value-Added Processing of Canadian Agriculture Products;Foster the Development of New Value-Added Products, Prototypes, and Processes;Reduce By-Product Waste; andExpand and Nurture Value-Added Businesses.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:This program allows stacking with other provincial or federal funding sources, provided the combined total of government assistance does not exceed 75% of eligible project costs; All sources of funding must be disclosed at the time of application and during final reporting; The program does not fund projects retroactively—costs incurred before formal approval are ineligible.Process Best Practices:Applicants must complete the Prospective Client Form and receive confirmation from the Saskatchewan Food Centre before starting any project work;Any changes to the project scope, timeline, or budget must be communicated to the Food Centre promptly for potential amendment and continued eligibility.Forms : Program Website : click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Project Development Fund will provide funding for the development of independent film and television productions, on a project-by-project basis, in the form of a non-recoupable development advance. Applications will be evaluated on a first-come, first-served basis until the budget has been fully designated for the fiscal year. Funding is based on a commitment from an eligible triggering agent. Grant Value: Up to $50000Note: The program does not take equity in any of the projects.Turnaround Time: 8 weeks.Eligible Applicants:Must be a company incorporated in British Columbia or Canada with its head office in British Columbia. A majority of the issued common voting shares must be held by BC residents;The applicant company may own 10% or less of the shares of a broadcaster;The applicant company may have 10% of its shares owned by a broadcaster or by a distributor;100% of the copyright of the project being developed must be owned, optioned, or controlled by the applicant; and,The market trigger must be at arm's length from the applicant company.Eligible Triggering Agents:Eligible applicants may apply to Creative BC for a total non-recoupable development advance of up to 50% of the committed cash amount from one of more of the following Triggering Agents for the development of an eligible project An arm’s length bona fide distribution entity (Canadian and international distributors);National Film Board of Canada (NFB co-productions only; 100% owned and controlled NFB productions are not eligible); A licensed public or private broadcaster (Canadian and international broadcasters);Over the top (OTT) subscription-based services (Netflix, Crave, Amazon, Hulu, YouTube Premium originals, Vimeo On-Demand originals);Telus Originals (Small Program Production Agreement);Bell Fund Slate Development; and Telefilm Canada Feature Film Fund (CFFF) Development Program.Eligible Projects:Feature films, destined for theatrical release (live action or animated);Televisions movies, pilots, televisions series and mini-series (live action, animated, variety, human interest, lifestyle and performing arts and entertainment);Short films and web series (live action or animated) (Limit of 10 short films and web series during fiscal year); andDocumentaries and docudramas for television broadcast or theatrical release.Eligible Expenses:Acquisitions of rights including option payments and license fees for platforms or formats;Research including the creation of a report, bible, outline and/or treatment; Writing of script stage including editing and various breakdowns (i.e. outline, treatment, first draft, second draft, final draft and polish and applicable fringes);Production of a demo-tape including, but not limited to, creation of a sizzle reel, presentation pilot, webisode or storyboards;Creation of a character model pack (for animated projects);Polishing, packaging, and a casting phase including creation of a casting reel;Travel costs necessary for creative work (e.g. interviewing, demo-taping and travel by/to/from the director); andAudience Development and Community Outreach Plan. Program Details:The program has an application submission fee of $105:Total development funding available to each eligible applicant(including affiliated related companies) may not exceed $50,000 in the fiscal year 2023/24;The total development funding available to an eligible project for the fiscal year 2023/24 is capped at $10,000;Except for television series, which include dramatic, animated, lifestyle, or documentary, which are capped at $20,000; and,The maximum 3 cumulative funding an eligible project can receive throughout its development history is $30,000, except for television series which are capped at $50,000;Eligible applicants must have a written agreement with one or more of the Triggering Agents confirming their commitment
to provide a development advance for the eligible project;Applications must be submitted to Creative BC no later than 30 days after the date that the BC applicant receives the letter of commitment or agreement with the Triggering Agent.Exceptions to the 30 days may be given. 

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:If a producer should receive funding from Telefilm’s CFFF Development Program above the $30,000 threshold for one project, they are not eligible to apply for the Telefilm Development Top-Up for that project; The program is not retroactive.Process Best Practices:Applications must be submitted to Creative BC no later than 30 days after the date that the applicant receives the letter or commitment or agreement with the Triggering Agent.Forms:Program webpage: click hereApplication form: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      Proof-of-concept plans for trials and demonstrations that are intended to exhibit the commercial feasibility of biologically-derived natural products or technologies may be granted up to 40% funding to a maximum of $350,000. The aim of this program is to prove the commercial feasibility of these products and technologies in order to minimize risk and advance future investment in the natural products sector. Grant Value: 40% of eligible project costs to a maximum of $350,000Turnaround Time: 2 monthsEligible Applicants:Canadian start-ups or SMEs:Must have the potential to achieve 10MM- 15MM in annual revenue within a market-reasonable period; andSole proprietors are ineligible.Research institutes:Products or technologies must address an industry or sector challenge with significant market potential; andNo limit on number of employees.Be a member of Canada’s Natural Product Innovation Cluster;Have a novel pre-commercial (Technology Readiness Levels(TRL) 4-9) 'natural product or technology';Defined as a biologically-based innovation that benefit people, animals and the planet, and can be applied to a range of industries, including: Food production and value-added agriculture; Bioproducts and sustainability; Human nutrition, health and wellness; Animal health and nutrition; and Water and waste management.Have potential for: Achieving 10MM- 15MM in annual revenue within a market-reasonable period;Significant economic, social, health and/or environmental benefits;Commercialization in Canada;Spillover benefits to more than one sector;Improving the representation of women, visible minorities, and Indigenous peoples in the natural products ecosystem.Eligible Activities:Animal, field, demonstration, or human trials;Late-stage trials for naturals products, services, or technologies that derive from a biological source; andCommercial demonstration trials.Ineligible Activities:Basic research or preliminary product/technology development;Pharmaceutical trials; andTrials that are not biological in nature.Eligible Expenses:Direct materials;Direct Labour;Subcontractors/consultants;Equipment (up to 10% of budget);Other direct costs (e.g. trial participant costs and some specialized software);Indirect costs up to ~15% of costs.Program Details:The project period cannot exceed 18 months; Applicants required to contribute 60% of project costs unless leveraging other government grant funding;Contract with NPC will include project scope, reporting requirements, and key milestones to be achieved;Applications will be reviewed by NPC staff, board members, and an external industry expert on a monthly basis;Disbursement of funds takes place through reimbursement of eligible project costs upon approval of quarterly reports;Includes a written and financial claim containing invoices and proof of payment.Annual reporting required for 5 years following program period; andFor research institutes, projects must be aimed at moving a product or technology from intellectual property disclosure to near-term spin-out and/or licensing opportunities.Evaluation Criteria: The novelty of the natural product or technology; Market opportunity; Business model/commercialization strategy;Competitors; Strength of the management team/research leadership team;Need and impact of the trial; Trial design and key activities; Qualifications of the individuals and/or centres conducting the trials; and Risk mitigation.

      Grant Criteria 
      This program provides a wage subsidy of up to 70% to a maximum of $7,000 to employers in the tourism and hospitality sector that hire post-secondary students for full-time or part-time placements. The goal of the program is to create employment and skills development opportunities that  benefit both students and employers.Grant Value:50% of wages up to $5,000;70% of wages up to $7000 for students from the following underrepresented groups:Women in STEM (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics);Indigenous students;Visible minorities; Newcomers to Canada (immigrated to Canada within the last 5 years);Persons with disabilities; andFirst year students. Turnaround Time: 2 weeksEligible Employers:Registered Canadian businesses, startups, and not-for-profits related to the tourism and hospitality sector; andI.e. accommodations, food and beverage services, culinary, recreation, entertainment, culture, events, transportation, travel services, etc.Must provide a work-integrated learning opportunity for the student.Ineligible Employers:Federal, provincial, territorial, and municipal governments;Crown corporations, hospitals, public long-term care facilities, and post-secondary institutions; andMembers the House of Commons and/or Senate.Eligible Candidate:Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or has refugee status;Registered at a recognized Canadian post-secondary institution in a program that includes a work-integrated learning component;Undergraduate or graduate student;Full- or part-time student; andLegally entitled to work in Canada.Ineligible Candidate:International students; andImmediate family members, unless a clear, transparent, and fair nepotism policy is in place.Peogram Details:Applications are being accepted for placements in the following semesters:Winter 2025 (January 1, 2025 to April 30, 2025): CLOSEDSummer 2025 (May 1, 2025 to August 31, 2025): CLOSEDFall 2025 (September 1, 2025 to December 31, 2025): OPENThe work experience must coincide with a course, degree, certificate, diploma, or other recognized program offered by the student's institution;The student will need to provide proof of enrolment (e.g. a letter from a registrar) in a recognized Canadian post-secondary institution;Ideally, the document will also demonstrate that the student’s program includes a work-integrated-learning component.Eligible placement types include:Co-op placements;Internships;Practicums;Mentorships;Field placements; and Applied projects.Placement can be full-time or part-time;Minimum 20 hours per week;4-15 weeks per semester;On-site, remote, or hybrid allowed; Participants must be placed on payroll; Students hired as independent contractors are not eligible for the subsidy;Placements must not displace an existing worker or fill a role left vacant due to a labour dispute;Placements must be "net new," meaning that the SWPP student is incremental to the employer's "baseline" of student hires. An employer's "baseline" is the number of students they hired without SWPP support the year prior to participating in SWPP;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2022, 2023, or 2024, use the number of students hired in the year prior to that first time you accessed SWPP support;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2024, use the number of students hired in 2023;Net new baselines must be calculated each year (if you participate in SWPP every year, your net new baseline will increase accordingly).Include co-op and non-co-op students in your initial baseline calculation. Do not include high school students, recent graduates, or international students, as they are not included in the SWPP program;If a student placement crosses over the fiscal year (ie: January - April), they count toward the earlier fiscal year;If you hire a student for separate placements in different fiscal years (ie: Summer 2022, Summer 2023), you must count them in both fiscal years.Apprenticeships that are part of the designated trades governed by regulations under the Provincial and Territorial Apprenticeship Acts (Red Seal Trades) are not eligible for the wage subsidy.

      Grant Criteria 
      The OVIN R&D Partnership Fund – Electric Vehicle (EV) Stream 2 provides co-investment funding of up to $1,000,000 to support the development, testing, validation, demonstration, and deployment of electric-vehicle and battery-focused technologies, covering light-duty vehicles, heavy trucks/buses, charging infrastructure, and intelligent-transport systems.Grant Value:Up to $1,000,000 per project over a maximum of 24 months. Requires a minimum 2:1 private-sector match (i.e., the applicant and/or private partners must cover at least two-thirds of total project costs). Note: This funding is a co-investment (non-repayable) grant. Eligible Applicants:Ontario-based SMEs (fewer than 500 full-time employees globally). Projects must be carried out in Ontario. Eligible partners can include other SMEs, large enterprises, academic institutions (as collaborators), municipalities, Indigenous communities, and not-for-profits/crown-corporations/transit authorities where relevant. Eligible Activities:Applied development, demonstration, testing, validation, and piloting of EV and battery technologies (e.g., electric powertrains, battery systems, charging infrastructure, hydrogen/alternative-fuel EVs, light-weighting, etc.) Deployment of early-stage EV or smart-mobility solutions (e.g., fleet electrification, charging systems, smart-mobility infrastructure, ITS, etc.) Activities must result in demonstrable, market-ready solutions that can be showcased in-Ontario (e.g., operational EVs, prototypes, pilot deployments) Program Details :Projects must occur within a 24-month timeframe. Private-sector match funds must be cash or eligible private investment; in-kind contributions are not sufficient to meet the match requirement. Applicants must sign a Contribution Agreement before incurring eligible expenses.Reporting requirements include financial, technical, and performance reports as outlined in the program guidelines.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Process Best Practices :The program requires applicants to provide at least two-thirds of total eligible project costs from private-sector sources, as OVIN will contribute up to one-third of eligible expenses, to a maximum of $1,000,000 per project;All matching funds must be cash contributions; in-kind contributions are not eligible toward the required match;Public funding from federal, provincial, municipal, or crown programs cannot be used to satisfy the mandatory private-sector matching requirement, although additional public funding may be used outside the match as long as total public support stays within allowable limits; andProjects must be completed within a maximum 24-month delivery window, and a Contribution Agreement must be executed prior to incurring eligible expenses.Eligible Best Practices :Only costs incurred after the submission of a fully completed application are eligible; retroactive expenses are not permitted under this stream;Applications must clearly disclose all confirmed and anticipated sources of project funding, including the applicant’s contribution and support from:Private-sector partners (required match);Industry associations, networks, or ecosystem partners;Academic or research collaborators;Municipal, regional, or Indigenous partners (permitted, but not toward the private-sector match).Applicants must ensure that no provincial, federal, or municipal public funding is counted toward the required two-thirds private-sector match, and that all combined public contributions remain within OVIN’s allowable funding thresholds;All project activities must take place in Ontario and demonstrate clear pathways toward the development, validation, demonstration, or deployment of EV and battery-related technologies.Links :Program Website : click hereProgram Guidelines : click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This provincial program helps SMEs in the advanced manufacturing sector invest in capital equipment, technology adoption, and skills development by funding 15% of the total project cost between $500,000 and $5,000,000, and by providing complementary services and support. In most cases, the funding comes as a loan, with no interest during the project period (up to four years). If investment and job/upskilling targets are met, up to 30% of the loan (up to $500,000) may be forgiven. For small companies located in rural areas, and for certain strategic projects, the funding may be awarded as a non-repayable grant. The goals of the program are to create jobs, attract private-sector investment, improve competitiveness, encourage innovation, and stimulate economic growth.Grant value:Loan portionUp to 15% of funding to a maximum of $5 million, interest-free during the project period (up to four years);If you achieve your investment and job or upskilling targets, up to 30% of the loan (to a maximum of $500,000) may be forgiven.Grant portionUp to 15% to a maximum of $500,000 for small companies in rural communities (less than 100 full-time employees and in a municipality of less than 100,000 people or a population density of 100 people per square kilometer or less.Up to 15% to a maximum of $1.5 million for strategic projects that are foreign direct investments or from companies competing against other jurisdictions or companies with significant reshoring projects.Turnaround Time: Notified July 22, 2025Eligible Applicants:For-profit businesses in the advanced manufacturing sector, including but not limited to the following sub-sectors:Aerospace;Automotive; Chemical;Information and Communications Technology;Life sciences; and/orSteel.Located in Ontario, or planning to locate in Ontario;Have at least 3 years of operations and financial statements;Employ at least 10 full-time equivalent employees;Committed to creating or upskilling at least 5 jobs; andAble to invest at least $500,000 in the project.Eligible Projects:Create jobs and build talent;Attract and encourage private sector investment;Help companies to adopt technologies to improve their competitiveness;Lead to business growth and broad positive economic impacts; andEncourage innovation, collaboration, and cluster development.Ineligible Projects:Ongoing operations including maintenance and capital replacement;Refinancing of existing business operations;Acquisitions and buyouts;Restructuring, or relocating to other jurisdictions within Ontario;Primary production;Retail;Construction (for example, residential development);Electricity generation;Waste management;Recycling.Eligible Expenses: Must be directly attributable to the project;Must be incurred and paid on or after the project start date identified in the funding agreement;Must be new investments to improve productivity, innovation, and growth, including:Project facilities and infrastructure;Equipment and machinery;One-time labour directly related to the project (ie: costs related to commissioning and/or setting up new equipment, technology, and systems for the project);Specialized labour directly related to the project (ie: research and development) for up to 2 years;Materials;Specialized expertise;Training and talent costs; andPermits and fees.Ineligible Expenses:Ongoing operational and production labour costs;Purchase of land and/or buildings;Costs associated with landscaping and staff parking lots;Purchase or lease of vehicles or other off-site equipment;Raw materials for commodity production;Preparation of funding proposal;Shareholder payments;Costs occurred outside Ontario, except purchases from suppliers;Mergers and acquisitions;Travel, hospitality, meal, and incidental expenses;Rebates, credit, or refund;Debt service; andMarketing, sales, or distribution costs. Program Details: To apply for AMIC funding, businesses must be registered on Transfer Payment Ontario (TPON);If you do not have a TPON account, you can create one using your CRA Business Number. Allow up to 5 business days for processing;Complete the Eligibility Checklist through TPON;Once the Eligibility Checklist is approved (usually within 3 business days), proceed to the application form;Include the following supporting documents with the application:A cash flow projection for the project period and loan repayment period (four years post-project completion date) showing sufficient detail for Ontario to assess the company's ability to repay the loan;Copy of articles of incorporation and/or patent letters;Corporate family tree showing parent company, affiliates, and related entities;Audited financial statements from the last three fiscal years;If audited statements are not available, contact an Ontario Government advisor; andLetters of support from project partners and financial institutions, ideally with financial commitments.If approved, applicants will enter into a funding agreement with the Government of Ontario. Funding will be disbursed after the applicant has met the disbursement conditions outlined in the agreement, including providing evidence of project financing and insurance;Successful applicants will be required to document project progress in detailed annual reports;If all investment and job creation targets are met, up to 30% of the loan may be forgiven;Funding may be issued as a non-repayable grant in the following cases:Small companies in rural areas with project budgets of $500,000; Projects with budgets of $1,500,000 that pursue one of the following strategic priorities:Foreign-direct investment;Competition with another jurisdiction;Significant reshoring.In addition to funding, successful applicants can access the following complementary supports:Advisory services, such as guidance on compliance approvals;Help with skills and talent;Health and safety support; andEnvironmental support.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:AMIC cannot be used in conjunction with other provincial funding;AMIC is not retroactive;Process Best Practices:Because the application process is quite competitive, applicants are encouraged to contact a provincial government advisor for help with their application; andProjects are assessed according to the following criteria:Alignment with the fund's goals of supporting advanced manufacturing in the province;Potential job creation and/or upskilling;The potential economic benefit to the province; andFeasibility.Forms:Program website: click hereProgram guidelines: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Regional Tariff Relief Initiative helps businesses and sectors negatively impacted by new tariffs from the U.S., China and/or Canadian counter-tariffs. The program aims to boost productivity, catalyze growth, and diversify markets by raising productivity, enhancing competitiveness, reducing costs to mitigate tariff impacts, and improving resiliency among Canadian businesses.Grant Value: Up to 50% of eligible project costs from $500,000 to $5 million per project for repayable funding; andUp to 50% up to  $1 million in non-repayable contribution funding for eligible.Turnaround Time: 90 days after submitting complete application.Eligible Applicants: Be an incorporated businesses conducting business in the Prairies;Have been viable prior to newly imposed tariffs by the U.S., China, and/or Canadian counter-tariffs and prior to March 21, 2025;Have at least 1 employee;Have been in operation for at least 2 years;Have staffed operating facilities in the Prairie provinces;Have at least 25% of your sales in the markets targeted by tariffs or are able to demonstrate having been directly negatively affected by the tariffs or the uncertainty they create. This could be demonstrated by:Higher cost of materials;Higher cost from suppliers;Higher retail cost of finished product;Fewer purchase orders or sales;Addition of an import or export tax;Loss of access to markets;Other proof of negative impact.If you are applying for non-repayable funding, you must also:Generate economic benefits for the local economy or region;Play an important role in supporting the local supply chain.Eligible Activities: Productivity improvement Including:Investing in digitization, automation, or technology to enhance business productivity and competitiveness; and Reshoring production, research & development operations, recruiting highly qualified personnel and expertise;Market expansion and diversification including:Developing and diversifying markets to help businesses find new customers; and Business support, market development and diversification, and guidance services.Strengthening supply chains and trade resilience including:Optimizing supply chain logistics and ensuring compliance with standards to gain market access and/or enhance sales;Strengthening domestic supply chains and facilitating internal trade to increase business resilience and reliability of domestic markets.Eligible Costs:Labour (wages and benefits) and material costs;Capital costs (machinery or equipment purchase);Consultancy fees (professional, advisory and technical services);Advisory expenses (planning, business information, counselling advisory services, coaching, mentoring or networking events, workshops or conference fees, fees for business training through business service organizations); Costs related to expanding or maintaining markets; andAll eligible costs must be incremental, reasonable and essential to carrying out eligible project activitiesIneligible Costs: RTRI funding does not support projects that move company operations outside of Canada;Basic and applied R&D (technology readiness levels 1-6);Land acquisition and goodwill;Salary bonuses and dividend payments;Entertainment and hospitality expenses;Refinancing of existing debts;Amortization or depreciation of assets;Purchase of assets for more than fair market value;Lobbying activities;Donations;Dues; andMembership fees.Program Details: Project activities can last up to 3 years and must be completed by March 31, 2028;Repayable contribution funding for businesses is normally repaid with no interest over 5 years in monthly instalments beginning 1 year after project end date;RTRI funding does not support projects that move company operations outside of Canada;Program requires an initial EOI to be submitted before being invited to submit a full application; andPriority will be given to activities that:Have higher proportions of Canadian inputs;Demonstrate greater economic benefits for the Prairies;Support local, regional or national supply chains.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Program allows for funding to be stacked up to 90% with other non Federal funding and prioritizes those that do so; Program may allow for retroactive funding for up to 12 months prior to receipt of signed funding request, but no earlier than March 21, 2025.Process Best Practices:Confirmed, at the time of application submission, other project funding sources including government and non-government;Applicants should consult with accountants and/or Canada Revenue Agency to understand how RTRI funding could affect taxes or other current or future funding agreements.Forms and Links:Program Webpage: click hereEOI application: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      Regional Tariff Response Initiative (RTRI) - Southern provides $125K-$10M in repayable funding or $125K-$1M non-repayable to southern Ontario incorporated businesses with 5-500 employees affected by trade disruptions and tariffs. Grant Value: Repayable contributions - up to 75% ($125K-$10M)Non-repayable contributions - up to 50% ($125K-$1M)Up to 100% for Indigenous applicants.Turnaround Time : Pending.Eligible Applicants:Business located and operating in southern Ontario;Be an incorporated, for-profit business (including Indigenous-owned businesses) registered in Canada or Ontario for at least 3 years;Must employ at least 5 full-time equivalent (FTE) employees in southern Ontario, and fewer than 500 FTE employees overall;Must have been viable before the US/CHINA tariffs took effect (before March 21, 2025);Businesses must meet at least one of the following criteria: At least 25% of sales are in markets targeted by the tariffs; ORDemonstrate direct negative impacts such as:Increased production material costs;Increased cost of finished products;Import/export tariffs;Decline in revenue or market access;Employment impacts (layoffs, hiring freezes, etc.);Other documented evidence of negative impact.Eligible Target Markets:Must specify whether markets are regional, national, or international;Must explain how the business serves its customers;Applicants must articulate how their project will:Diversify the markets they serve;Expand into new Canadian or international markets;Reduce exposure to tariff-affected markets; andStrengthen competitive position and increase market share.Eligible ActivitiesDigitizing, automating, adopting/adapting technologies to boost productivity;Market development, diagnostics, expansion (including trade missions);Strengthening supply chains, building strategic partnerships, and compliance upgrades;Activities supporting domestic supply chain resilience and internal trade;Business support, advisory, or market development activities; andReshoring/onshoring production, R&D, or personnel to southern Ontario. Ineligible Activities:Land or real estate purchases, including buildings;Entertainment and hospitality expenses;Motor vehicle purchases, leases, or operational costs;Refinancing existing debt or covering ongoing operational/production costs unrelated to the project;Non-incremental or unreasonable costs, or costs not directly related to eligible project activities;Costs incurred before March 21, 2025 (not eligible).Program Details:Businesses may request either:Repayable contribution;Non-repayable contribution (available only once per business for this initiative).For Non-repayable ($125,000 – $1,000,000), applicants must demonstrate strong economic benefits for the region;Indigenous businesses have tailored provisions (e.g., up to 100% funding coverage);If the applicant has an existing FedDev project, the RTRI project must be distinct;Priority for Non-repayable Funding Based on :Business operates in the region where funding is requested;Business is Canadian-owned;Being able to finish the project on time;Can secure some funding from non-government sources;Work in a sector strongly affected by tariffs;Provides economic benefits to the local community;Prefers to buy Canadian-made goods or use domestic suppliers.Mandatory Attachments:Financial statements (last 2 fiscal years, externally prepared);Most recent interim financial statements;Articles of incorporation/amendments / constituting documents;Supplementary Form;Work plan or project schedule, showing activities, milestones, and detailed budget.Additional documents (required depending on project type):Intellectual Property (IP) strategy (mandatory for IP-intensive firms);Financial projections for 3–5 years;Company structure diagram;Any documents demonstrating:Tariff impacts (e.g., cost increases, lost contracts, revenue decline);Market impacts or opportunities;Sales in affected markets. 

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Total government assistance cannot exceed 90% of eligible costs;In-kind contributions are NOT eligible as matched funding;Retroactive costs allowed up to 12 months prior to application receipt, but not earlier than March 21, 2025;Process Best Practices:Applicants should first complete the self-screening step before applying;Only one application allowed at a time across all FedDev programs;Project must end by March 31, 2028;Funding is reimbursed based on approved costs incurred during the project;Projects are assessed againt the following criteria :Extent of tariff impacts on the company or sector and the project’s contribution to new or expanded initiatives;Potential to improve productivity, drive growth, or diversify markets;Strength of expected results, project plan, budget, readiness, and organizational capacity, including ability to repay;Quality of risk mitigation measures and, where applicable, the IP strategy.Forms and Links:Program Webpage: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This regional program funds primary food producers to trial and transition to climate-resilient food crop varieties that can be produced on a commercial scale and have not been widely grown or tested in their area. The aim of the program is to reduce climate-related production risk, improve crop resilience, and strengthen local and regional food systems.Grant Value: Up to $15,000 per approved project.Turnaround Time:The program does not have a fixed turnaround time for processing applications. Review timelines depend on the volume of applications received and available funding.Eligible Applicants:Primary food producers that:have been in commercial operation for a minimum of two years;can provide a T2042 Statement of Farming Activities or a corporation income statement for 2024 and an estimate of 2025 revenues;have a minimum of $50,000 in average annual revenues per year over the past two years;have a WorkSafeBC account in good standing, if employing staff; are a taxable entity with a GST number and business number;If incorporated, should be in good standing with the BC Corporate Registry; adhere to all applicable labour laws; andintend to apply or have applied to other available federal, provincial, local and/or industry funding programs and/or rebates.Ineligible Applicants:Non-producers;Organizations or individuals not engaged in primary food production; andApplicants outside the eligible geographic area.Eligible Activities:Trialing new or alternative climate-resilient food crop varieties;On-farm testing and evaluation of crop performance;Small-scale commercial production trials;       Grant Criteria 
      Free digital twin technology training (valued at $15,000) for Ontario-based Agriculture, Food/Beverage Processing, Clean Tech, and Manufacturing businesses ready to implement advanced simulation and modelling technology in their operations.  Turnaround Time: Approximately 2-3 weeks.Grant Value:  Free training and Licence estimated at $15,000 CAD per participating company;$2,000 stipend to offset the cost of wages during the training (the funding for this stipend has been exhausted for 2026 intake).Eligible Applicants:Must be a Canadian or Ontario-registered business operating in the Agriculture or Food/Beverage Processing sector (related businesses may also qualify);Must operate in one of four eligible sectors: Agriculture;Food and Beverage Processing;Clean Technology; andManufacturing. The business must have operating facilities in Ontario (with some limited seats available for businesses outside Ontario);Leadership team must be willing and able to participate in all training sessions- Company must demonstrate readiness to implement digital twin technology;Business must have operational processes suitable for digital twin applications (simulation, modeling, optimization). Eligible Trainees:Leadership team members (owners, executives, senior management);Operations managers and production supervisors;IT/Technology leads responsible for implementation;Project managers overseeing digital transformation initiatives;Multiple team members from the same organization can participate;Trainees must commit to attending all scheduled training sessions;Participants must be authorized to make technology implementation decisions. Eligible Training: Digital twin technology fundamentals and applications;Advanced simulation and modelling techniques;Process optimization using digital twin platforms;Hands-on training with Plataine's digital twin software;Implementation planning and strategy development;Data integration and system connectivity;Real-world case studies and sector-specific applications;Practical workshops focused on applying digital twins to business operations; andOngoing technical support and implementation guidance throughout the cohort period. Eligible Training Provider:Plataine (primary digital twin technology provider and training delivery partner);Ontario Chamber of Commerce (program administrator and delivery partner); andExpert trainers and technical specialists are affiliated with the program. Program Details:Free training plus a one-year Unity software license and access to the Unity Hub learning library (including over 400 self-paced learning activities);Cohort-Based Learning (First-Come, First-Served);Training covers digital twin topics like :  Improving CAD files so they work smoothly in digital tools;Connecting live data so systems update in real time;Accessing 3D environments online and modelling real-world settings remotely;C# programming;Building practical tools like product configurators, interactive demos, and real-time building management systems.12-week online program with live weekly classes plus self-paced learning (Total 120 hour commitment based on 10 hrs/week x 12 weeks);The program value includes:access to Plataine's digital twin technology platform during the training period;Expert-led training sessions and workshops;Hands-on implementation support and technical guidance; and Ongoing access to program resources and community.Employers must support participants in achieving a positive employment outcome within six months after training (e.g., change in job duties, title, or compensation);Technical prerequisites include access to a computer with Windows 10, 11; macOS 11+, 8GB RAM,  at least 15 GB of free storage space ,  dedicated graphics card. Hardware upgrades may be needed for successful participation;Possibility to access The Talent Opportunities Program (TOP) with subsidies of up to 50% of the wages -to a maximum of $5,000- for each ‘net new’ placement.Employer Stipend Funding (for Wage Offset) is now exhausted for 2026 applications. - There was not context to this, had to look the guidelines to figure out what this was (see notes above on how to input)

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Possibility to apply for multiple team members (leadership, operations, IT, project managers) to better support outcomes;Apply with a clear business problem or improvement idea in mind so the training can be directly applied to real work and deliver meaningful results.There is a $2,000 non-completion penalty per employee if the participant does not complete the program. This requires strategic candidate selection and schedule commitment planning;Participants are expected to receive one positive career advancement opportunity from their employer within 6 months post-completion. This includes a change in job description/responsibilities (including new responsibilities associated to advancement track), change in title, or change in compensation.Process Best Practices:Early applications are highly advised. Cohorts have limited spaces and fill on a first-come, first-served basis; waitlists may apply;Confirm leadership availability before applying: all participants must attend every scheduled sessions;Show operational readiness: applications are favoured when clear, well-defined processes are in place;The program focuses on practical, real-world implementation;Planning for post-program costs (training is free, but software or implementation costs may follow).Forms: Program Website: click hereProgram Guidelines: click hereRegistration Link: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This is a wage incentive program that offers up to $25,000 of funding to Nova Scotian employers with a labour need that are looking for support to offset the cost of hiring, training, or equipping a new employee to succeed in a permanent position. The amount of financial support made available through START is assessed by Employment Nova Scotia (ENS) on a case-by-case basis. The intent is to help Nova Scotians find meaningful long-term employment while helping employers attract the talent they need.Grant Value: $25,000Turnaround Time: up to 3 weeksEligible Employers:Private-sector, government-funded, non-profit, or charitable organization, social enterprise or a municipality;Have workplace accident/injury insurance coverage for employees;Have business locations in Nova Scotia; andI.e.; Companies with headquarters outside of Nova Scotia are eligible if they also have a physical location in Nova Scotia.Have the capacity to supervise and develop the participants.Note: The program prioritizes assisting small and medium enterprises with fewer than 500 staff.Eligible Candidates:Unemployed and actively seeking full time or increasing employment;A resident of Nova Scotia;Canadian citizens or permanent residents who are legally entitled to work in Canada.Participants may self-identify as:Mi’kmaq or Indigenous; Recent graduates (within the last three years);Persons with disabilities;Recent immigrants (within the last three years);African Nova Scotians;Visible minority (including Persons of African Descent);Acadian and francophone Nova Scotians; orIncome assistance recipients.Unemployed international graduates who meet the following requirements are eligible:Must have graduated from a Nova Scotia (NS) public or private post-secondary institution;Note: not all programs of study authorized by private institutions are eligible for START;Graduates must have studied in NS to obtain a Canadian post-secondary credential that
requires at least 2 academic years of study.The participant must have a valid post-graduate work permit;The occupation must be a NOC (National Occupational Classification) code O, A or B (professional occupations);The position funded through START must be available for a minimum duration of one year.Family members are eligible if the participant is in an underrepresented group and the employer has conducted a fair hiring process.Eligible Expenses:Salary and mandatory payroll deduction costs of a new hire;Training costs of a new hire (1 price quote is required); orEquipment and/or miscellaneous costs of a new hire (2 price quotes are required).Program Details:1 employee per application;Employers can submit only 1 application for START;Exceptions may be granted on a case-by-case basis.The full wage must be paid to the participant including the payment of mandatory and voluntary payroll deductions;Minimum of 30 hours per week:Exception: 15 hours per week may be considered for:Recently established small businesses creating a part-time position which will develop into a full-time position;Cases where special accommodations need to be considered for Persons with
Disabilities; orCases where this level of employment is the norm for the industry.Employers will be required to provide feedback to Employment Nova Scotia on how participants are progressing and the impact of the program on your business;Employers can hire more than one individual through START on a case-by-case basis; andEmployers can reapply to the grant for additional funding 6 months after the end date of your current agreement.Ineligible Employment:Paid strictly on a commission basis, or by the kilometre;Already funded through the Labour Market Development Agreement
(LMDA), Workforce Development Agreement (WDA), or through Department of Community
Services (DCS);Displacing current employees, or those on layoff, vacation,
maternity/parental, or sick leave; andSummer employment.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:This program cannot be used in conjunction with other hiring programs;Ordinarily, the program does not provide retroactive funding, but exceptions may be made in some cases.Written approval must be given by the program for hires made pre-approval to be eligible for funding;Process Best Practices:Early Termination: If an employee is terminated, quits or is unable to continue in the position:Employer must contact ENS immediately (within a 2 business days);Assessment will be made based on the time elapsed, funds issued and reason for leaving, to determine if the employer will be required to reimburse Employment Nova Scotia;Employers with unsafe working conditions or who terminate employees hired under the START program without just cause will be required to return funds paid by ENS.Forms:Program website: click hereApplication portal: click here
