      Grant Criteria 
      The Strategic Energy Management for Industry program (SEMI) helps industrial and manufacturing facilities improve their energy performance by offering co-funding  up to $1.4 million to implement an integrated system of practices, processes and capital retrofits.Grant Value: Energy Assessments and Audits: Up to $50,000;Strategic Energy Management (SEM): Up to $100,000;Energy Management Information Systems: Up to $50,000 for facility energy consumption less than 400,000 GJ;Up to $250,000 for facility energy consumption more than 400,000 GJ.Capital Retrofits up to $1,000,000.NOTE: SEMI offers financial incentives that cover up to 50% of eligible project costs for for-profts and up to 100% for non-profits.Turnaround Time: Up to 30 days. Eligible Applicants:Be one of the following:Corporation;Non-profit;Co-operative;Sole proprietorship;Partnership;Government or public entity;Indigenous owned-organization.Operates a business with facilities located in Alberta.Eligible Activities:Facility Readiness Assessment:The FRA provides a facility wide-assessment of how, where, and when energy is used in the production process;Provide an energy assessment;Identify opportunities for improvement;Define a path forward in SEMI.Comprehensive Energy Studies:After completing the FRA, facilities may proceed with more detailed studies which can include:Comprehensive Energy Assessment;Computational Fluid Dynamics Studies;Process integration.Strategic Energy Management:SEM supports
facilities in developing and implementing long-term energy
management plans that align with their business objectives;Setting Clear Goals;Engaging Employees; andContinuous Monitoring.Energy Management Information Systems:EMIS activities include hardware and
software components that support:Data Collection and Monitoring;Analysis and Optimization;Reporting and Decision Making.Capital Retrofits:Capital retrofits are essential for implementing the energy-saving
measures identified through energy assessments or studies and
supported by SEM and EMIS. Examples include:Equipment Upgrades;Renewable Energy;Process Improvements.Program Details:First step in SEMI is to complete a facility readiness assessment(FRA) at the chosen facility;After completing the FRA facilities can proceed with more detailed projects including:Comprehensive Energy Studies;Strategic Energy Management; orEnergy Management Information systems.Once one of these is complete the the FRA will provide additional insight to support capital retrofits. Eligible Facilities:Industrial, commercial, or manufacturing facilities that must be located in Alberta;The facility has been in operation for at least one year with fixed equipment and energy consumption information;Must own or lease the facility (for leased you have gotten permission from landlord to undertake activities);The facility belongs to one of the following North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) economic sectors:Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing and Hunting;Mining, Oil and Gas;Utilities;Construction;Manufacturing;Transportation; and Services and Waste Management.

The goals of the program are to increase the number of viable businesses owned by Aboriginal Canadians in the Coast Salish area, to cultivate a culture of entrepreneurship in the Aboriginal community, and to increase access to capital for Aboriginal businesses. Grant Value:Up to $99,999 for individual businesses;Up to $250,000 for community-owned businesses.Turnaround Time: 6 weeksEligible Applicants:Canadian Aboriginal individuals (Status or Non-Status, Métis, Inuk) residing in the TACC service area, which includes:Lower Mainland (to Squamish);Fraser Valley; andVancouver Island.*Canadian corporations, partnerships, associations, or other legal entities majority owned and controlled by Aboriginal individuals residing in the TACC service area;Applicant must be involved full-time in a management capacity in the proposed business project, and must possess the relevant certifications, qualifications, and/or licenses; andApplicant must be able to contribute at least 15% of the total project cost.  *Note: Northern BC, Central BC, and some parts of Vancouver Island are not included in TACC's service area, but TACC will refer applicants to other Aboriginal Financial Institutions as necessary. If your business falls outside of TACC's service area, you can access similar programming through the AFI that serves your region. Eligible Projects: Projects may involve starting, purchasing, expanding, or modernizing a business, and must create measurable benefits, including but not limited to additional revenue, new markets, and/or new job opportunities;Eligible market expansion activities include advertising campaigns, trade shows, seminars, and conferences;Eligible innovation activities include research, process and product development, productivity improvement, and investment in new technology and/or systems;The minimum project budget for starting, purchasing, expanding, or modernizing a business is $25,000; andThe minimum project budget for marketing and innovation is $10,000. Ineligible Projects:Community infrastructure projects that are unrelated to commercial enterprise;Purchase of land, buildings, and/or investment property; andBusiness activity related to pawn shops, payday loan firms, gaming operations, and/or the production/distribution of alcohol, tobacco, and sexually exploitative materials.Program Details:BEP contribution levels vary depending on the type of project the applicant submits. Higher contribution levels (60-75%) are available for business planning and market expansion activities. Capital projects (including equipment purchase, start-ups, and acquisition) typically qualify for a 25% non-repayable contribution through BEP, but may receive additional fundsthrough the  First Citizen's Fund or the NRT Equity Match grant; The First Citizen's Fund offers loans with a 40% forgiveness portion. All Indigenous entrepreneurs (Status, non-status, Métis, Inuit) can borrow a lifetime maximum of $75,000 from this fund. Applicants who have not already exhausted their First Citizen's Fund allowance can combine it with a BEP contribution;The New Relationship Trust (NRT) Equity Match Grant is offered in conjunction with TACC's other programs and is available to Indigenous entrepreneurs who are members of a BC First Nation, and who live in the TACC service area. The Equity Match Grant is a non-repayable contribution of up to $5000 that reduces the amount of cash equity the applicant has to provide to receive a BEP contribution.TACC will determine whether BEP applicants are eligible for a First Citizen's Fund loan and/or an Equity Match Grant;Combining all three programs significantly increases the non-repayable portion of the funding, but applicants who do not qualify for the additional programs can still receive a non-repayable contribution through BEP.There is one application form for all types of projects (business planning, market expansion, and capital). The  form requires the applicant's business information, a description of their project, a summary of their  business experience, an approximate budget, and the following supporting documents:Evidence of Aboriginal ancestry;Evidence of identity;Resume;Evidence of sufficient cash equity to undertake the project;Letters of commitment from other funders;Financial statements from the last three years (for projects related to existing businesses);Projected financial statements for the next three years;Copies of partnership agreements or incorporation documents;Business plan, if available; andAny additional information supporting the proposal (ie: market studies).Applications are reviewed within 10 business days, and are deemed eligible, ineligible, or sent back to the applicant with a request for more information;Eligible projects can proceed to the next stage in the application process, in which the applicant submits a detailed business plan;TACC provides a template for business plans, but can also issue funding to cover up to 75% of legal, accounting, and/or consulting fees related to the development of the plan;The business plan will be assessed within 30 business days; if approved, TACC will issue a Letter of Offer, outlining the amount and terms of the funding; Each funding agreement is unique, but typical contribution levels for various project costs are outlined in the table below; andProject financials and performance may be monitored for up to three years after the agreement is signed.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:This funding can be combined with other provincial and/or federal funding programs;BEP will not fund project costs retroactively; applicants are advised not to commit any project costs before finalizing the funding agreement with TACC; andCredit rating is an important factor in the eligibility assessment; applicants are encouraged to seek a credit report before applying. Forms:Program website: click hereProgram guidelines: click hereApplication form: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This program provides a wage subsidy of up to $7,000 for internships for employers operating in any industry sector. Up to 70% of the new employee’s salary is offered for post-secondary students where a work placement is part of their study plan. The program aims to help to bridge the gap between formal post-secondary learning and the skill requirements of Canadian employers.Grant Value:50% of wages up to $5000 per regular participant;70% of wages up to $7,000 per participant in any of the following under-represented groups:Women in STEM or business;Indigenous students;Visible minorities;Recent immigrants (immigrated to Canada within the last 5 years);Persons with disabilities;First-year students;Students on their first work term. Turnaround Time: 15 business daysEligible Employers:Be a registered Canadian business or non-profit;Have Workplace Safety and Insurance Board (WSIB) or alternate workplace insurance coverage;Committed to paying the student for the role for the duration of the placement in full;In compliance with all federal and provincial human rights and labour legislation, regulations, and any other relevant standards including the Occupational Health and Safety Act and the Employment Standards Act;Employers in all industries may apply; andMust place participants on payroll (must make CPP, EI, and vacation pay contributions).Ineligible Employers:Federal, provincial, territorial or municipal governments;Crown corporations;Hospitals;Post-secondary institutions; andMajor financial sector employers.Eligible Candidates:Registered as a full- or part-time domestic student in a recognized Canadian post-secondary institution;Master's or PhD students are eligible;International students are ineligible.Registered in any program of study;Canadian citizens, permanent residents, or protected persons;Registered in a class with work-integrated learning (WIL) component as part of their study plan;Must send a signed document from the post-secondary institution indicating the student is registered in a program/course where a work-integrated learning component is part of their study plan (e.g. co-op document, letter, etc.);Ideally, the documents should state the school term, the program enrolled, start and end dates,  etc; andTranscripts are generally not acceptable.Cannot be a family member of the employer; andCannot be part of another Student Work Placement Program simultaneously.Note: Apprenticeships are ineligible for program funding.Placement Details:Wage subsidy will apply to gross wages between:Winter 2025 - January 1, 2025, to April 30, 2025: No funding AvailableSummer 2025 - May 1, 2025 to August 31, 2025: CLOSEDFall 2025 - September 1, 2025 to December 31, 2025: OPENFull-time or part-time;Eligible forms of Work-Integration Learning:Internships;Field placements;Part-time/short-term intensive hands-on practical experience in a setting relevant to their subject of study.Co-operative education;Alternating academic terms and paid work terms.Apprenticeships;Note: Apprenticeships in a skilled trade are not eligible under this program;Community and industry research/projects;Research that occurs primarily in workplaces, includes consulting projects, design projects, and community-based research projects.Entrepreneurship;Engage in the early-stage development of business start-ups and/or to advance external ideas that address real-world needs for academic credit.Mandatory practicum/clinic placement; andWork experience under the supervision of an experienced registered or licensed professional (e.g. preceptor) in any discipline that requires practice-based work experience for professional licensure or certification.Community service-learning.Meaningful community service with classroom instruction and critical reflection to enrich the learning experience and strengthen communities.No maximum participants per company;Placements must be "net new," meaning that the SWPP student is incremental to the employer's "baseline" of student hires. An employer's "baseline" is the number of students they hired without SWPP support the year prior to participating in SWPP;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2022, 2023, or 2024, use the number of students hired in the year prior to that first time you accessed SWPP support;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2024, use the number of students hired in 2023;Net new baselines must be calculated each year (if you participate in SWPP every year, your net new baseline will increase accordingly).Include co-op and non-co-op students in your initial baseline calculation. Do not include high school students, recent graduates, or international students, as they are not included in the SWPP program;If a student placement crosses over the fiscal year (ie: January - April), they count toward the earlier fiscal year;If you hire a student for separate placements in different fiscal years (ie: Summer 2022, Summer 2023), you must count them in both fiscal years.Work from home placements are eligible;Placements will be counted in the term they start in;Employers can still receive funding for placements with start dates outside the academic term; andEmployers cannot postpone placements and will need to ensure placement(s) occur before the agreement end date or request an agreement extension.

The greater focus will be placed on projects that aim to reach product commercialization within their allotted timeframe. Grant Value: Grant value is set at $4.1 million however this is the average across Protein Industries Canada programs as there is no set maximum a project can receive however the program will reimburse up to 45% of eligible costsTurnaround Time: Approximately 6-8 weeks.Eligible Applicants: Applicants must be a member of Protein Industries Canada;Must be a consortium of a minimum 3 Protein Industries Canada members, at least one of which is a Small or Medium Enterprise with 499 or fewer employees;Each member of the consortium must contribute to the project in a meaningful way;At least 2 members of the consortium must contribute financially to the project;A consortium may include academic or research institution(s). Not mandatory but encouraged;At least two partners must be Canadian companies or multi-national corporation that are legally entitled to do business in Canada with a significant Canadian business operation; andAt least one consortium member should represent a target customer or user of the new technology solution.Program Details: This call has a focus on ingredient processing and selling at every point in the value chain;Areas of investment include: Genetics (15%) - germplasm development with an aim to improve processing efficiency, quality, sensory qualities and the development of novel ingredients:Improved protein content, quality, sensory qualities, functionality and/or nutritional profile;Improved co-product quality, functionality and/or nutritional profile;Reduced anti-nutritional factors;Improved efficiency of protein extraction and/or crop fractionation; andIncreased availability of supply for emerging field crops.Crops (10%) - technologies to measure and improve on-farm sustainability and information flow along the value chain: Systems that support the measurement, verification and reporting of traceability / chain of
custody, sustainability and food safety of Canadian crops and ingredientsIngredients (50%) - the development, scaling and optimization of plant-based ingredients:Testing and scaling of new and novel ingredient manufacturing processes;Improved rates of protein extraction and nutrient density;Reduced water and energy requirements in ingredient manufacturing processes;Optimized ingredient manufacturing processes for Canadian crops and Canadian conditions;The development of new and novel ingredients and co-products from Canadian crops; andImproved processing efficiency in the manufacturing of plant-based ingredients. Products (25%) - the conversion of Canadian-made ingredients and co-products into the consumption-ready goods: The creation and commercialization of consumer-ready food products that align with consumer needs, expectations and trends, including clean-label, sustainable and nutritious products;The creation and commercialization of value-added animal feed products; andThe creation and commercialization of new industrial bio-products derived from the co-products of protein extraction and ingredient manufacturing.Technology program projects are required to document an IP rationale as part of their project proposals (template will be given to applicants submitting a project application;All applications will also be required to report on the IP assets generated by their project; andPrior to signing the final Master Project Agreement every member of the consortium will be required to complete a detailed financial assessment, including submitting the last two years of accountant-prepared financial statements and their current organizational structure.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:The program does not fund retroactively;This program can be stacked with other funding sources;The project cannot be a "designated project" or a "project" under the applicable federal environmental and impact assessment legislation;2 members must contribute financially to the project; Process Best Practices:Applicants must be a member of Protein Industries Canada; andPrior to signing the final Master Project Agreement every member of the consortium will be required to complete a detailed financial assessment, including submitting the last two years of accountant-prepared financial statements and their current organizational structure.Forms & Links: Program Webpage: click here.Program Guidelines: click here.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Training-on-the-Job program provides a subsidy for training wages to employers for up to 9 months coverage worth up to 100% of the cost of hiring an individual who is no longer able to return to their regular job and employer due to a workplace injury.Grant Value:Negotiated amount up to 100%Note: While the grant value above is noted at $0, it is because the rate fluctuates per applicant.Turnaround Time: 2 weeksEligible Applicants:Willing to hire a new employee for a permanent position;Have WCB Alberta coverage unless their industry is exempt. (in that case we can do a work assessment)Eligible Trainees:Must be a registered individual with WCB Alberta;Has endured a permanent workplace injury and are experiencing a barrier to employment;May be located within or outside of Alberta at the time of hire.Program Details:The percentages of reimbursement vary and depends on the related skills and abilities the new employee brings to the position;Amounts are negotiated with the case manager or service provider. In addition to wage subsidy, WCB may also provide support with: Coordination and cost coverage of external courses and training if required.Arrangement and cost coverage of ergonomic assessments and workplace modifications that may be needed; andThe cost of any adaptive equipment needed for the new hire to carry out the required tasks.Albertan business will receive WCB protection for the costs of any injury or re-injury that might occur during the program;Canadian businesses outside of Alberta will need to demonstrate other insurance;Employers receive support with prescreening and recruitment of the new hire; andEmployers who are seeking assistance with bringing a permanently injured worker back to work may consider the Workplace Assessment (WA) stream of the TOJ program;WA is designed to help the employee learn new skills outside of their date-of-accident position;Employers receive assistance in: Developing a suitable training plan (if applicable);Coordinating external training, job coaching, or ergonomic assessments (if applicable); andReceive a subsidy for training wages on a declining scale.For a 9 month WA period, WCB-Alberta could subsidize:1st two months at 100%;3rd and 4th months at 75%;5th and 6th month at 50%; and The last 3 months at 25%.This is negotiable and should reflect the skills the worker is expected to learn over the training period and
as per the training plan when applicable.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:WCB often seeks entry-level jobs that provide workers with room for growth (i.e. sedentary and light entry-level positions usually work best).Process Best Practices:For a faster application, employers are recommended to contact a WCB representative at TOJ@wcb.ab.ca to discuss the position they are looking to fill; andIf an employer does not have WCB coverage and does not belongs to a WCB mandatory industry, they can apply for a Workplace Assessment.Forms:Program website: click hereApplication portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This program offers funding of up to 50% of eligible expenses to a maximum of $250,000 for projects that are aimed at commercializing products or processes in a variety of key economic sectors including food processing, life sciences, manufacturing, digital arts and culture, and more. The goal of the program is to help eligible organizations commercialize the results of university or public research in a new market outside Quebec.Grant Value: Up to $250,000 per projectUp to 50% of eligible expenses for priority sectors; and Up to 35% of eligible expenses for strategic sectors.Turnaround Time: around 3-4 months.Eligible Applicants:Incorporated for-profit businesses;Social enterprises and non-profits organizations (NPOs);Co-ops;Headquartered and registered in Quebec City, Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures or L-Ancienne-Lorette;Has a product or process that has reached the commercialization phase; The first significant sale of the product/process is expected approximately within 24 months;Has proof of a) ownership of the intellectual property, or b) of the rights of exclusive use of the selected product or process; ANDOperates in one of the following priority sectors; ORAgri-food, food processing and healthy foods;Digital arts and interactive entertainment, financial technologies, artificial intelligence, smart city or other digital products and technologies (excluding services and consulting);Optics-photonics, advanced electronics, measurement and control technologies;Life sciences, biotechnologies, and health technologies;Clean technologies: water, air, soil treatment, eco-mobility, energy efficiency, renewable energies, green chemistry, residual materials, enabling technologies and sustainable development.Operates in one of the following strategic sectors:Arts, culture and heritage;Insurance and financial services;Shops located on commercial arteries;Manufacturing, materials, industrial processing, robotics and industry 4.0;Urban security; andTourism.Ineligible Applicants:Social enterprises, NPOs, and co-ops that do not demonstrate sound democratic governance;Applicants who have not been discharged from a bankruptcy judgment; andApplicants who have outstanding debts with the City of Quebec.Eligible Expenses:Professional fees, consulting services, and studies;Costs and working capital necessary for the implementation of the project;Salaries for human resources assigned to the project at an hourly rate; andPurchase or rental of goods, equipment, and assets related to the project.Ineligible Expenses:Funding for regular business operations;Financing of charitable activities and payment for volunteers;Payment of a debt or the repayment of existing loans;Replacement of government support or existing programs;Expenses incurred before the date of submission of a complete application;Any expense relating to the relocation of a business or part of its production outside the agglomeration of Quebec, unless the City of Quebec consents in writing; andFederal and provincial taxes (GST and QST).Project Details:Projects must be carried out as part of a structured commercialization plan aimed at growth and improving profitability;The location of the project is not restricted to the agglomeration of Quebec though the company must still be headquartered there; Projects must support an applicant's goal of commercializing the results of university or public research, or to commercialize in a market outside of Quebec, the results of R&D developed in the private sector; Projects developed through this program cannot be supported by the "Vitrine Technologique" program as well, since pre-commercial validation must be completed before submitting an application to the Valo-Capitale program; Ineligible projects include those that are discriminatory, controversial or that risk creating a negative image for the City of Quebec;One-time projects of an event nature are also ineligible.Assessment Criteria:Quality and soundness of the business model;Financial capacity of the applicant to complete the project and achieve its objectives;Viability and coherence of the submitted project (relevance of the project, viability of the financial plan, and strength of  the partners involved);Organizational management capacity;Distinctive and innovative character of the project;Economic benefits and impact on employment in the agglomeration of Quebec;Demonstration of the need for financial assistance;Innovative nature of the product or process;Market potential of the product or process; andSupport structure.

      Grant Criteria 
      This federal program offers salary subsidies to employers who hire full- or part-time post-secondary students for positions in manufacturing and manufacturing-related industries. The intention of the grant is to effectively align the work-ready skills of students with the skills required by Canada's manufacturers. The government is supporting new hires in this industry sector by offering a 70% matching wage subsidy to employers. The intent of the program is to support the current business needs of employers while helping students gain exposure to the work environment.Grant Value: (net new requirement - see Program Details section below): 50% of wages up to $5,000 for regular participants70% of wages up to $7,000 for underrepresented participantsTurnaround time: 10 business daysEligible Employers:A registered Canadian business or organization;Not-for-profit and charitable organizations that support Canada's manufacturing and related sectors are eligible;Be in manufacturing and related sectors (e.g., North American Industry Classification -NAICS codes 31-33);Provide Workplace Safety and Insurance Board (WSIB) or alternate workplace insurance coverage for the student employee;Financially capable to hire a student for a part-or full-time work term, pay them consistently, and provide a meaningful work experience;Not a federal or provincial government organization; andMust have participants on payroll (includes, Federal/Provincial tax deductions such as CPP, EI, etc.).Eligible Participants:Full-time or part-time post-secondary students in any field;Be in a recognized publicly-funded post-secondary institution;Students must be enrolled in the Summer semester to be eligible for summer placement funding.Be enrolled in a program or course where a work placement is part of the study plan;Canadian citizens, permanent residents or protected persons; andLegally entitled to work in Canada in accordance with relevant provincial or territorial legislation and regulations.Underrepresented groups:Women studying in STEM (science, technology, engineering, mathematics);First-year students;Recent immigrants (within last 5 years);Indigenous people;Visible Minorities; andPersons with disabilities.Traditional apprentices are ineligible.Note: The placement roles must be relevant to their field of study and must be validated by the post-secondary institution.Program Details:Program intakes:Winter 2025 - January 1, 2025 to March 31, 2025: CLOSEDSummer 2025 - May 1, 2025 to August 31, 2025: CLOSEDFall 2025 - September 1, 2025 to December 31, 2025: Opening July 28, 2025.Full- or part-time positions;Duration: 6 - 16 weeks;Positions can be directly or indirectly related to manufacturing (e.g. human resources, finance, graphic design, I.T., etc.);Co-op placements, mentorship programs, practicums, applied research projects, and internships are eligible under this program;Must meet the net new requirement:Employers must demonstrate a projected increase in the number of students hired in their “baseline year” compared to the number of students they plan to hire in the current fiscal year;The“baseline year” is the fiscal year BEFORE first participating in the SWPP through any delivery partner.Traditional apprentice positions are not supported by the WILWorks program;Back-to-back placements for the same student are eligible;Employers can receive funding for more than one student per term. However, employers must submit one application per student placement;The recruitment, interviewing, and selection of the student to fill eligible WILWorks positions is done by the employer;The final subsidy amount as calculated by EMC will be determined at the end of the placement pending receipt of the employer's and student's Exit Surveys and the student's first and final pay stub; andEMC retains the right to conduct on-site employer visits and/or video calls to ensure the placement is as described in the employer's application and that all contractual obligations are being met.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:This program cannot be used in conjunction with other federal government-funded programs, though provincial/territorial/municipal sources are permitted;This program allows for retroactive placement funding;For recruitment, employers are encouraged to use usual recruitment channels to hire or contact the region's postsecondary institutions and contact their Coop/Career Services department;EMC could also connect employers to post secondary institutions in the applicant's region or with programs aligned to the hiring needs to support the recruitment efforts.Underrepresented groups are encouraged to apply; andWomen in STEM, first-year students, recent immigrants (<5 years), Indigenous people and persons with disabilities.Placement employment agreements are between the student and the employer. EMC is not a party to these agreements and assumes no financial or legal responsibility with regard to events or actions by either party that affect the employment situation for any student (e.g. layoffs, intellectual property issues, confidentiality agreements, strikes, etc.).Program website: click hereEmployer FAQ: click hereTerms & Conditions: click hereApplication portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This highly demanded provincial program offers employers a maximum of $12,000 salary subsidy to hire new employees, and provide on-the-job training and the possibility for long-term employment. It is intended to provide British Columbians with work opportunities to increase productivity and build a stable and competitive economy.Grant Value:Regular stream: Up to a maximum of $7,200 over 24 weeks1st 8 weeks: 50% subsidy up to $500/week2nd 8 weeks: 25% subsidy up to $250/weekFinal 8 weeks: 15% subsidy up to $150/weekPriority stream: Up to a maximum of $12,000 over 24 weeks1st 8 weeks: 75% subsidy up to $750/week2nd 8 weeks: 50% up to $500/weekFinal 8 weeks: 25% subsidy up to $250/weekCustom stream: over 72 weeks1st 18 weeks: 85% subsidy2nd 18 weeks: 55% subsidy3rd 18 weeks: 25% subsidyNote: Mandatory Employment Related Costs are added on top of the maximum amounts and paid out by the program.Turnaround Time: 10-15 business daysEligible Employers:Be a registered business in BC;Have third party liability coverage;Have no more than 5 active Wage Subsidy agreements per CRA business number at one time and no more than 10 WorkBC subsidized employees per fiscal year;Be compliant with the Employment Standards Act, Workers Compensation Act, Income Tax Act, the Employment Insurance Act, and other relevant legislation;Offer Insurable Employment, as defined by the Employment Insurance Act;Must have employee on payroll;Pay reasonable, competitive wages; andOffer the likelihood of long-term employment or provide needed work experience to enable the job seeker to achieve long-term employment elsewhere.Ineligible Employers:Have an existing relationship with a potential employee (non-arm's length);Public sector employers, including but not limited to:Municipalities;Schools and school boards;Public universities and colleges; andHospital and health authorities.Active WorkBC clients participating in self-employment services; andWorkBC contractors.Eligible Candidate:Must choose from WorkBC's pre-screened pool of candidates.Eligible Expenses:Employee wages;Mandatory Employment Related Costs (MERCs);Employment Insurance, Canadian Pension Plan (CPP), WorkSafe BC and vacation pay.Disability support to reduce barriers at work; andNecessary work equipment (e.g. steel toe boots, high visibility vests etc.)Note: Sick days and severance pay are ineligible costs.Program Details:Positions must be full time;Minimum 35 hours per week.Work must be done primarily in BC;The positions cannot result in the displacement of existing employees or volunteers;Cannot be piecework or 100% commission based work;Reimbursement claims should be made monthly;Monthly check-ins plus 2 formal check-ins (once at the halfway point and at the end);Site visits are still required (in-person and/or virtually); Monthly check-ins and mid-point questionnaire are required;Employers can have up to 5 active wage subsidies (per CRA Business number) at any given time; andThe maximum number of wage subsidies per employer per fiscal year is 10.

      Grant Criteria 
      This program funds up to 100% of eligible costs for projects that provide workplace training for Nova Scotian organizations, through a customized curriculum based on essential skills.  The goal of the program is to develop programs that provide the foundation needed for learning other skills in order to enable employees to adapt to workplace changes. Grant Value: Up to 100% of eligible costs.Note: The Grant funding amount is listed at $0 because funding amounts vary. Funding is based on a needs assessment and subject to approval.Eligible Employers:All businesses with operations in Nova Scotia.Eligible Candidates:All employed individuals in Nova Scotia.Eligible Expenses:The skills, knowledge and time of a Workplace Training Coordinator;Funding to conduct an Organizational Training Needs Assessment;Funding to hire an Instructor for the development and delivery of programs for your organization;Program materials may include General Educational Development (GED) manuals;Participant costs may include calculators; andConsulting Services. Consultant fee is based on hours of preparation and delivery of activity (course).Ineligible Expenses:Employee salaries;Cost of photocopying and materials; andCost of the closing celebration.Program Details:Essential skills include (varying levels of complexity):Math (numeracy), reading, writing, document use, oral communication skills, working with
others, continuous learning, problem-solving, and basic computer use.The total number of participants per class is a minimum of 7 and a maximum of 12;Multiple courses can be funded at any one workplace or organization;Courses vary in length from 40 to 120 instructional hours and are delivered in two-hour to four-hour classes over a defined term;Projects can be delivered to an individual business or a collection of businesses or organizations; andOn-going and end-of-program evaluation is required by the project team, the
participants, and the instructor.

      Best Practices & Forms

grants.industries: All Industries
grants.program_provider: Labour and Advanced Education Nova Scotia
grants.grant_criteria: This program offers up to $100,000 per fiscal year for an employer to provide technical and incremental training for their full-time employees. Generally, WIPSI provides up to 50% of direct training costs to eligible employers. Additional funding may also be granted for any accommodations for disabilities (100%) or some administrative costs (15%) for hosting training that are incurred upon by organizations or associations applying on behalf of their members. The goal of this program is to increase the inter-provincial and international competitiveness of Nova Scotia businesses by training the workforce to adapt to new technology, machinery and equipment, or work processes.
grants.best_practices:
Eligible Best Practices:The program allows funding to be used in conjunction with other sources of federal government funding. However, applicants must declare the other sources of funding in their application;If the employer is not yet generating revenue from commercial activity, they may be eligible for funding if they are in a LAE identified priority sector;Proposed training cannot result in the business having a competitive advantage over other NS businesses providing similar goods and/or services;Professional services where businesses have revenue streams in markets where they do not compete with NS businesses may be eligible to participate;NS businesses that are generating profit solely from wholesale, retail, accommodation and/or food service would not be considered.The outcomes of the proposed training cannot be suitable for business essential training that would otherwise be covered under WEI;Process Best Practices:Submit completed applications at least 1 month prior to training start date to ensure all documentation for training activities are approved;Training can start as soon as a fully complete application is submitted at the expense of the applicant.Include proof of the trainers' qualifications to provide the training in the application;Multiple training projects may be submitted in one application; however, the participants must complete all training in
the application within this 12-month period; Applications may be approved in full, in part, or declined upon assessment for eligibility requirements, strength in supporting WIPSI program
objectives, and return on investment for both the employer and the province; Amendments to the agreement may be possible after the project has been approved; andApplicants may have the right to appeal the decision if the application has been declined.

        November 24, 2025:Intake is now closed. The next intake period will begin 1 April 2026.
      

      Grant Criteria 
      This program offers up to $100,000 per fiscal year for an employer to provide technical and incremental training for their full-time employees. Generally, WIPSI provides up to 50% of direct training costs to eligible employers. Additional funding may also be granted for any accommodations for disabilities (100%) or some administrative costs (15%) for hosting training that are incurred upon by organizations or associations applying on behalf of their members. The goal of this program is to increase the inter-provincial and international competitiveness of Nova Scotia businesses by training the workforce to adapt to new technology, machinery and equipment, or work processes.Grant Value: Up to $100,000Businesses with 49 employees or fewer:Project minimum size is $5,000;Up to 100% of eligible training costs up to $10,000 per fiscal year; andUp to 50% of eligible training costs for amounts that exceed $10,000, up to a maximum of $100,000 per fiscal year.Businesses with 50  employees or more:Project minimum size is $10,000;Up to 50% of eligible training costs.Organizations, business associations and private sector unions:Minimum application amount is $10,000 in direct training costs;Funding may be available for administration costs as determined on a case-by-case basis.Funding may also cover other expenses like travel (up to 50%) and accommodation costs for persons with disabilities (up to 100%).Turnaround Time: 30 business daysEligible Employers:Registered and active in the NS Registry of Joint Stock Companies or incorporated by an Act of the
Nova Scotia Legislature;Over one calendar year into operations; andGenerating at least 30% of revenue from commercial activity,  unless operating in a LAE identified priority sector.Ineligible Employers:Businesses that are generating profit solely from wholesale, retail, accommodation
and/or food service; andProfessional services such as veterinarians, dentists, lawyers, advertising professionals and consultants, among others; who compete with other NS businesses.Eligible Trainees:Employees (including full-time seasonal) receiving full-time compensation while in training;Be at least 19 years of age; andLive permanently in Nova Scotia.Eligible Expenses:Registration, tuition, course fees, or examination fees;Manuals, books, and support materials;Employee travel costs (up to 50%) where training takes place at least 100 km (each way) from the employee’s regular work site;Costs for accommodations for persons with disabilities (100%); andFor organizations or associations applying on behalf of their members:Administration costs to host training (up to 15% on a case-by-case basis).Eligible Training:Training that is new and/or incremental to the employees and/or the business which will:Result in a new direction and/or expansion to the core operations;Foster skills in the workforce that will support business and/or sector growth, exportability, productivity and/or innovation; and/orCreate more inclusive, welcoming workplaces.Eligible types of training include:Information technology training;Technical training;Workflow systems and processes training; andOther training that will benefit your business or organization and that isn’t typically eligible for funding through other government programs.Ineligible Training:Legislated or regulated mandatory training;Orientation training or onboarding;Training outside the province which has comparable learning outcomes to training available
in NS;Training that could be supported under another Government program, such as the Workplace Education Initiative (WEI);Training that has already been supported by WIPSI;Informal training, and/or training by internal staff or trainers;Training included with the purchase of equipment or new business processes; Apprenticeship training;Conference hosting costs or participation fees; Professional development intended to build an employee’s skills that are considered typically
necessary to operate in their current job (e.g. qualifications or credentials); and Consulting or coaching services intended to assist businesses or organizations with the operation, including assessments to determine the need for training.Program Details:Funding agreements should not exceed 12 months;Trainers must belong to a third party, have appropriate qualifications to provide the training, and cannot be an immediate family member of the principal of the employer; A one or two-time payment schedule is selected during the application process;Applications are submitted through the Labour Market Programs Support System (LaMPSS);Reporting takes place before the first payment, at the end of the project, and one year after training ends; and requests:Annual sales/revenues;Annual training investments; andNumber of employees and total annual salaries paid.The first payment is typically made within 5 business days if all required documents are received, and final payments may take slightly longer depending on the size of the agreement; andEmployers need to fill out a survey after training is delivered and
a follow-up survey one year later.Selection Criteria:The extent to which the training project is linked to a LAE priority sector;The level of benefit the training project delivers during and beyond the project:Number of people directly benefiting from the training;How the training will increase the capability and technical expertise of the workforce;How the project will enable the workforce to better meet economic opportunities; andHow the project will increase opportunities for employees from diverse backgrounds and/or create more welcoming, inclusive workplaces.The value for money offered by the training:Likelihood of the project going ahead without WIPSI funding;Expected return on investment from the training; andThe extent to which the training leverages additional partnerships or in-kind contributions.The applicant's capacity, capability, and resources to carry out the training:The applicant's track record with similar WIPSI funded training; andThe applicant's readiness to start the training.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Applied Innovation Grant is part of WorkSafeBC’s Innovation funding stream and provides up to $50,000  to support small-scale, practical research projects that produce solutions that can be used in workplaces to improve occupational health, safety, and work disability outcomes.Grant Value: Up to $50,000 for one year. Turnaround Time: PendingEligible Applicants:Any Canadian resident (worker, employer, small business owner, or researcher) can apply as a principal applicant.Projects must fit WorkSafeBC’s research priorities (occupational health and safety);Academic applicants must include an industry partner or non-academic collaborator on the team.International applicants and full-time WorkSafeBC employees cannot be principal applicants (but can be co-applicants).Eligible Projects:Projects that apply existing knowledge in new ways to solve workplace problems;Typical outcomes: new programs, procedures, frameworks, or methods that address health and safety or work-disability challenges.Eligible Activities :Research that leads to practical workplace change, such as:Surveys and focus groups with workers/employers;Risk assessments on-site;Developing and testing programs or procedures;Impact evaluations of interventions.Eligible Expenses :Salaries and benefits;Supplies and expenses ;Permanent equipment (no more than $5000 of the total
budget);Travel, accommodation and meals;Knowledge transfer and exchange. Program Details:Designed for small, shop-floor research projects that lead to real workplace solutions;Applicants must submit a complete application package that includes the standard application form and required supporting documents;Each applicant and co-applicant must submit a signed consent form for use and disclosure of personal information;WorkSafeBC Research Services may assist with access to internal data or experts to assess relevance before submission;All standard terms and funding conditions apply to funded projects.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best PracticesConfirm early that the applicant and project meet all eligibility rules, especially residency, partnership, and alignment with WorkSafeBC priorities;Clearly demonstrate scientific quality and validity to succeed in peer review.Process Best PracticesA completed Application Form, including all required signatures and supporting documents;A signed Applicant Consent Form for Use and Disclosure of Personal Information for each project team member;Applications to be electronically completed, in Word format (no PDFs); electronic signatures are accepted;Upload the full package to OneDrive using the required file-naming format (e.g., 2026 AI Lastname), with a maximum file size of 5 MB;More guidelines of formatting are provided in the application guidelines;Submit by the application deadline; late or incomplete applications are not accepted, except for required ethics or biosafety certificates, which may be submitted after the deadline.Forms:Program Webpage: click hereProgram Guideline: click hereApplication Form: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This provincial program offers employers a maximum of $5,000 salary subsidy to hire a pre-screened and employment-ready intern and provide job-specific training. It is intended to provide unemployed Ontario youth (aged 15-29 years old) with work experience and valuable skills to improve their career prospects.Grant Value: Up to $5,000 salary subsidyNote: Funding amounts are negotiated with the delivery organization based on job complexity and skill level as well as length of on-the-job training. Funding can vary between placements.Turnaround time: 2 business daysEligible Employers:Must be licensed to operate in Ontario;For-profit and non-profit organizations;Maintains a CRA/business number;Have adequate third party general liability insurance;Comply with Occupational Health and Safety Act and the Employment Standards Act;Must have and maintain Workplace Safety and Insurance Board (WSIB) or private workplace safety insurance coverage;Not currently or recently involved in lay-offs;Offer opportunities for on-the-job training;Contribute to costs associated with job-specific training or wages; andMust have the intention of hiring the participant after the placement ends.Ineligible Employers:Federal, provincial and municipal governments and agencies;Must not be receiving other government funds (federal, provincial or municipal) for the same placement;Use placement services to displace existing staff or replace staff who are on lay-off; andHire his or her immediate family members.Eligible Candidates:Canada citizens, permanent residents or protected persons;Must be residents of Ontario;Must be between the ages of 15 - 29 at registration;Individuals between 15 - 17 must be legally excused from attending high school using formal SAL agreement.Must be unemployed and not participating in full-time training or education;Be experiencing multiple barriers to employment; andBe able to attend 60 hours of short-term pre-employment workshops and activities.Program Details:Delivery organization will provide job matching from pool of pre-screened candidates and will also provide placement and work transition support;Placements may be full- or part-time job placements;Maximum placement of 6 months;No maximum placements per company;Participants must be on payroll upon approval;Must offer training/work experience that will help participants achieve their career goals; andTraining/skill enhancement must be delivered by a third-party provider.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Applicants cannot combine funding with other federal, provincial or municipal hiring incentives for the same placement;This grant cannot be applied retroactively;However existing employees who improve in employment circumstances (e.g. part-time to full-time) may be eligible;Considerations to be given to Indigenous youth, persons of disability, recent immigrant, disadvantaged youth (education level, essential skill level, work experience, family circumstances, mental health, housing).Process Best Practices:Spots can be held for companies applying without candidates;Employers must ensure they have valid WSIB or private insurance to access funding. Registration for WSIB may take time if not already done, so applying as soon as there is interest in YJC is recommended;Employers must advise delivery organizations immediately of learning of an accident/injury/disease.Forms:There are several service providers accepting applications for this program.
